jobs.title: Services Project Manager
jobs.description:
As the global leader in high-speed connectivity, Ciena builds the critical infrastructure powering the AI era. We’re a technology company shaping the future of networking, guided by innovation, integrity, and collaboration. Through development opportunities, meaningful work, and flexibility, Ciena supports growth and well-being—on and off the job. Connect with a career that matters.

Ciena is seeking a delivery-focused Services Project Manager to lead customer engagements and service delivery projects across the United States East Coast region. This role drives project execution across the full delivery lifecycle while aligning customer commitments, operational objectives, and financial outcomes. Success in this position comes from coordinating cross-functional teams, managing project complexity, and delivering consistent customer results.

How You Will Make An Impact

Lead customer-facing service delivery projects across the full project lifecycle.
Coordinate project scope, schedules, milestones, resources, and execution activities.
Implement communication plans and provide project status updates, risk visibility, and resolution tracking.
Conduct risk assessments and execute mitigation plans throughout project delivery.
Chair customer and internal project meetings to communicate progress, issues, and delivery outcomes.
Monitor project execution against scope, resource utilization, budget expectations, and delivery commitments.
Interface with customers, engineering teams, sales, bid management, service delivery groups, partners, and finance teams to achieve project and business objectives.

The Must Haves

Education: Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or related field.
Experience: 3–5 years of experience in Service Delivery, Project Management, Service Coordination, or a relevant industry.
Utilization of project management tools.
Application of network lifecycle activities including design, deployment, migration, and validation.
Background in optical transport and networking environments including DWDM and L0/L1 technologies.
Experience interacting with customers, cross-functional delivery teams, and engineering resources.
Demonstrated influencing and collaboration across multiple teams.

Nice To Haves

Certifications: PRINCE2 certification preferred.
Certifications: PMP certification preferred.
Application of effort estimation, cost drivers, and delivery risk evaluation.
Background contributing to commercially sound decisions during presales and delivery activities.
Experience working in matrix environments with multiple stakeholders.
Outstanding planning, scheduling, and coordination skills.
Outstanding verbal and written communication skills.

Pay Range

The salary range for this role, in the USA, is $79,900.00 -$ !27,700.00 USD.

Pay ranges at Ciena are designed to accommodate variations in knowledge, skills, experience, market conditions, and locations, reflecting our diverse products, industries, and lines of business. Please note that the pay range information provided in this posting pertains specifically to the primary location, which is the top location listed in case multiple locations are available.

Non-Sales employees may be eligible for a discretionary incentive bonus, while Sales employees may be eligible for a sales commission. In addition to competitive compensation, Ciena offers a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision plans, participation in 401(K) (USA) & DCPP (Canada) with company matching, Employee Stock Purchase Program (ESPP), Employee Assistance Program (EAP), company-paid holidays, paid sick leave, and vacation time. We also comply with all applicable laws regarding Paid Family Leave and other leaves of absence.

At Ciena, we are committed to building and fostering an environment in which our employees feel respected, valued, and heard. Ciena values the diversity of its workforce and respects its employees as individuals. We do not tolerate any form of discrimination.

Ciena is an Equal Opportunity Employer, including disability and protected veteran status.

If contacted in relation to a job opportunity, please advise Ciena of any accommodation measures you may require.

jobs.title: Deployment Strategist
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Picogrid is a leading venture-backed defense technology company founded to bridge the decades-long gap between modern technology and the critical demands of national security. Today, we're building the essential infrastructure to unify sensors, autonomy, and operators with our technology deployed in active operations around the world. Our mission is to deliver an operational advantage to secure the United States and its allies.

About The Role

As a Deployment Strategist at Picogrid, you will deploy and operationalize our platform in complex, real-world environments. You will work directly with warfighters and government program stakeholders to understand mission needs, translate them into clear plans, and coordinate the people, technology, and decisions required to deliver operational outcomes.

This is not a traditional engineering role or a conventional customer-success position. It combines technical fluency, customer relationship ownership, program execution, and hands-on field operations. Your focus is making each assigned engagement successful: establishing the plan, coordinating internal and external teams, preparing field activity, resolving blockers, and closing the loop on outcomes.

You will work closely with experienced Deployment Strategists, Forward Deployed Engineers, Product, Engineering, Logistics, Capture, and other operational leaders. You will begin with a defined set of engagements and grow your scope as you demonstrate sound judgment and consistent execution. The role requires travel up to 50%, including to military installations, exercises, demonstrations, and customer sites.

This is a role for someone who wants meaningful ownership early in their career, learns quickly across technical domains, and wants to see their work produce real outcomes in the field.

What You'll Do

Drive day-to-day execution of assigned customer engagements, contracts, pilots, exercises, and deployments from kickoff through delivery and follow-through
Translate customer objectives and ambiguous mission needs into clear scopes, timelines, responsibilities, technical requirements, and decision points
Serve as a primary point of coordination for assigned customers, building trust through proactive communication, responsiveness, and consistent delivery
Coordinate across Engineering, Product, Logistics, Capture, external partners, and customer teams to keep integrated efforts aligned and moving
Capture customer and product insights to drive growth identifying appropriate opportunities to expand applications of Picogrid technologies
Plan and support field activities, including site coordination, readiness reviews, equipment and personnel requirements, execution, and after-action follow-up
Maintain accurate engagement records and provide timely inputs for contract, invoicing, deliverable, and program reporting
Identify operational, technical, or schedule risks early; develop practical mitigation plans; and escalate issues with the context needed for decisions
Gather feedback from operators and program stakeholders and translate it into actionable input for product improvements, deployment practices, and future engagement planning
Document decisions, customer context, and repeatable processes so engagements can scale and transition without losing mission knowledge

Who You Are

You turn ambiguity into action by identifying what is known, asking the right questions, and building an executable plan
You take ownership within your scope, follow through on commitments, and know when a risk or decision should be escalated
You develop working knowledge of technical systems quickly and can explain requirements and tradeoffs across engineers, operators, government stakeholders, and external partners
You earn trust through preparation, sound judgment, discretion, and reliable execution
You communicate clearly and concisely, surface risks early, and keep the right people informed without creating unnecessary process
You are collaborative, low-ego, and comfortable working alongside customers and technical teams in the field

Basic Qualifications

2+ years of experience in deployments, military operations, technical program or project execution, customer-facing operations, consulting, or a related role
Demonstrated experience owning a customer-facing technical or operational workstream from planning through delivery
Experience coordinating complex work across customers, technical teams, and other stakeholders
Technical fluency and the ability to understand integrated hardware and software systems well enough to support planning, troubleshooting, and customer communication
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to brief technical, operational, and leadership audiences
Willingness and ability to travel up to 50%, sometimes on short notice, to military installations, exercises, and customer sites
Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Government security clearance

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working with the U.S. military, Department of Defense, or other national-security organizations
An active U.S. Government security clearance
Experience supporting field deployments, military exercises, pilots, demonstrations, or test events
Familiarity with command and control, autonomy, robotics, sensors, communications, or other integrated mission systems
Experience working at a startup, high-growth company, or another environment where processes are still being built

Why This Role Exists

Picogrid’s growth depends on more than building strong technology. We must translate that technology into reliable outcomes for customers operating in demanding environments. As our portfolio expands, every customer engagement needs a clear owner who can maintain mission context, coordinate execution, and earn the trust of the operators involved.

This role ensures assigned engagements have someone driving action, resolving gaps, and closing the loop between the customer and Picogrid. By staying close to operators and technical teams, Deployment Strategists turn field feedback into better deployments, better product decisions, and repeatable practices that allow Picogrid to scale without losing operational intimacy.

Compensation & Benefits

Base salary range: $100,000–$160,000 per year. Base salary is just one part of your total compensation package at Picogrid.
Significant stock options with a high potential upside as an early-stage company
401(k) with employer matching
Health coverage for you and your family (medical, dental, and vision insurance)
Relocation assistance provided (if applicable)
Unlimited PTO (two-week minimum) and 13 paid holidays per year
Paid parental leave for both parents
Lunch provided when working in-office and a fully stocked kitchenette
Free EV charging at the HQ
Unique office in El Segundo, CA stocked with quality coffee, snacks, and craft beer

Export Control Requirements

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C.

1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C.
1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) Policy

Picogrid is committed to providing a professional work environment free from discrimination, harassment, and retaliation. We are an equal opportunity employer and make all employment decisions based on merit, qualifications, and business needs.

Compensation Range: $100K - $160K

We are dedicated to exceeding expectations throughout the entire construction project lifecycle and adapt to the needs of each assignment to develop tailored approaches and solutions to meet those needs.

Hill is a GISI Consulting Group company, part of the Global Infrastructure Solutions, Inc. (GISI) family of companies. Learn more about GISI Consulting Group at www.gisiconsulting.com .

jobs.title: Manufacturing Data Analyst
jobs.description:
Your Job

Molex is seeking a Manufacturing Data Analyst to turn production data into accurate, actionable information that helps our manufacturing leaders make better decisions. This role builds and maintains the reports, dashboards, and metrics that show how our operations are performing, and digs into the data to find opportunities to improve safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, and capacity. This is not a desk-only analytics role: you will spend time on the production floor observing processes, validating data, and conducting time studies alongside Manufacturing and Engineering teams.

Our Team

You will support our Manufacturing Operations and Manufacturing Engineering teams in an on-site, regulated manufacturing environment. Working closely with Quality, Planning, and other functions, our team relies on timely, trustworthy data to improve visibility into production performance and drive continuous improvement.

What You Will Do

Create and own the daily, weekly, and monthly reports, dashboards, and KPIs that give manufacturing leadership a clear view of production performance.
Analyze productivity, throughput, cycle time, labor utilization, capacity, schedule attainment, quality, and delivery to uncover trends, bottlenecks, and improvement opportunities.
Get on the production floor to conduct time studies, cycle-time measurements, and workflow observations that support labor standards and capacity planning.
Safeguard data integrity by validating manufacturing data and investigating discrepancies between production records, reports, and systems.
Reduce manual effort by developing reporting tools and automating data collection and reporting activities.
Partner with Manufacturing Engineering on Travelers, work instructions, process records, and data collection tools.
Serve as a go-to resource for manufacturing software, internal applications, and production label systems, troubleshooting issues and helping implement improvements.
Provide the data and analysis behind continuous improvement projects and measure the results after implementation.

Who You Are (Basic Qualifications)

High school diploma or equivalent with experience in a manufacturing, operations, or engineering environment, OR an Associate degree in Engineering Technology, Manufacturing Technology, Data Analytics, Business, Information Systems, or a related technical field.
Experience using Microsoft Office tools, including Excel.
Ability to work on-site and spend regular time on the production floor.

What Will Put You Ahead

2+ years of experience supporting manufacturing, operations, engineering, production reporting, or data analysis.
Experience using Microsoft Excel formulas, lookups, and PivotTables to analyze data and develop reports.
Experience with ERP/MRP systems such as SAP.
Experience with Power BI, SQL, Snowflake, or similar data and visualization tools.
Experience with programming languages such as Python, Java, or PHP.
Experience with barcode and manufacturing label systems.
Experience in electronics, aerospace, defense, or other regulated manufacturing environments.

In order to comply with U.S. export control laws and regulations, this position requires applicants to either provide proof of U.S. citizenship or lawful permanent resident status or be eligible to receive an export authorization (a license) under the International Traffic in Arms Regulations and/or the Export Administration Regulations.

For this role, we anticipate paying $25.00 - $30.00 per hour.

At Koch companies, we are entrepreneurs. This means we openly challenge the status quo, find new ways to create value and get rewarded for our individual contributions. Any compensation range provided for a role is an estimate determined by available market data. The actual amount may be higher or lower than the range provided considering each candidate's knowledge, skills, abilities, and geographic location. If you have questions, please speak to your recruiter about the flexibility and detail of our compensation philosophy.

As a Koch company, Molex is a leading supplier of connectors and interconnect components, driving innovation in electronics and supporting industries from automotive to health care and consumer to data communications. The thousands of innovators who work for Molex have made us a global electronics leader. Our experienced people, groundbreaking products and leading-edge technologies help us deliver a wider array of solutions to more markets than ever before.

jobs.title: Senior Physical Security Project Manager
jobs.description:
WHO WE ARE

ZBeta is a world-class physical security design, consulting, and managed services firm that partners with some of the most dynamic, high-profile organizations and individuals in the world. We leverage a Data-Driven, Technology-Led, Human-Centered approach in order to help our clients architect and engineer superior physical security solutions, implement them seamlessly, and operate them at peak efficiency. ZBeta prides itself on its level of technical expertise but remains independent and product-agnostic. Our highly experienced team brings decades of security expertise, diverse organizational perspectives, and proven best practices to every project and customer. It is our meticulous attention to detail, and our ability to deliver at scale that positions us to deliver an exceptional customer experience.

Our primary goal is to redefine the standards of professional security, equipping our clients with innovative tools to master today’s challenges and fortify against tomorrow's risks. By consistently delivering exceptional solutions and pioneering advancements in the security field, we can exceed expectations and set new standards of excellence in pursuing our vision.

Find out more about us here.

WHO YOU ARE

You are a forward-thinking strategic partner with a passion for enhancing security measures and fostering community resilience. You excel in fast-paced settings where your leadership abilities can catalyze meaningful transformation. You thrive in a workplace culture that is:

Innovative
Strives for Excellence
Reliable
Detail Oriented
Adaptable
Highly Organized
Client Obsessed
Curious
Resilient

Does this sound like you? If so, join us in our mission to redefine security standards and make a lasting difference in our community.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

As a Senior
Project Manager, Design,
you will lead the planning and design phases of multiple, complex physical security projects throughout the North Coast. You will serve as the primary project manager from project initiation through design completion, ensuring projects remain aligned with client objectives, schedules, budgets, and quality expectations.

This role requires a unique combination of business acumen, communication, leadership, strategy development, tactical ability, and project management skills. You are a resourceful, knowledgeable, and self-motivated security professional who thrives in a collaborative and supportive environment.

CORE COMPETENCIES

Growth Minded:
Strong self-awareness of strengths and development areas with a curiosity and appetite for change and innovation
Data-Driven:
Strong analytical skills with critical thinking driven by data
Collaborative
: Ability to solicit and understand multiple perspectives
Evaluative:
Ability to evaluate outputs rigorously to ensure consistent excellence in delivery
Strategic Thinker:
Ability to think proactively about the future of the business and relate current business activities to desired outcomes

POSITION RESPONSIBILITIES

The essential duties and responsibilities include, but are not limited to the following:

Project Management

Identify project schedule, scope parameters, and oversee security design and implementation per client design requirements and standards.
Manage early project initiation activities and develop project security scope, schedule, critical deliverables, and requirements.
Manage scheduling, status, and tracking of critical project tasks, issues, and deliverables.
Prepare, issue, and manage Request for Proposal (RFP) documents for security systems installation scope.
Evaluate RFP responses and prepare evaluation reports, to include evaluation criteria, scoring, and recommendation details.

Design

Perform security site evaluations of potential client properties and review proposed design concepts.
Apply client system design standards to in-progress site design, collaborate with client owner and user group stakeholders to define use cases and verify functional requirements, and produce a security functional specification for the project.
Review all security system design documentation for compliance with published security requirements, technical standards, and installation standards.
Redline documentation with corrections and log issues, as required.

Client Relationship

Accountable for keeping clients informed of project status, including budget, schedule, issues, etc., and managing the client's expectations around the project design through individual and project team member communication.

Collaborate

Serve as a primary security point of contact for project teams and stakeholders.
Attend regular project design, project management, Owner/Architect/Contractor (OAC), and construction meetings.
Manage site activation activities for physical security amongst project parties and stakeholders to drive schedule, quality, and cost.
Coordinate with ZBeta design resources to develop the complete scope of work documents for security systems procurement and installation.

Documentation

Produce project status and issues reports and meet with client stakeholders weekly to review and resolve high-priority project issues.
Log all instances of issue resolutions that constitute exceptions to the published client security requirements to facilitate effective requirements exceptions reporting and/or requirement document updates.

Quality Control

Review security system designs for technical accuracy, constructability, and compliance with client standards.
Coordinate internal quality assurance reviews prior to client delivery.
Verify design deliverables are complete, coordinated, and ready for procurement.
Ensure project documentation meets ZBeta quality standards and established design methodologies.
Capture lessons learned and recommend improvements to enhance future project delivery.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED

Experience:
5+ years of project management experience, preferably in consulting with external clients on complex, aggressively scheduled projects
Education:
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience
Knowledge:

Detailed knowledge of access control system hardware, wiring standards/practices, installation methods, and programming required

Skills:

Working knowledge of Lenel OnGuard, with experience performing basic programming functions, is a plus. Certification in either S2 or Lenel Access Control Systems is preferred
Highly proficient in the use of Microsoft Office software
Proficiency in Studio and Bluebeam is a plus
Proficiency in project management tools, such as MS Project, SharePoint, and QuickBase

Abilities:

Demonstrated ability to lead complex projects and manage multiple competing priorities
Demonstrated excellence in communicating and presenting complex information to technical and non-technical stakeholders, both verbally and in written form
Demonstrated ability to identify critical path activities, prioritize tasks and deliverables, and realize consistent progress
Ability to influence and drive accountability across teams without direct authority
Ability to coach and support project team members

WHAT WE OFFER

Competitive salary based on job-related skills, experience, and qualifications
ZBeta is a remote-first company with a distributed team. This role is open to individuals based in the United States.
Our excellent benefits package includes 100% paid premiums on health, dental, vision, and life insurance, a 401k retirement plan, and significant work schedule and workplace flexibility.
Diverse and supportive culture

WHAT'S IMPORTANT TO KNOW

We are open to hiring candidates to work out of the North Coast (Santa Rosa, Sonoma, Napa)
This is an embedded position and will work directly with our client
This position requires the ability to travel up to 50%
This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship
Candidates must be able to meet client and/or government security screening requirements for the role
The successful completion of a background check is required upon hire and every two years thereafter

We look forward to connecting with individuals who are passionate about our mission and can bring diverse contributions to our team — not just those who check all the boxes.

We are committed to creating a supportive, encouraging environment where everyone can fully express their diverse perspectives, showcase their talents, and grow their knowledge, skills, and abilities.

The base pay offered will depend on factors, including but not limited to job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and internal equity. At ZBeta, new hires are rarely placed at the top of the pay range; compensation is determined by the specific circumstances of each position and candidate.

A note to third-party recruiters - we do not accept unsolicited agency resumes, and we are not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes.

jobs.title: Implementation Manager
jobs.description:
Role Overview

The hiring organization is seeking an Implementation Manager
to ensure healthcare data solutions are successfully implemented, adopted, and delivering measurable value for customers. This role combines hands-on implementation and project leadership with customer-facing work to drive adoption across clinical, operational, and technical stakeholders from pilot through ongoing delivery.

Role Details

Title: Implementation Manager

Description

Position at Matson Navigation Company, Inc

About Us

Founded in 1882, Matson (NYSE: MATX) is a leading provider of ocean transportation and logistics services. Matson provides a vital lifeline of ocean freight transportation services to the domestic, non-contiguous economies of Hawaii, Alaska, and Guam, and to other island economies in Micronesia. Matson also operates premium, expedited services from China to Long Beach, California, which includes cargo from other Asia origins, provides services to Okinawa, Japan, and the South Pacific, and operates an international export service from Alaska to Asia.

Matson Logistics extends the geographic reach of Matson's transportation network throughout North America and Asia. Its integrated logistics services include rail intermodal, highway brokerage, warehousing, freight consolidation, supply chain management, and freight forwarding to Alaska.

Matson is honored to be certified as a Great Place to Work. Learn more at www.matson.com.

About The Role

The Program Manager, Sanctions Compliance (OFAC)
serves as Matson’s specialist professional and subject matter resource for enterprise sanctions compliance, restricted-party screening, and related international trade controls. The position independently manages large and complex compliance processes with limited oversight and is responsible for translating applicable sanctions requirements into practical policies, procedures, controls, investigations, training, and business guidance.

The role leads administration and continuous improvement of sanctions screening across relevant counterparties, transactions, shipments, and geographies. It partners across Legal, Operations, Technology, Finance, Procurement, and Commercial functions to strengthen screening coverage, data quality, system reliability, documentation, audit readiness, and timely escalation of potentially significant matters.

This is a hybrid position requiring onsite work at our Corporate Office in Walnut Creek, CA, three (3) days per week (Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday).

What You’ll Do

Sanctions screening, investigations, and advisory support; additional Treasury activities

Own and administer enterprise sanctions and restricted-party screening processes for relevant counterparties, transactions, and shipments.
Independently review, investigate, document, and disposition potential screening matches using available identifiers, ownership information, transaction details, shipment information, and other relevant evidence.
Exercise sound judgment in determining false positives, documenting conclusions, identifying matters requiring further review, and escalating unusual, unresolved, or potentially significant concerns to designated Legal and business stakeholders.
Prepare clear written findings, recommendations, decision records, and supporting evidence; coordinate required holds, restrictions, approvals, remediation, and follow-up actions through completion.
Provide practical subject matter guidance to business teams regarding sanctions requirements, control expectations, and risk-mitigation measures.
Participate in other day-to-day Treasury related tasks, including cash management, compliance (SOX, FBAR, KYC, Nacha, etc.), and bank account maintenance.

Program governance, policies, and risk management

Develop, maintain, and implement sanctions compliance policies, procedures, standards, and controls aligned with applicable requirements and business operations.
Lead or support periodic assessments of sanctions risk across operations, counterparties, transactions, shipments, and geographies; recommend control enhancements based on identified risk.
Monitor relevant sanctions developments, evaluate potential business impacts, and communicate recommended actions to appropriate stakeholders.
Promote consistent execution of sanctions requirements across business units and operational processes without direct people-management responsibility.
Maintain complete, organized, and audit-ready records demonstrating program execution, decision quality, and control effectiveness.

Technology, data, metrics, and continuous improvement

Partner with Technology and business system owners to improve screening coverage, data quality, system integrations, workflow reliability, and the compliance evidence trail.
Provide subject matter leadership for the selection, testing, implementation, and enhancement of sanctions screening platforms, case-management tools, and related compliance technology.
Develop and maintain metrics, dashboards, and management reporting for screening volume, exceptions, escalations, completion, remediation, and control effectiveness.
Identify and implement opportunities to automate controls, reduce manual effort, improve timeliness, and strengthen documentation and monitoring.
Participate in the AI initiative by leveraging AI-driven solutions to enhance processes.

Audit, training, and stakeholder engagement

Support internal audits, compliance reviews, control testing, assessments, and regulatory inquiries involving sanctions compliance.
Develop and deliver sanctions compliance training and awareness materials for relevant employees and stakeholders.
Track corrective actions and process improvements through completion and verify that identified deficiencies are remediated.
Lead cross-functional workstreams and coordinate the contributions of other professionals; coach or provide technical guidance on sanctions processes as needed.

You Have These Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Finance preferred, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience.
Five or more years of progressively responsible experience in sanctions compliance, international trade compliance, regulatory compliance, financial-crimes compliance, risk management, maritime compliance, or a related discipline.
Demonstrated subject matter expertise in sanctions or restricted-party screening, including investigation and disposition of potential matches and documentation of well-supported conclusions.
Experience independently managing significant compliance programs, processes, projects, or control enhancements with limited oversight.
Ability to interpret regulatory requirements and translate them into practical business policies, procedures, controls, system requirements, and training.
Strong analytical, investigative, problem-solving, and decision-making skills, including the ability to address difficult and often complex matters.
Ability to influence and coordinate stakeholders across Legal, Operations, Technology, Finance, Procurement, and Commercial functions without relying on formal authority.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including preparation of concise findings, recommendations, and management reporting.
Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Word, Outlook, and PowerPoint.

Extra Credit If You Have

Experience in maritime transportation, logistics, freight forwarding, supply chain, international trade, financial services, or another regulated industry.
Working knowledge of OFAC regulations, sanctions programs, restricted-party screening, and risk-based compliance frameworks.
Familiarity with related export-control considerations, including the Export Administration Regulations and International Traffic in Arms Regulations.
Experience with screening tools, case-management systems, third-party risk databases, system integrations, workflow automation, audit support, regulatory reviews, compliance assessments, or remediation programs.
Basic familiarity with AI and generative AI tools.

The annual salary range is posted for this position in California. The salary offered will depend upon qualifications and other operational considerations.

jobs.title: Program Manager, Jewish Leadership Accelerator
jobs.description:
PROGRAM OVERVIEW

The Jewish Leadership Accelerator (JLA) is a highly selective nine-month fellowship that brings the most ambitious young Jewish leaders in their 20s into one room. It was founded by philanthropist Laura Lauder through The Jewish Leadership Fund and Jewish Federation Bay Area and will launch in San Francisco in January 2027 with an inaugural cohort of 20 fellows before expanding nationally.

Over nine months, fellows sit down to private dinners with founders, investors and public leaders currently shaping the city, and moderate those dinners themselves. They take part in a day-long weekend retreat, set their own mentorship goals with introductions through JLA's network, and close the fellowship with JLAction, where they share their leadership vision with mentors and community leaders. Fellows receive a $2,000 stipend on completion and join a lifelong alumni network.

ROLE SUMMARY

The Program Manager is the engine behind JLA's first few cohorts. Reporting to the Program Director, they will think strategically about how the program should run, then get into the details to make it happen: planning the retreat, curating and preparing speakers, producing each weeknight dinner, and working hands-on with fellows from application onward. This is a new role at a new program. The Program Manager will build systems in real time, and the processes they document will become the playbook for JLA's expansion. The ideal candidate is organized, high-energy, and self-directed; equally at ease with a 25-year-old fellow and a foundation board chair; and motivated by building something new rather than inheriting an established structure. The role is base in Bay Area working primarily remotely with occasional travel, local meetings and events.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

Strategic Planning and Program Management

Planning:
Partner with the Program Director on the nine-month plan: the program calendar, cohort timeline and session themes. Run a debrief after each dinner and gather fellow feedback to improve the next one.
Project management:
Own timelines, task lists and deadlines across every workstream. Prepare updates for Laura Lauder, the JLA Board, and advisory committees.
Budget and vendors:
Manage the program budget day to day, including stipends, vendor contracts and event costs.
Data and KPIs:
Keep fellow, speaker and partner records current, and report on fellow engagement, attendance, retention and alumni activity.

Retreat, Dinners and Speakers

Retreat:
Plan and run the day-long weekend retreat early in the fellowship, including venue selection, curriculum, and day-of logistics.
Speaker curation:
Work with the Program Director and founder to identify, invite and confirm the speakers for each dinner, with two guests per evening from business, tech, government and communal life. Support speaker outreach, scheduling, and keep speaker bios and materials current.
Speaker and dinner prep:
Prepare a brief for every speaker on the format, the cohort and the topic, and build a run-of-show for each evening.
Dinner logistics:
Coordinate venue selection, catering, guest lists, and day-of coordination.

Hands-On Work with Fellows

Fellow preparation:
Coach the teams of two to three fellows who moderate each dinner, introducing guests, leading the opening Q&A and running table discussions, so they walk in ready.
Day-to-day support:
Be the first point of contact for every fellow and offer support when needed.
Community:
Support JLA-funded, fellow-curated social gatherings and administer microgrant requests.

Selection, Alumni and Expansion

Selection:
Run the day-to-day of admissions: applications, rolling review, nominations and references, Selection Committee interviews, and timely communication with every applicant.
Alumni engagement:
Run local alumni events and support the annual cross-city gathering so the network stays active as each cohort joins.
Expansion:
Document processes, templates and lessons learned from the first cohort as input to the playbook for New York City and future cities.

QUALIFICATIONS, KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, ABILITIES

Required

Hands-on experience in program or project management: comfortable planning, prioritizing and tracking many workstreams, timelines, and vendors at once, with strategic thinking about what the next cohort needs.

jobs.description:
Who We Are

Applied Materials is the global leader in materials science and engineering solutions that are at the foundation of virtually every new semiconductor chip and advanced display in the world. The equipment that we create and service is essential to advancing AI and accelerating the commercialization of next-generation semiconductor chips. Join us and push the boundaries of materials science and engineering in a company at the foundation of the electronics industry. The work we do together advances the world’s technology.

What We Offer

Salary:

$110,500.00 - $152,000.00

Location:

Santa Clara,CA

You’ll benefit from a supportive work culture that encourages you to learn, develop, and grow your career as you take on challenges and drive innovative solutions for our customers. We empower our team to push the boundaries of what is possible—while learning every day in a supportive leading global company. Visit our Careers website to learn more.

At Applied Materials, we care about the health and wellbeing of our employees. We’re committed to providing programs and support that encourage personal and professional growth and care for you at work, at home, or wherever you may go. Learn more about our benefits.

Role Overview

Central Engineering is seeking an experienced Technical Program Manager (TPM) to lead the development and commercialization of Central Engineering capabilities required by Etch products.

This role has end-to-end program accountability for complex, cross-functional initiatives spanning platform, robotics and automation, software, systems integration, and advanced R&D capabilities. The TPM will work across Etch product groups and Central Engineering functions to translate product and chamber requirements into clearly scoped engineering programs and drive those programs from requirements definition through development, system integration, lab readiness, customer introduction, and commercialization.

The TPM is expected to operate as an accountable program owner, not simply as a coordinator between organizations. The role owns program definition and execution across multiple engineering organizations, including scope, priorities, deliverables, schedule, resources, dependencies, risks, customer introduction, and Product Development Process execution.

Success requires strong technical judgment, systems thinking, program leadership, and the ability to drive execution across organizations where engineering resources and priorities must be negotiated and aligned.

Key Responsibilities

Program Ownership and Execution

Own end-to-end execution of cross-functional technical programs supporting Etch product development and commercialization, from initial requirements and program definition through engineering development, integration, lab validation, customer introduction, and release.
Serve as the single-point accountable owner for Product Development Process execution for assigned Central Engineering programs supporting Etch.
Establish clear program scope, objectives, technical requirements, milestones, deliverables, resource requirements, dependencies, risks, and success criteria.
Drive programs to deliver integrated, working solutions, ensuring individual engineering deliverables come together successfully at the system level rather than managing functional activities independently.
Maintain accountability for program commitments and proactively drive recovery plans when technical, resource, schedule, or integration issues place commitments at risk.

Requirements And Systems Integration

Partner with Etch product and engineering organizations to scope and translate chamber and product requirements into requirements for Central Engineering capabilities, including platform, robotics and automation, software, controls, systems engineering, and advanced R&D technologies.
Drive requirements alignment across product, chamber, platform, software, robotics, and engineering organizations to ensure interfaces, dependencies, and system-level requirements are clearly understood.
Work across multiple technical disciplines to identify integration risks, architecture dependencies, qualification requirements, and gaps that could impact product readiness or customer introduction.
Ensure engineering solutions are developed and integrated to meet the needs of the Etch product roadmap and intended customer use cases.

Portfolio, Priority, and Resource Management

Manage a portfolio of Central Engineering programs and capabilities supporting Etch, maintaining visibility across program health, engineering resources, technical maturity, milestones, dependencies, risks, and customer commitments.
Lead the scoping and prioritization of new program requests and determine the engineering capabilities, resources, and organizations required for execution.
Negotiate and align priorities between Etch product groups and Central Engineering functions when resource capacity, technical dependencies, schedules, or competing priorities require trade-offs.
Identify portfolio-level resource constraints and cross-program dependencies early and drive decisions with appropriate engineering and product leadership.
Provide leadership with clear visibility into program health, resource needs, critical risks, decision points, and recovery actions.

Cross-Functional Technical Leadership

Work across Product and Engineering disciplines to establish clear ownership and drive teams toward a common technical and program outcome.
Lead cross-functional execution across organizations responsible for platform, robotics, automation, software, controls, systems integration, and advanced engineering technologies.
Drive decisions across organizational boundaries and hold teams accountable for agreed deliverables, timelines, and technical outcomes.
Influence without direct authority by establishing clear requirements, data-driven priorities, decision frameworks, and escalation paths.
Resolve ambiguity around scope, ownership, priorities, interfaces, resources, and execution responsibility before those gaps affect program delivery.

Risk and Customer Introduction

Own identification and management of technical, integration, resource, schedule, qualification, and customer-introduction risks across assigned programs.
Establish mitigation and recovery plans for critical program risks and escalate decisions when cross-organizational alignment or leadership intervention is required.
Coordinate readiness across engineering teams for lab integration, system qualification, product release, and customer introduction.
Ensure issues discovered during system integration or customer introduction are driven to root cause, corrective action, ownership, and closure.

Qualifications

Required

BS or MS degree in Engineering or a related technical discipline.
5+ years of experience in high-tech product development, systems engineering, systems integration, engineering program management, or technical program management.
Demonstrated experience leading complex, multidisciplinary engineering programs involving multiple engineering organizations and technical dependencies.
Strong understanding of structured product development processes and experience driving programs from requirements through development, integration, qualification, and release.
Demonstrated ability to manage scope, schedules, resources, dependencies, risks, and technical integration across matrixed organizations.
Strong systems thinking and the ability to understand interactions between hardware, software, automation, controls, and product-level requirements.
Demonstrated ability to negotiate priorities and drive decisions and execution without direct authority.
Strong executive communication skills, with the ability to clearly communicate program status, risks, trade-offs, and decisions to technical and business leadership.

Preferred

Experience in semiconductor capital equipment or semiconductor manufacturing technology.
Experience supporting complex semiconductor equipment development involving process chambers, platforms, robotics and automation, controls, embedded or application software, and system integration.
Experience with New Product Development, Product Development Process, NPI, system qualification, and customer introduction.
Familiarity with Etch equipment and technologies such as process chambers, vacuum systems, RF/plasma systems, gas delivery, automation, robotics, controls, and related platform technologies.
Experience driving engineering execution across product engineering, systems engineering, software, hardware, manufacturing, supply chain, quality, service, and business organizations.

Ideal Candidate

The successful candidate is a technically credible program leader and systems thinker who can operate across both product and engineering organizations.

This person does not need to be the subject-matter expert in every technical discipline, but must be able to understand how the pieces come together at the system level, challenge assumptions, expose gaps and dependencies, and drive engineering organizations toward an integrated solution.

The ideal candidate can take an initially ambiguous product or chamber requirement and turn it into a well-defined technical program with clear requirements, architecture dependencies, engineering ownership, resources, priorities, milestones, risks, and customer deliverables, and then remain accountable until the solution is working and successfully introduced.

Why This Role Matters

Etch products increasingly depend on capabilities that span multiple Central Engineering organizations and technical disciplines. Successful execution requires more than coordination of individual engineering activities. It requires system-level ownership of how those capabilities are scoped, prioritized, developed, integrated, qualified, and delivered as a working solution.

The Technical Program Manager provides that ownership.

By managing both individual programs and the broader portfolio of Central Engineering commitments supporting Etch, this role will improve requirements clarity, resource and priority alignment, engineering integration, risk management, Product Development Process discipline, customer readiness, and predictability of execution.

Full time

Yes, 10% of the Time

Yes

jobs.description:
Who We Are

Applied Materials is the global leader in materials science and engineering solutions that are at the foundation of virtually every new semiconductor chip and advanced display in the world. The equipment that we create and service is essential to advancing AI and accelerating the commercialization of next-generation semiconductor chips. Join us and push the boundaries of materials science and engineering in a company at the foundation of the electronics industry. The work we do together advances the world’s technology.

What We Offer

Salary:

$110,500.00 - $152,000.00

Location:

Santa Clara,CA

You’ll benefit from a supportive work culture that encourages you to learn, develop, and grow your career as you take on challenges and drive innovative solutions for our customers. We empower our team to push the boundaries of what is possible—while learning every day in a supportive leading global company. Visit our Careers website to learn more.

At Applied Materials, we care about the health and wellbeing of our employees. We’re committed to providing programs and support that encourage personal and professional growth and care for you at work, at home, or wherever you may go. Learn more about our benefits.

Company

Applied Materials is the leader in materials engineering solutions used to produce virtually every new chip and advanced display in the world. Our expertise in modifying materials at atomic levels and on an industrial scale helps our customers – who make smartphones, supercomputers, virtual reality headsets, autonomous vehicles and more – transform their ideas into reality.

The technologies we create are the foundational building blocks of the future. Our systems make semiconductor devices, called chips—"the brains" of the electronics used in almost every aspect of our lives. The promise of new and exciting applications, transforming industries such as consumer electronics, transportation, communications, healthcare, and supercomputing/AI, are enabled by advances in semiconductor and display technology.

While virtually every nationality, culture, and background are currently represented within Applied Materials, we strive for a more robust Culture of Inclusion (COI) and diversity. Leveraging our COI vision helps drive innovation, build organizational capabilities, create equal opportunities for everyone and achieve our company’s definition of Winning.

Our innovations Make Possible® a Better Future. If you’re looking for the next step in your future, consider Applied Materials. With the data explosion and new investment in semiconductors, it’s an exciting place to be.

Role

Project Manager, Tools Installations & Upgrades will report to the Manager, R&D Lab Tool Installations & fit-up Upgrades .
The individual will be responsible to provide broad and impactful leadership of tool installations within the Silicon Valley area.

The R&D Lab Tool Installations and Upgrades team is accountable for lab tool install design, permitting, and construction, including Lab process and building system infrastructure upgrades. Total annual Capital Expenditures for this team exceeds $50m and is increasing. The team consists of 20+ Applied Materials full time employees and 300+ project construction managers, design, and construction, contractors. Your role will be to manage projects.

Be responsible for establishing highly credible and effective partnerships with multiple internal business groups for whom the labs support.

Key Responsibilities

Execute Applied Materials’ Tool Installations & Upgrades to achieve key business objectives through reduced project cycle time.
Responsible to safely design, plan, execute, construct, start-up, and commission advanced semiconductor R&D lab facilities upgrades and tool installations in Silicon Valley.
Oversee a team of facility PM’s in the preparation and management of project plans, scope, schedule, and budget through all phases of design, contracting, construction, start-up and commissioning.
Order long lead equipment & materials and review & approve engineering submittals with stakeholders.
Serve as a leader with whom multiple Applied Materials business units collaborate to develop strategies that align with key business objectives.
Ability to respond to changing corporate business environments. Adjusting plans as needed.
Designs, develops and implements organizational policies and procedures relevant to the facilities department.
Collaborate with planning department peers for optimal solutions and transition into project execution within the group.
Develop and secure support for project Capital approvals.
Develop and track key performance metrics that align with both Tool Hook-up, Infrastructure Team and Business Unit objectives.
Coordinate with internal business partners, architecture/engineering firms, Facilities Operations, and EH&S in developing, reviewing and approving design criteria, layouts and detail drawings.
Ensures function processes result in strict compliance to permitting requirements and building codes.
Schedule building inspections and obtain inspection approvals.
Manage/direct construction for RFI’s, project scope of works, bid comparisons, work plan generations, conditional use, and full use approvals.
Develop a global platform from which all R&D Tool Hook-up teams globally can leverage, including methods and process, resources and expertise, contracting methodologies and performance improvement.
Manage construction contractors and ensure that they follow safe work practices and work to resolve safety or constructability issues.

The Ideal Candidate will have the Following:

7+ years’ experience in the semiconductor, Thin Films, or similar industry.
Experience with highly technical facility planning, design, and build.
Proven success managing the installations of semiconductor tools into R&D facilities.
Prior management experience
Strong management presence with ability to communicate effectively and influence stakeholders to achieve project objectives.
Passion to challenge the status quo in pursuit of material performance improvements.
Experience selecting, developing and managing tool hook-up related service providers.
Experience leading project management teams or equivalent.
Bachelor Degree or higher in an Engineering discipline
Strong computer skills with moderate-to-advanced Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint abilities.
Ability to analyze data for efficiency improvements and achieve reduced project cycle times.
Good financial accounting practices (capital vs. expense, scope funding gap review)

To Succeed in this Role Requires:

Ability to partner effectively with demanding and highly technical business unit tool owners, EHS professionals, and lab managers.
Ability to manage in a complex environment with multiple stakeholders across multiple groups.
Ability to make improvements to existing business process and manage supplier base for optimal performance.
Ability to translate complex technical project requirements into manageable and constructible pieces

jobs.description:
Description

Position at Matson Navigation Company, Inc

About Us

Matson has been the leading ocean shipping and logistics provider throughout the Pacific since 1882. We are the supply chain lifeline for Hawaii, Alaska, Guam, and islands of the South Pacific. We also offer the top two ocean shipping services in the world’s largest trade lane - Asia to the U.S. West Coast. With our subsidiaries Matson Terminals and Matson Logistics, our business focus is exceeding customer expectations with quality, reliability, and integrity.

We strive to operate in an environmentally sustainable manner and promote land-based environmental programs in Hawaii, Guam, and Alaska. We help improve the communities in which we work and live through our community giving program that annually supports hundreds of local organizations.

Matson is honored to be certified as a Great Place to Work. Our team of dedicated and talented employees consistently deliver exceptional results for our customers and the communities in which we serve.

Learn more at matson.com.

About The Role

The Principal Financial & Operations Analyst
is a key business partner to Operations leadership, combining financial and accounting expertise, operational understanding, and technical capability to solve complex business problems and improve performance. Working at the intersection of operations, finance, data, and technology, this role helps shape how information is structured, analyzed, and used to drive decision-making across the organization.

The role is responsible for building the data, reporting, and analytical capabilities that support operational and financial performance. This includes enterprise reporting solutions, Power BI dashboards, budget and forecasting models, AI-enabled analytics, and other tools that help leaders understand performance, allocate resources, evaluate opportunities, and make informed business decisions.

This position offers the opportunity to solve complex operational and financial challenges while building capabilities that shape how the organization operates. The successful candidate will be intellectually curious, self-directed, and motivated by ownership. They will invest the time to understand the operation, work confidently through ambiguity, challenge assumptions, and identify the underlying business need before developing a solution. They will possess the technical depth to build that solution, the financial and operational judgment to ensure it is meaningful, and the persistence to see it through implementation, adoption, and continuous improvement.

This is a hybrid position requiring onsite work at our Corporate Office in Walnut Creek, CA, three (3) days per week (Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday).

What You’ll Do

Design, build, and maintain data pipelines, reporting solutions, Power BI dashboards, financial models, and analytical tools that support Vessel and Network Operations, budgeting, forecasting, and performance management.
Establish and maintain trusted sources of financial and operational information by integrating, transforming, and governing data from multiple business systems.
Build scalable Excel-based budget, forecasting, and scenario models that incorporate operational assumptions, cost drivers, historical performance, and accounting requirements.
Partner directly with business leaders to understand operational challenges, identify root causes, define requirements, and develop practical data and analytical solutions.
Translate operational activity into financial insights through analysis of cost drivers, rate, volume, and mix impacts, contract terms, budget variances, forecasts, and performance trends.
Partner with Operations, Finance, Accounting, and IT to strengthen data governance, standardize reporting logic, and establish a single source of truth for key business metrics.
Identify and apply AI, automation, and advanced analytics capabilities to enhance reporting, forecasting, recurring analysis, and operational decision support.
Conduct Vessel and Network and operating cost analysis to explain performance, identify risks and opportunities, and recommend actions.
Evaluate reports, workflows, and business processes to identify opportunities for simplification, improved controls, and scalable technical solutions.
Support contract compliance and financial review processes, including invoice analysis, rate validation, cost recovery review, and alignment with approved accounting treatment.
Maintain strong internal controls and support SOX 404 compliance by ensuring data, models, reports, and analytical processes are documented, repeatable, validated, and auditable.
Lead cross-functional initiatives involving reporting modernization, financial planning, process improvement, and operational performance improvement.
Prepare executive-ready analysis that clearly communicates financial performance, operational impacts, risks, opportunities, and recommended actions.
Maintain ownership of solutions from problem definition through implementation, adoption, and continuous improvement.

You Have These Skills

Expertise in data architecture, data integration, ETL processes, data modeling, governance, and analytics platforms used to establish trusted reporting environments and a single source of truth.
Advanced Power BI capabilities, including semantic models, DAX, dashboard design, visualization best practices, performance optimization, and executive reporting.
Advanced Excel modeling skills supporting budgeting, forecasting, scenario analysis, variance analysis, and long-range financial planning.
Experience with Microsoft Fabric, enterprise reporting architectures, and scalable analytics solutions.
Strong foundation in finance and accounting, including budgeting, forecasting, accruals, cost allocation, internal controls, invoice review, and financial analysis.
Understanding of the operational drivers that influence financial performance.
Practical application of AI, machine learning, copilots, large language models, and advanced analytics tools to reporting, forecasting, operational analysis, and decision support.
Critical thinking and problem-solving skills, including the ability to navigate ambiguity, challenge assumptions, identify root causes, and develop effective solutions.
Sound business judgment with the ability to balance technical sophistication and practical business needs, creating solutions that are scalable, maintainable, and widely adopted.
Effective communication skills with the ability to translate technical concepts, operational information, and financial analysis into actionable business recommendations.
Commitment to data integrity, transparency, strong controls, repeatable processes, and defensible analysis.

And These Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Analytics, Data Science, Information Systems, Computer Science, Engineering, Operations Management, or related field required.
Three more years of experience in operations finance, financial analysis, business intelligence, data analytics, accounting, or related disciplines.
Demonstrated experience developing enterprise reporting solutions, Power BI dashboards, financial models, or analytical tools used to support business decision-making.
Advanced proficiency in Power BI, Excel, Power Query, SQL, and related analytics technologies.
Experience supporting budgeting, forecasting, management reporting, operational analysis, and performance measurement.
Experience working with financial, accounting, operational, and planning data within a complex business environment.

Extra Credit If You Have

Experience with Microsoft Fabric, Workday, Vena, cloud analytics platforms, or similar technologies preferred.
Experience applying AI and advanced analytics tools to practical business problems preferred.
Maritime, transportation, logistics, terminal operations, or other asset-intensive industry experience preferred, but not required.

jobs.title: Sr. Technical Program Manager - Storage, AWS Hardware Engineering, Hardware Engineering Services
jobs.description:
Description

Application deadline: Nov 21, 2026

AWS operates the world’s largest fleet of storage servers powering exabyte-scale cloud storage services. Our team designs, builds, and operates this fleet — solving systemic hardware issues and building systems that detect and prevent recurrence so customers experience the highest quality of service.

We are seeking a Senior Technical Program Manager to drive end-to-end delivery of storage servers across our global fleet. You will coordinate cross-functional engineering teams spanning hardware, firmware, and software, manage ODM partnerships across multiple continents, and establish closed-loop quality systems that drive continuous improvements. This role requires technical depth to translate engineering constraints into program risk, combined with program management excellence to deliver complex hardware at global scale.

Key job responsibilities

RFP & ODM Selection

Translate technical requirements into ODM evaluation criteria. Build scoring frameworks covering technical capability, manufacturing capacity, DFx maturity, automation capability, and commercial terms. Coordinate technical deep-dives between engineering and ODM design teams during competitive evaluation. Compile selection decision packages and drive decision meetings. Transition to NPI with requirements locked and statement of work signed.

NPI Program Delivery

Facilitate requirements gathering with internal customers; develop Technical Requirements Documents (TRDs) covering server specs, rack configurations, PCIe topology, NVMe/SSD layout, power/cooling topology, and drive interconnects. Build program timelines with critical path analysis, risk identification, and milestone tracking. Own milestone-driven gate progression: manufacturing readiness, production readiness, operational readiness review, and general availability. Drive cross-functional dependencies across firmware, thermal, mechanical, and silicon teams. Communicate program status to leadership with clear reporting on milestone progress, risk posture, and mitigation plans.

Production Yield & Manufacturing Delivery

Own manufacturing readiness gates and production yield tracking from first build through volume ramp. Monitor first-pass yield by test stage, drive root cause analysis on excursions, and ensure corrective actions close before yield issues compound. Track ODM delivery cadence, line throughput, and supply chain continuity.

Fleet Operations & Feed-Forward

Maintain fleet-level program visibility: AFR targets, unsellable resolution velocity, and component lifecycle risk. Own the feed-forward cadence — ensuring fleet failure patterns, manufacturing yield data, and vetting escapes translate into requirements and test content for next-generation programs.

Dashboards & Mechanisms

Build and own mechanisms for program visibility — defining metrics, dashboards, and review cadences that enable data-driven decisions and early risk detection. Define leading indicators: unsellable inflow/outflow rate, NPI milestone velocity, first-pass yield by test stage, and component lifecycle risk. Streamline delivery processes across teams; identify and eliminate dependencies, redundant gates, or coordination overhead that slow velocity.

Risk & Quality

Challenge technical workstreams to surface risks early; quantify impact to schedule and reliability (annualized failure rate targets, availability SLAs) with proposed mitigations. Drive root cause analysis of fleet-wide hardware failures and ensure corrective actions flow back into qualification criteria and design requirements. Define acceptance criteria, coordinate qualification testing at server and rack levels, and manage go/no-go decisions for mission-critical storage services.

May require occasional (<10%) regional and international travel to Design and Manufacturing Partner sites.

A day in the life

You start the day syncing with ODM partners across time zones on build status and open engineering actions. Mid-morning, you run an engineering review connecting firmware, software, and hardware teams to unblock a qualification gate. In the afternoon, you lead the weekly feed-forward review — translating fleet failure patterns into test content requirements for the next-generation program. You end the day reviewing NPI milestone readiness and updating the production yield dashboard before the ODM delivery cadence call.

About The Team

The Storage Server Hardware Engineering team designs and delivers the storage platforms that power Amazon S3, EBS, and other critical AWS storage services. We own our platforms cradle-to-grave: from architecture definition through NPI, manufacturing, fleet deployment, and end-of-life. Our sustaining engineers are the backbone of fleet reliability — ensuring that deployed platforms continue to meet quality and performance targets throughout their operational life.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering or a related discipline or equivalent
6+ years of technical product or program management experience, working directly with multiple engineering teams.
6+ years of experience driving hardware development programs (servers, racks, networking, or storage) through full product lifecycle including design, validation, manufacturing, and fleet deployment
Experience managing programs across cross-functional teams, building processes, and coordinating release schedules

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field
5+ years of experience coordinating complex server programs with ODM/JDM partners across multiple geographies, managing design reviews, manufacturing readiness gates, and quality checkpoints
5+ years of experience working with storage server platforms or NVMe/SSD infrastructure across NPI qualification phases (EVT, DVT, PVT)
Experience driving root cause analysis and corrective action processes for hardware reliability issues at fleet scale
Knowledge of server hardware development lifecycle: electrical/mechanical design, firmware, thermal/power validation, and manufacturing testing.
Experience driving zero-touch automation or fleet health programs for large-scale infrastructure
Experience communicating engineering trade-offs and technical risks in business terms to leadership.

Veolia is a global leader in environmental services, operating across all five continents with nearly 218,000 employees. Specializing in water, energy, and waste management, Veolia Group designs and implements innovative solutions for decarbonization, depollution, and resource regeneration, supporting communities and industries in their ecological transformation.

Within this framework,Veolia's Water Technology Business brings together a dedicated team of experienced professionals committed to tackling the world’s most complex challenges related to water scarcity, quality, productivity, and energy. Together, we pursue a shared mission to create a more sustainable future.

Job Description

This position is remote and can be based anywhere in the US.

The Project Manager (PM)
guides a team of engineers and professionals that design, build and manage complex water treatment projects. In this role, the PM is responsible for the overall success of projects in the Industrial Market portfolio.

Working closely with the Lead Engineer and Sourcing Project Leader, you direct and coordinate all activities on a given project, beginning with contract signature and following through process/equipment design, vendor selection, fabrication, shipment, installation and startup. The PM is a passionate advocate for quality and safety across every aspect of the project, and ensures that the team delivers on commitments while adhering to scope, schedule and budget. The PM will need to communicate the project status, provide updates on the budget and progress against schedule while setting and managing client and vendor expectations.

Able to work in a networked and highly flexible role and collaborate with several stakeholders
Skilled communicator that approaches problems analytically and with intellectual rigor
Foundation in engineering principles and knowledge of water treatment design and operation
Able to direct a team of experts and coach individuals as needed to ensure that the project stays on track
Effective facilitator of project team meetings and deliverables, and as needed able to resolve conflicts within the project team
Able to handle multiple shifting demands with professionalism and good judgment
Able to effectively communicate information to varying audiences including Senior and Executive Leadership in the Veolia organization and within Client organizations

Duties & Responsibilities

Oversees the delivery of water treatment equipment projects from initiation through completion.
Organizes how the contract will be executed and defines clear project objectives.
Develops and maintains realistic plans for scope, budget, schedule, and key milestones.
Coordinates the project team so everyone understands priorities, project structure, and their responsibilities.
Works closely with customers, suppliers, and internal teams to satisfy contractual and technical requirements.
Promptly escalates issues or events that could significantly impact cost, schedule, scope, or quality.
Monitors progress through regular reviews and internal reports, adjusting plans as needed.
Identifies, evaluates, and manages project risks and opportunities.
Oversees project changes and supports claims management where required.
Actively participates in technical meetings and project reviews.
Collaborates with technical experts and discipline engineers to resolve issues and address critical topics.
Maintains and updates action plans, ensuring timely closure of actions and adherence to project objectives.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Impeccable planning, organization and time management
Clear, concise communication and presentation skills
Team player, with the ability to exercise good judgment under ambiguous or changing conditions.

Qualifications

Education & Experience

Required

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Business, Economics, or an equivalent field
Ten years experience managing projects which include equipment supply and construction
Project Management Professional (PMP) certification, or the ability to obtain it within one year.

Preferred

Experience managing Engineering, Procurement contracts preferred
Experience in industrial process system design/construction, specifically water treatment in the , chemical, oil & gas or power markets.

Working Conditions

The role requires the ability to travel domestically and internationally 5-20% of the time.

Imagine having the power to stress-test an entire power grid against a hurricane or thunderstorm before the clouds even gather. That is the reality we are creating at Neara.

We use advanced machine learning to create engineering-grade, physics enabled digital twins of electricity grids across four continents, this helps asset owners understand their biggest challenges and bring the most viable solutions to life across millions of kilometres of infrastructure.

By simulating extreme weather and structural stress at a network-wide scale, we empower the world’s largest utilities to pinpoint risks, optimise investments and build a more resilient global energy future.

Our team is a collection of brilliant minds who are fanatical about making a tangible difference in the real world, utilising AI and machine learning to accelerate everything from data classification to complex scenario analysis. We have built a special culture where innovation thrives because everyone owns the mission and we need smart, creative people to help us scale this impact to every corner of the globe.

We're hiring a Technical Program Manager to own delivery of complex, high-value programs for our largest US utility customers. This is a customer-facing role, where you will be the trusted point of contact for customer teams and executive sponsors. While our Customer Success team members will own technical excellence and delivering the value to customers, you will be accountable for delivering every program on time, to scope and to a standard of excellence that customers will remember.

You will be the connective tissue between Customer Success, Product and Engineering, and a champion for change with both customers - adopting new technology and ways of working - and inside Neara, as our delivery model evolves. That includes a relentless pursuit of ways to deliver more and larger customer projects with the same resources, using AI and automation to make our work faster, more consistent and more scalable.

What You’ll Do

Lead end-to-end delivery of a portfolio of complex enterprise programs, from kickoff through go-live and adoption, involving large-scale data ingestion (LiDAR, GIS, asset data), model builds, integrations and value driven use cases
Be the primary point of contact for customer program teams and executive sponsors, building trusted relationships at every level
Run program governance, incl. steering committees, executive updates, status reporting & decision logs
Define scope, milestones, dependencies and success criteria, and keep programs on track by coordinating across Customer Success, Product and Engineering
Plan ahead for risks and dependencies, and guide stakeholders through key decisions with clear options and trade-offs
Champion change with customers through stakeholder alignment, training and adoption plans, so new workflows become part of how teams work
Apply and improve program management standards, templates and reporting across the US team
Identify opportunities to use AI and automation across the delivery lifecycle, such as status reporting, data validation and project setup, and help the team adopt them

What You’ll Bring

5+ years in technical program or project management, delivering complex enterprise software, data or infrastructure programs
Significant customer-facing experience, comfortable leading the room with senior stakeholders and building lasting trust
A consistent record of delivering multi-stakeholder programs on time and to a high standard
A natural change leader who has helped customers and teams adopt new tools, processes or ways of working
Technical enough to go deep with engineers on data pipelines, integrations and cloud platforms. Python or SQL skills are highly regarded
Comfortable working at multiple altitudes: shaping program strategy with executives one day, unblocking execution on the ground the next
Confident with data, tooling and project management tools (e.g. Fibery, Jira, Asana), and a practical user of AI tools to improve how work gets done
Experience in utilities, energy, GIS or LiDAR is a plus but not essential

Work on technology that matters. Our digital twins are actively protecting energy grids from increasingly common extreme weather and structural failure
Strategic autonomy, paired with a collaborative culture where everyone, from engineering to leadership, is accessible and aligned on the same mission
