jobs.title: Principal Technical Program Manager, Industry Software
jobs.description:
About The Team

The Industry Software organization builds the B2B SaaS platforms that power Zillow's software and services for real estate professionals, including:

Home listing, lead delivery, and home shopper lifecycle workflows
Identity and access: account hierarchies, user identity, team roster/permissions management
Enterprise integrations: broker rosters, listing feeds, partner data pipelines
Monetization: purchasing, pricing, billing, entitlements, and internal tooling for sales, support, and operations

We work in tight partnership with Product, Engineering, Design, Data, Marketing, Sales, Customer Support, and Finance to build an integrated, reliable, and scalable B2B ecosystem for our industry customers - and we aim to do it smart, humble, hardworking, and highly collaborative.

About The Role

We're seeking a Principal Technical Program Manager
to own some of the most complex, strategically important initiatives in Industry Software - multi-team, cross-organizational programs that span multiple product areas, from strategy and scope through execution, launch, and post-launch learning. You'll act as a thought partner to senior and executive leaders, bridge Product, Engineering, and Design to create clarity from ambiguity, and build deep expertise across our domains (monetization, identity and access, enterprise integrations, real estate SaaS and lead delivery) while operating as a strong generalist who ramps up quickly elsewhere.

You'll operate at both strategic and tactical levels: energized by building structure where little exists, balancing technical depth with strong stakeholder management, and setting direction while rolling up your sleeves to get high-quality work done on time.

What You'll Do

Strategy and planning: Define cross-org initiatives that align with Industry Software and broader Zillow B2B priorities; translate strategy into program charters, success metrics, and multi-release execution plans; shape scope and sequencing with Product, Engineering, and Design leaders.
Execution and delivery: Own the program lifecycle end to end - planning, dependency mapping, execution, launch, and post-launch follow-through - and drive the operating rhythms (status reviews, dependency checkpoints, release readiness) that keep teams delivering reliably, without subsuming team-level agile ceremonies owned by EMs and PMs.
Risk and metrics: Identify risks, dependencies, and bottlenecks early; drive mitigation and tradeoff decisions with leadership; use data to measure program health and guide iterative improvement.
Stakeholder communication: Orchestrate cross-functional collaboration across Engineering, Product, Design, Data, Sales, Marketing, Customer Support, Finance, Legal, and Operations; communicate status, risks, and decisions in a crisp, executive-ready narrative up to VP/SVP level.
Technical leadership: Build working knowledge of the systems, APIs, and data flows within your program scope; partner with Principal Engineers and architects to shape technical approach; ramp up quickly across domains like monetization, identity and access, enterprise integrations, and real estate SaaS/lead delivery.
TPM craft: Define and refine planning, risk, and reporting best practices for Industry Software; mentor other TPMs as a force multiplier for program management excellence; use AI-native tools to increase program efficiency and decision speed.

This role has been categorized as a Remote position. “Remote” employees do not have a permanent corporate office workplace and, instead, work from a physical location of their choice, which must be identified to the Company. U.S. employees may live in any of the 50 United States, with limited exceptions.

In California, Connecticut, Maryland, Massachusetts, New Jersey, New York, Washington state, and Washington DC the standard base pay range for this role is $182,100.00 - $290,900.00 annually. This base pay range is specific to these locations and may not be applicable to other locations. In Colorado, Hawaii, Illinois, Maine, Minnesota, Nevada, Ohio, Rhode Island, Vermont, and Virginia the standard base pay range for this role is $173,000.00 - $276,400.00 annually. The base pay range is specific to these locations and may not be applicable to other locations.

In addition to a competitive base salary this position is also eligible for equity awards based on factors such as experience, performance and location. Actual amounts will vary depending on experience, performance and location. Employees in this role will not be paid below the salary threshold for exempt employees in the state where they reside.

Who you are

8+ years in Technical Program Management (or equivalent), leading large-scale, multi-team, cross-org programs - including portfolio-level and multi-quarter planning - at mid-size or large companies.
Significant experience with B2B SaaS products or platforms, ideally serving business customers with complex account, identity, integration, or monetization needs.
Proven track record owning end-to-end delivery of complex, distributed systems or platforms, with strong technical fluency in modern architectures (microservices, event-driven patterns, data pipelines) and the ability to engage deeply with engineering teams.
Demonstrated ability to build program structure from the ground up: operating rhythms, governance, and metrics for complex initiatives.
Exceptional written and verbal communication, including executive-ready narratives, and proven ability to influence without authority across Product, Engineering, Design, and other partners up to senior and executive leadership.
Comfortable applying data-driven prioritization to trade off scope, quality, cost, and schedule across multiple simultaneous programs in a fast-moving environment.

Preferred Qualifications

Deep experience in one or more Industry Software domains - identity and access, monetization and billing, enterprise integrations, or real estate SaaS and lead delivery - or in adjacent complex B2B platforms (ecommerce, fintech, ad tech), ideally within a platform or internal tools organization where reliability and partner integration are critical.
Demonstrated experience mentoring TPMs or shaping TPM best practices within an organization.
Familiarity with AI and modern collaboration tooling (program dashboards, automation, document generation) to streamline program management.
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

If this sounds like you, we'd love to have you help lead the next chapter of Industry Software at Zillow.

Get to know us

At Zillow, we’re reimagining how people move—through the real estate market and through their careers. As the most-visited real estate platform in the U.S., we help people navigate buying, selling, financing and renting with greater ease and confidence. Whether you're working in tech, sales, operations, or design, you’ll be part of a company reshaping an industry and helping more people make home a reality.

How we work is a key part of that transformation. Through Cloud HQ, our strategic approach to distributed work, most employees have the flexibility to work from wherever they’re most productive—enabling us to move fast, stay connected and deliver on our people promise.

Zillow is honored to be recognized among the best workplaces in the U.S. Zillow was named one of FORTUNE 100 Best Companies to Work For® in 2026, and included on TIME’s America’s Best Companies 2026 list, reflecting our commitment to creating an innovative, inclusive, and engaging culture where employees are empowered to grow.

No matter where you sit in the organization, your work will help drive innovation, support our customers, and move the industry—and your career—forward, together.

Zillow Group is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering an inclusive, innovative environment with the best employees. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status. Description

Associate Project Manager

Location:
Denver, CO or Remote (US)

At Enverus, we’re committed to empowering the global quality of life by helping our customers make energy affordable and accessible to the world.

We are the most trusted energy-dedicated SaaS company, with a platform built to maximize value from generative AI, and our innovative solutions are reshaping the way energy is consumed and managed. By offering anytime, anywhere access to analytics and insights, we’re helping our customers make better decisions that help provide communities around the world with clean, affordable energy.

The energy industry is changing fast. But we’ve continued to lead the way in energy technology, creating intelligent connections across the entire energy ecosystem, from renewables, power and utilities, to oil and gas and financial institutions. Our solutions create more efficient production and distribution, capital allocation, renewable energy development, investment and sourcing, and help reduce costs by automating crucial business operations. Of course, this wouldn’t be possible without our people, which is why we have built a team of individuals from a diverse range of backgrounds.

Are you ready to help power the global quality of life? Join Enverus, and be a part of creating a brighter, more sustainable tomorrow.

Spatial Business Systems (SBS), now a part of Enverus, is seeking an Associate Project Manager to keep project delivery running smoothly while learning from experienced Project Delivery Managers and taking on more ownership over time.

About The Role

As an Associate Project Manager, you will split your time roughly evenly between project administration (resource planning, scheduling, reporting, and documentation) and client-facing delivery (small projects, upgrades, and EVP support). You will support Senior Project Managers and Project Delivery Managers on medium-to-large software implementations (AutoCAD-based design and similar applications) for utility, telecommunications, and government clients, growing into full project ownership on the path to Project Delivery Manager.

Essential Functions & Responsibilities

Project Administration

Build and maintain project schedules, work breakdowns, and task trackers (Jira, MS Project) under Project Delivery Manager direction.
Track budgets, burn rates, and hours against plan, and escalate variances early.
Prepare status reports and dashboards for assigned projects.
Maintain project workspaces, templates, and logs (meeting notes, action items, risks and issues, change requests).
Maintain the M&S backlog (Jira/DevOps, Salesforce/Axosoft), the defect list for active projects, and PPM tool and workbook maintenance across the PMO.
Support time entry compliance and invoicing readiness by following up on timesheets.

Coordination & Communication

Schedule and facilitate project meetings, distribute agendas, and capture and circulate minutes and next steps.
Act as the day-to-day point of contact for internal teams on logistics, scheduling, and process questions.
Prepare client materials for Project Delivery Manager review, join client meetings in a supporting role, and lead communications on your own projects.
Track dependencies and deadlines, and follow up with owners to keep work on schedule.

External Delivery

Manage small, well-defined projects, upgrades, and EVP support engagements as the client-facing contact, with guidance from a Project Delivery Manager.
Lead DDS M&S / Delivery (Data Services) status calls and coordinate follow-ups with project teams and clients.

Resource Planning support

Keep project allocations, forecasts, and staffing assignments in the resourcing system current as plans change.
Monitor team capacity and flag over-allocation, under-utilization, and unfilled demand to Project Delivery Managers and AUD/DDS leadership.
Prepare capacity and utilization views for AUD/DDS leadership and support weekly and monthly resourcing reviews with clean data and clear summaries.
Reconcile forecasted (pipeline) hours against logged hours and follow up on discrepancies.

Organizational Support

Help maintain Delivery Team templates and methodology materials, contribute to AUD/DDS KPI tracking, and assist with process improvements as assigned by Project Delivery Managers and Delivery Leads.
Reporting structure: No direct reports. Reports to an AUD/DDS Project Delivery Manager, works closely with the AUD/DDS Director and Delivery Leads, and takes assignments from each project’s Project Delivery Manager.

Desired Experience

1–3 years of experience in project coordination, project administration, resource management, or a similar support role; recent graduates with relevant internships or coursework will be considered.
Working proficiency with MS Office; Excel skills (formulas, pivot tables, data cleanup) strongly preferred.
Exposure to Jira, MS Project, DevOps, Axosoft, Clarizen, or comparable scheduling and backlog tools is preferred; experience with resource management or time-tracking tools is a plus.
Consulting or professional services experience and client-facing project experience are preferred; familiarity with utilities, energy, telecommunications, or government sectors is a plus.

Requisite Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities

Strong attention to detail and commitment to accurate, timely data.
Excellent organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines across several projects.
Clear written and verbal communication, with the confidence to follow up with team members, PMs, and leaders.
Analytical mindset: reads allocation, utilization, and time-entry data, spots trends or gaps, and explains them simply.
Proactive and self-starting, raising issues early rather than waiting for them to grow.
Thrives in a fast-paced, event-driven environment, learns the delivery methodology, and accepts feedback and mentoring.
Collaborative and professional with technical teams, business stakeholders, and clients.

Education, Training & Certifications

Bachelor’s degree in MIS, Computer Science, Business, Accounting, or a related field preferred; equivalent experience considered. CAPM or PMP certification (or progress toward one) is a bonus but not required.

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Extensibility Platform
jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About Our Organization

The Developer Experience & Product Platform (DEeP) organization empowers all of Stripe's products with a shared product platform that delivers high-quality, consistent, cross-product experiences across our UI and API surfaces. DEeP focuses on providing a scalable developer experience that any developer can leverage to accelerate a customer's ability to create value from Stripe.

Within DEeP, the Extensibility program is how Stripe expands its total addressable market, and increases customer retention. With extensibility, Stripe becomes programmable — customers and product teams can adapt Stripe to their needs on a common platform.

Stripe Has Three Interconnected Extensibility Primitives

Scripts — Secure, isolated TypeScript runtime allowing merchants and developers to customize Stripe product behavior (e.g., discount calculations, invoice logic, proration).

Custom Objects — User-defined data models (e.g., Shipments, Locations, Warranties, Entitlements) with first-class APIs, SDKs, and Dashboard experiences.

Workflows — A programmable orchestration layer (graduating to GA at Sessions) enabling no-code and pro-code business logic across Stripe, including custom actions, delays, smart retries, and 3P integrations.

These primitives are deeply interdependent, involve 10+ cross-functional teams and culminate in a flagship product launch.

What you’ll do

We are seeking a product-focused Technical Program Manager to drive the Extensibility program across the Workflows, Custom Objects, and Scripts workstreams. This is a newly created, high-impact role at the intersection of platform engineering, product management, and cross-organizational program ownership.

In this role, you will own one of the most strategically consequential programs in DEeP — driving the direction, health, and outcomes of Stripe's Extensibility platform across Scripts, Custom Objects, and Workflows. You will set the program strategy in partnership with DEeP leadership, holding organizations accountable to the success of the program.

Drive cross-org decisions across DRIs in Script Platform, Custom Objects, Apps, SDK, Observability, DevEx, and Versioning — actively resolving the hard, ambiguous integration and ownership questions that fall between team boundaries.
Own the critical path to major launches — proactively shaping scope, driving descope decisions, and negotiating trade-offs across teams so that launches reflect deliberate strategic choices.
Influence and shape product and engineering roadmaps — bringing a program-level perspective to team planning cycles, pushing back where individual team roadmaps are misaligned with broader extensibility strategy, and advocating for cross-cutting investments that no single team will prioritize on their own.
Support ProServ and Partnerships — Ensure ProServ and Partnerships requirements are surfaced into the roadmap with the same rigor as product requirements, and hold the bridge between what the platform delivers and what those teams need to close and serve complex customers.

Qualifications

Minimum requirements

5+ years of technical program management experience with demonstrated success in driving complex cross organizational programs.
Strong product sense and ability to understand enterprise customer needs
Demonstrated ability to communicate with precision and credibility across engineering, product, and executive audiences, translating complex technical trade-offs into strategic decisions, and driving alignment.
Demonstrated ability to lead and align cross-functional teams — driving decisions, resolving conflict, and building consensus across organizations with competing priorities
Proven track record of successful program delivery in complex technical environments
Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience

Preferred Qualifications

Background in product management or product operations
Experience with developer platforms, API products, or payment systems

Hybrid work at Stripe

This role is available either in an office or a remote location (35+ miles or 56+ km from a Stripe office).

In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This hits a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility about how to do this in a way that makes sense for individuals and their teams.

Working remotely at Stripe

A remote location is defined as being 35 miles (56 kilometers) or more from one of our offices. While you would be welcome to come into the office for team/business meetings, on-sites, meet-ups, and events, our expectation is you would regularly work from home rather than a Stripe office. Stripe does not cover the cost of relocating to a remote location. We encourage you to apply for roles that match the location where you currently live or plan to live.

Pay and benefits

The annual US base salary range for this role is $157,700 - $236,500. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.

We look forward to hearing from you.

At Stripe, we're looking for people with passion, grit, and integrity. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. Your skills and passion will stand out—and set you apart—especially if your career has taken some extraordinary twists and turns. At Stripe, we welcome diverse perspectives and people who think rigorously and aren't afraid to challenge assumptions. Join us.

Apply now

jobs.title: Principal Technical Program Manager, GTM Integration & Launch
jobs.description:
ClickHouse is powering the next generation of real-time analytics and AI infrastructure. We recently raised a $400M Series D at a $15B valuation, and we're growing fast: expanding our customer base, scaling our cloud business, and widening our product line through acquisitions and net-new Tier-1 launches into new product categories.

We're looking for a Principal Technical Program Manager, GTM Integration & Launch to own how those products get to market. An acquired product isn't sellable on day one, and neither is a Tier-1 launch: the pricing, packaging, quoting logic, approval rules, and controls have to be built and tested end-to-end, the acquired base has to be migrated onto ClickHouse paper, and the field has to know who to sell it to and how they get paid for it. This role owns getting there.

Reporting to the Sr. Director of Global Revenue Operations, you'll own the path to market across Product, Finance, Legal, Operations, Engineering, Enablement, and the acquired team: the commercial diligence, the requirements, the design decisions, the build, the testing, and go-live readiness. You'll also shape the GTM plan itself – who we sell to first, how reps are compensated, how the field is trained – and report monthly to leadership on how our emerging products are actually selling. Beyond any single launch, you'll turn integration into a repeatable playbook and build the tooling that makes the commercial system faster and more reliable. This is a senior individual contributor role on the critical path for every acquisition and every Tier-1 launch.

What You'll Be Doing

Own the integration path for acquired products. Bring an acquired offering onto the commercial system, reconcile its pricing and contract mechanics with how ClickHouse sells, and get it sellable through the same standard as an organic launch.
Shape GTM strategy for the products you're integrating. Help define the motion for newly acquired products (e.g., Langfuse) and net-new Tier-1 launches (e.g., Postgres): who we sell to first and why, how reps get paid for it, and how the field gets trained – partnering with Sales Leadership, Comp/Planning, and Enablement, and building the target account lists from usage signals and account intelligence.
Run commercial diligence and pre-close planning. Assess the target's pricing model, contract paper, billing stack, metering, and revenue recognition, and land at close with a sequenced integration plan rather than a blank page.
Own the commercial and operational design. Define the requirements and make the calls on pricing setup, quoting logic, discount and approval rules, and the controls that govern how the product gets sold, in partnership with Commercial leadership.
Own contract and customer migration. Map the acquired base's entitlements to ClickHouse SKUs, move customers onto ClickHouse paper at renewal, and protect revenue through the transition.
Own the program end-to-end. Hold the timeline, drive deliverables across Product, Finance, Legal, Operations, Engineering, and the acquired team, and synthesize the cross-functional work into a single readiness plan.
Test the end-to-end flow before launch. Run UAT on the quote-to-cash path, catch what breaks, and confirm the full flow works before go-live.
Own go-live readiness. Set the launch criteria with product marketing, run the go/no-go, and make the call on whether the flow is ready. Coordinate field activation with Enablement so the product lands when it ships.
Own monthly GTM reporting. Report wins, gaps, and what broke to leadership, and feed it back into the process so the next integration goes faster.
Build the playbook and the tooling. Turn each integration into a repeatable path, and find and fix what's manual, slow, or error-prone in the commercial system along the way.

What You Bring

10+ years in technical program management, revenue operations, product operations, or commercial systems, with a track record of owning launches end-to-end and building the systems behind them.
Direct experience building GTM strategy for a new or unproven product.
Experience with usage-based or consumption-based business models. You understand how metering, commits, and overages create dependencies across billing, contracts, revenue recognition, and the commercial system – and that a launch has to get all of them right together.
Strong working knowledge of the systems an integration depends on: Salesforce and CPQ, financial and billing systems, product rating, and telemetry. You can design quoting rules, approval logic, and automated controls across them.
Depth to own the design, not just the plan. You write the requirements, facilitate the design calls on quoting, approval, and control logic, and build parts of the solution yourself.
Sales compensation design experience, or direct partnership with Sales/Comp teams on incentive structures.
M&A or technology integration experience. Bringing an acquired product onto the commercial system runs the same path as an organic launch, and this role owns that work.
Cross-functional program management at the core. You hold a timeline, drive deliverables across teams, and synthesize across stakeholders. You measure readiness by whether the full flow works end-to-end.
Partnership with enablement teams to build training programs and measure them against outcome metrics.
Strong analytical skills, including SQL, to build target lists, measure pilot results, and report on launch effectiveness.
Strong written and verbal communication. Comfortable driving a cross-functional forum and presenting readiness status to senior stakeholders.
Bachelor's degree; quantitative or technical field preferred. MBA or equivalent experience a plus.

Perks

Flexible work environment - ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and remote-friendly. We currently operate in over 25 countries.
Healthcare - Employer contributions towards your healthcare.
Equity in the company - Every new eligible team member who joins our company receives equity.
Time off - Flexible time off in the US, generous entitlement in other countries.
A USD$500 Home office setup if you’re a remote employee.
Global Gatherings – We believe in the power of in-person connection and offer opportunities to engage with colleagues at company-wide offsites.

Culture - We All Shape It

As part of a rapidly scaling start-up, you will be instrumental in shaping our culture.

Are you interested in finding out more about our culture? Learn more about our values here. Check out our blog posts or follow us on LinkedIn to find out more about what’s happening at ClickHouse.

Equal Opportunity & Privacy

ClickHouse provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type based on factors such as race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.

Please see here for our Privacy Statement.

Compensation Range: $200K - $250K

Technical Program Manager – Machine Learning / AI

Remote, United States | Competitive Base + Equity | Energy AI

We're partnering with a Tier 1-backed AI company on a mission to transform how critical energy infrastructure operates. They're developing intelligent systems that combine machine learning, advanced optimisation and automation to improve how energy is produced, transported and managed.

Unlike many AI businesses, they're working with real physical assets, operational data and complex engineering environments. Their long-term ambition is to build the intelligence layer that enables increasingly autonomous energy operations.

With an exceptional engineering team bringing experience tier 1 ML/Engineering teams, scientific research and industrial technology experts, they're now looking for a Technical Program Manager to help turn ambitious ML research and engineering into real-world outcomes.

The opportunity

This is not a traditional project-management role. You'll work closely with ML researchers, engineers and company leadership, helping a highly technical team execute without slowing down its ability to innovate.

You'll be responsible for:
→ Driving execution across multiple ML research, engineering and deployment workstreams, from early experimentation through production.
→ Managing roadmaps, milestones, technical dependencies and blockers, helping engineering teams maintain momentum.
→ Coordinating across Machine Learning, Product, Engineering and commercial teams to ensure priorities translate into delivery.
→ Supporting external research collaborations, evaluating new R&D opportunities and helping prioritise technical initiatives.
→ Building lightweight processes, documentation and operating rhythms that allow a growing engineering organisation to scale effectively.

What we're looking for

Experience in technical program management, ideally supporting Machine Learning, AI or complex software engineering teams.
Strong understanding of the ML development lifecycle, from research and experimentation through evaluation and deployment.
Ability to engage credibly with researchers and engineers, understand technical trade-offs and help unblock difficult problems.
Experience managing multiple concurrent technical initiatives and coordinating cross-functional stakeholders.
High ownership, clear communication and the ability to bring structure to ambiguous, fast-moving environments.

Why join?

You'll be joining a small, technically ambitious team tackling problems at the intersection of AI, energy and physical infrastructure. There's genuine scope to shape how the ML organisation operates, work alongside exceptional technical talent and help bring technology into production where its impact extends well beyond a benchmark or dashboard.

Location:
Remote, US
Package:
Competitive base salary + equity + benefits

jobs.title: GynOnc Research Program Manager
jobs.description:
University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus

Department: OBGYN

Job Title: GynOnc Research Program Manager

Position #: 00854512 – Requisition #:
41733

Job Summary:

The Gynecologic Oncology Division Research Program Manager is a full-time position within the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology at the University of Colorado School of Medicine. This role will be responsible for providing management and oversight for clinical trials in close partnership with the Division Chief, Division Administrator Director, and Division Faculty members. This position will be team lead and have direct oversight of the GynOnc Division’s Research Services Professional positions. In order to succeed in this position, this detail-oriented individual must be able to demonstrate superior organizational skills to successfully track multiple tasks occurring in parallel. This incumbent must be self-motivated to complete tasks quickly and within set deadlines. This position is the ‘hub’ of communication between external (review committee coordinators, review committee members, study monitors) and internal (clinical study staff, investigators, clinical managers) contacts, thus superior communication skills (oral and written) are required. The position may be utilized to support research at the main Anschutz Medical Campus as well as in Northern Colorado. The professional in this position will not be called on to make independent medical decisions at any time, but a solid fundamental knowledge of biological and medical sciences is necessary for this position. Additionally, appreciation of accepted methods of clinical research is highly desirable.

In addition to their team lead role, this position will be responsible for cross-training and providing coverage to clinical coordination duties including active patient recruiting and consenting, visit coordination, and study team compliance with regulatory documents (Delegation of Authority Log, Form 1572, Financial Disclosure forms, Site Qualification Documents). This position will be responsible for human subjects research regulatory compliance of study teams in the GynOnc Division and will interface with regulatory and financial bodies in conjunction with the contacts within the OBGYN Administrative Research Core (ARC) Team.

Key Responsibilities:

Personnel Management: 25%

Provide direct supervision to GynOnc research staff personnel in their day-to-day work and with matters including recruitment, hiring, onboarding, training and retention strategies.

Financial Management: 10%

Works with finance team members to review invoices for accuracy in work performed, resolve discrepancies, and to review outgoing invoices and account balances on a regular basis.
Manage expenses and allocate resources from all research funding sources including gifts, grants and contracts funds.

Team Lead Operational Duties & Responsibilities: 40%

Assists with identifying issues related to operational efficiency and shares results with leadership.
Assists clinical research staff with technical issues, problem solving and intervention when appropriate; delegates responsibility for elements of the conduct of selected clinical trials.
Serves as study team contact for ongoing and potential clinical research studies including multi-center studies and meets with representatives from sponsoring pharmaceutical firms or in-house staff for initial orientation to studies and for review of regulatory records.
Provides service coverage for RSP/CRC to complete day-to-day patient focused research activities when necessary.
Oversees the operational execution of clinical trials by ensuring protocol compliance, participant eligibility and enrollment, informed consent processes, study visit coordination, specimen management, safety reporting, and regulatory documentation.

Quality Assurance: 25%

Oversees data review, collection, and documentation of all research subject data pertaining to the research protocol onto protocol-specific Case Report Forms (CRFs) and into the Cancer Center clinical trials database in an accurate and timely fashion.
Obtains oncology grading levels for study product toxicities, including assessment of clinical significance of all lab and test results and relatedness of adverse reactions to study product according to protocol guidelines.
Meets with Monitors to respond to any question of data validity and corrects/revises data as appropriate; responds to queries from Sponsor.
Participates in external audits and internal process improvement strategies to promote consistent best practices.

Work Location:

Hybrid – this role is eligible for a hybrid schedule of 4 days per week on campus and as needed for in-person meetings.

Why Join Us:

The University of Colorado, Department of Obstetrics & Gynecology’s, Division of Gynecologic Oncology is a women's health oncology practice dedicated to treating, curing and providing support for reproductive cancers. As the only National Comprehensive Cancer Network in the rocky mountain region, CU's Gynecologic Oncology group provides patients with the highest level of expertise available delivered in compassionate and individualized care.

Why work for the University?

We have AMAZING benefits and offer exceptional amounts of holiday, vacation, and sick leave! The University of Colorado offers an excellent benefits package including:

Medical: Multiple plan options
Dental: Multiple plan options
Additional Insurance: Disability, Life, Vision
Retirement 401(a) Plan: Employer contributes 10% of your gross pay
Paid Time Off: Accruals over the year
Vacation Days: 22/year (maximum accrual 352 hours)
Sick Days: 15/year (unlimited maximum accrual)
Holiday Days: 15/year
Tuition Benefit: Employees have access to this benefit on all CU campuses
ECO Pass: Reduced rate RTD Bus and light rail service

There are many additional perks & programs with the CU Advantage.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in any field. Substitution: A combination of education and related technical/military/paraprofessional experience may be substituted for a bachelor’s degree on a year for year basis.
Four (4) years clinical research or related experience.

Applicants must meet minimum qualifications at the time of hire.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in science or health related field.
Master’s degree in public health, public administration, social/behavioral sciences, physical sciences, nursing, healthcare, finance, accounting, business administration, business, or a directly related field from an accredited institution.
Five (5) years clinical research or related experience.
Prior experience providing program and/or project management duties in a clinical research setting.
Experience with electronic data capture systems (e.g. EMR or EHR and data management systems).
One of the below certifications:
CCRC – Certified Clinical Research Coordinator
CCRP – Certified Clinical Research Professional
CCRA – Certified Clinical Research Associate

Bilingual, Spanish Fluency.
Prior training and/or experience in Cancer Research, specific to OBGYN.
Experience working at a large health care related organization, University or state agency.
Experience working in the local (Denver or Colorado) health care environment.
Experience with Phase I clinical research trials.
Experience serving as a primary coordinator for clinical trials.
Previous personnel management, supervisory experience, or successful completion of the CU SOM Management Certification Program.

Conditions of Employment:

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States without requiring sponsorship. We are unable to provide work visa sponsorship or employment authorization for this position now or in the future.

Competencies: Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities (KSAs)

Strong project management skills and experience within a complex and diverse environment.
Advanced knowledge and understanding of federal regulations and Good Clinical Practice (GCP).
Demonstration of strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Ability to communicate effectively, both in writing and orally.
Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with employees at all levels throughout the institution.
Outstanding customer service skills.
Knowledge of basic human anatomy, physiology, and medical terminology.
Ability to interpret and master complex research protocol information.
Organization, time management, and prioritization skills.
Outstanding leadership skills.
Advanced knowledge of GCP, FDA Rules and Regulations in relation to clinical trials, NIH guidelines, ICH guidelines and HIPAA regulations in relation to clinical trials, and NCI common toxicity definitions.
Understanding of the phases and concepts of clinical trials and the overall philosophies of conducting cooperative group research as they differ with National Cancer Institute (NCI) sponsored, private industry and investigator initiated clinical trials.

How to Apply:

For full consideration, please submit the following document(s):

A letter of interest describing relevant job experiences as they relate to listed job qualifications and interest in the position.
Curriculum vitae / Resume
Three to five professional references, including name, address, phone number (mobile number if appropriate), and email address.

Questions should be directed to: Jaden Burroughs, jaden.burroughs@cuanschutz.edu

Screening of Applications Begins:

Immediately and continues until position is filled. For best consideration, apply by November 30th, 2026
.

At AMD, we believe technology has the power to solve the world’s most important challenges. From advancing healthcare and scientific discovery to powering AI and the technologies people rely on every day, innovation at AMD is shaping the future.

Whether you’re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or bringing leading edge products to market, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger — technology that moves the world forward. Join us and, together, we’ll advance your career.

The Role

AMD's Global Sales Strategy & Planning organization is seeking a highly motivated and execution-focused Senior Manager, Cloud Partner Program Manager
to lead the implementation and operational readiness of the AMD Partner Network (APN) Cloud Program.

This highly visible role will serve as the operational leader and program management lead, translating the approved program strategy into a scalable, governed, and partner-ready operating model. The opportunity combines enterprise program leadership, cloud and channel operations, financial governance, and cross-functional execution to support the continued growth of AMD's cloud partner ecosystem. Beyond the initial implementation, this position is expected to evolve into end-to-end operational leadership of AMD's Cloud Partner Program, providing continuity, governance, and accountability as the program scales throughout 2027 and beyond.

Working closely with Cloud Sales, the Cloud Business Unit, Finance, Legal, IT, Sales Operations, regional channel teams, and external platform providers, you will drive critical decisions, establish clear accountability, and coordinate implementation across the full partner lifecycle, from onboarding and certification through usage reporting, incentives, claims, and payments.

The successful candidate will bring strong operational discipline, business and financial acumen, and the ability to navigate complex organizational dependencies while turning program design into an effective, sustainable operating model.

The Person

Does this sound like you? We'd love to talk!

Enterprise Program Leadership: Proven ability to lead complex, cross-functional programs from strategy and design through implementation, launch, and ongoing operations.
Influence & Stakeholder Alignment: Ability to build alignment across Sales, Business Units, Finance, Legal, IT, Operations, regional teams, and external providers, influencing decisions without direct authority.
Operational Excellence: Strong discipline in establishing governance frameworks, integrated plans, accountability models, risk management, and measurable launch-readiness criteria.
Cloud & Channel Business Acumen: Understanding of cloud partner ecosystems, consumption-based business models, partner programs, incentives, Market Development Funds (MDF), and channel operations.
Financial & Analytical Acumen: Ability to translate program economics, usage metrics, partner tiers, rate structures, forecasts, and financial controls into actionable processes and management reporting.
Executive Communication: Strong ability to simplify complex issues, present clear recommendations, facilitate decisions, and communicate effectively with senior leadership.
Ownership & Adaptability: Self-directed, resourceful, and comfortable managing ambiguity, evolving requirements, and multiple interdependent priorities in a fast-paced environment.

Key Responsibilities

Lead the end-to-end implementation of AMD's 2027 APN Cloud Program, establishing an integrated program plan, milestones, dependencies, risk management, and executive reporting.
Drive cross-functional decisions related to program measurement, data validation, partner tiers, rate structures, funding, partner caps, and regional implementation priorities.
Translate approved program design into scalable operating processes, standard operating procedures (SOPs), workflows, and governance controls across the partner lifecycle.
Coordinate implementation across partner onboarding, certification, usage reporting, incentives, Market Development Funds (MDF), claims, and payments.
Establish clear accountability through governance frameworks, responsibility matrices (RACI), decision tracking, escalation processes, and cross-functional operating cadences.
Partner with Cloud Sales, the Cloud Business Unit, Finance, Legal, IT, Sales Operations, and regional teams to ensure implementation readiness and timely resolution of dependencies.
Lead operational readiness for cloud usage reporting, including partner billing inputs, data validation, exception management, reconciliation, and audit documentation.
Collaborate with Finance and Cloud Business Unit stakeholders to operationalize program funding, budgets, forecasts, partner caps, accruals, and payment controls.
Partner with program design owners to implement consistent usage-based measurement methodologies, including virtual CPU (vCPU) and Mix Value calculations, eligibility rules, tier thresholds, and validation standards.
Coordinate pilot execution and launch readiness, including partner onboarding, agreements, test claims, operational testing, readiness reviews, and lessons learned.
Develop executive dashboards and management reporting covering implementation progress, program economics, incentive and MDF performance, financial exposure, risks, and launch readiness.
Facilitate cross-functional workstream reviews, leadership checkpoints, and decision-making forums, ensuring accountability and timely execution.
Establish a sustainable operating model for ongoing program management, including governance, ownership, escalation processes, quarterly business reviews, and change control.

Proven experience in cloud program management and operations, with direct responsibility for implementing and managing complex cloud partner or commercial programs.
Demonstrated ownership of large-scale, cross-functional implementations across Sales, Finance, Legal, IT, and regional teams, from program design through launch.
Strong knowledge of cloud partner ecosystems and program operations, including partner onboarding, tiering, incentives or rebates, Market Development Funds (MDF), claims, and governance.
Experience developing and managing integrated program plans, accountability frameworks (RACI), decision logs, risk registers, executive dashboards, and operating cadences.
Strong analytical and financial capabilities, including program economics, forecasting, rate structures, consumption or usage data, and financial controls.
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including executive-level recommendations and senior stakeholder decision facilitation.
Highly autonomous and detail-oriented, with the ability to manage multiple interdependent workstreams under tight timelines.

Preferred Experience

Experience working within major public cloud ecosystems, including AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle Cloud, or comparable platforms.
Experience operationalizing consumption- or usage-based cloud partner programs, including data ingestion, validation, baseline and growth calculations, reconciliation, and exception management.
Understanding of financial governance, budgeting, accruals, payment controls, legal review processes, and SOX compliance requirements.
Experience with partner relationship management, incentive management, analytics, or cloud usage platforms such as Impartner, Model N, Salesforce, Power BI, or comparable enterprise systems.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint, including executive dashboards, business analysis, and management reporting.
Experience leveraging AI-enabled tools and automation to improve analysis, documentation, reporting, and program management efficiency.
Formal project or program management training, certification, or experience with Agile program delivery methodologies.

Academic Credentials

Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Operations, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Advanced degree preferred.

LOCATION:

Austin, TX, Santa Clara, CA or Seattle, WA

This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship.

jobs.description:
Company Description

Work with Us. Change the World.

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

Job Description

Lead Complex Remediation Programs. Develop High-Performing Teams. Shape the Future of Environmental Program Delivery.

AECOM is seeking a senior remediation leader to oversee one of our largest environmental remediation portfolios supporting Oil & Gas clients across the western United States.

This is a strategic leadership role responsible for delivering a portfolio of approximately $30M-$50M annually
, while leading a team of 3-5 Program Managers and multidisciplinary project delivery teams
. You will play a critical role in ensuring safe, compliant, profitable, and high-quality project execution while partnering closely with clients to solve complex environmental challenges.

The successful candidate will be a proven leader with remediation experience, strong business acumen, and a demonstrated ability to build high-performing teams, strengthen client relationships, and drive operational excellence.

The Opportunity

As the Remediation Program Manager,
you will serve as the senior delivery leader for a major Oil & Gas remediation program. You will be accountable for portfolio performance, resource planning, risk management, client satisfaction, and financial success, while coaching and developing the next generation of Program Managers.

You will work closely with business line leadership, technical experts, client account teams, and operations leaders to drive execution certainty and support future growth.

Key Responsibilities

Portfolio Leadership and Delivery

Lead the successful delivery of a $30M-$50M remediation portfolio across multiple programs and projects.
Provide leadership and oversight to a team of Program Managers and project delivery professionals.
Ensure projects are delivered safely, on schedule, within budget, and in accordance with contractual commitments.
Drive portfolio performance against key operational, financial, safety, and client satisfaction metrics.
Serve as the primary escalation point for complex delivery, commercial, and client issues.
Lead portfolio-level risk identification, mitigation, and contingency planning.
Champion execution certainty through proactive project reviews and performance management.
Advance the adoption of digital tools, data-driven decision making, and operational efficiencies.

Client Leadership

Develop and maintain trusted relationships with key client stakeholders.
Act as a strategic advisor to clients, helping them navigate complex environmental and remediation challenges.
Ensure delivery excellence while identifying opportunities to expand services and strengthen partnerships.
Collaborate with Client Account Managers to support account growth and client retention.

People Leadership

Directly lead and mentor Program Managers and senior project professionals.
Foster a culture of accountability, safety, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
Support workforce planning, succession planning, recruitment, and talent development.
Develop future remediation leaders through coaching and structured career development.

Business Growth

Partner with Environmental Business Line leadership to grow profitable backlog and expand client relationships.
Support strategic pursuit planning and major opportunity capture efforts.
Contribute to annual business planning, forecasting, and portfolio management activities.
Help shape the future direction of AECOM's remediation practice and technical capabilities.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Geology, or a related discipline and 10+ years of relevant environmental consulting, remediation, or program management experience. or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education, including 2 years of leadership.
A valid driver’s license is required, along with the ability to pass a Motor Vehicle Records (MVR) check in accordance with company policy
Ability to meet applicable background screening requirements.
U.S. Citizenship or Permanent Residency required.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in Environmental Engineering, Geoscience, or related discipline.
Professional registration such as P.E. or P.G.
15+ years of environmental consulting and remediation experience.
Demonstrated experience leading large, complex remediation portfolios and multidisciplinary teams.
Experience managing Program Managers or other senior project leaders.
Strong understanding of environmental remediation programs supporting the Oil & Gas sector.
Experience operating within state and federal regulatory frameworks, including Colorado, Texas, California, or similar jurisdictions.
Proven success managing client relationships, financial performance, and business growth.
Exceptional communication, leadership, and stakeholder engagement skills.

Additional Information

Sponsorship for this role now and in the future will not be available.

Why This Role?

This position offers the opportunity to:
Lead one of AECOM's large Oil and Gas remediation portfolios.
Manage and mentor a team of Program Managers.
Influence strategic decisions impacting clients, operations, and growth.
Drive meaningful environmental outcomes across complex remediation programs.
Work with industry-leading technical experts and delivery teams.
Shape the future of remediation delivery within a global organization.

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

Offered rate of compensation will be based on individual education, qualifications, experience, and work location. The range for this position is $170000 to $225000.

About AECOM

AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options, well-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan.

AECOM is the global infrastructure leader, committed to delivering a better world. As a trusted professional services firm powered by deep technical abilities, we solve our clients’ complex challenges in water, environment, energy, transportation and buildings. Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at aecom.com.

What makes AECOM a great place to work

You will be part of a global team that champions your growth and career ambitions. Work on groundbreaking projects - both in your local community and on a global scale - that are transforming our industry and shaping the future. With cutting-edge technology and a network of experts, you’ll have the resources to make a real impact. Our award-winning training and development programs are designed to expand your technical expertise and leadership skills, helping you build the career you’ve always envisioned. Here, you’ll find a welcoming workplace built on respect, collaboration and community—where you have the freedom to grow in a world of opportunity.

As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in your potential and are here to help you achieve it. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

jobs.title: Senior Program Manager, Forward Deployed Engineering
jobs.description:
At NiCE, we don’t limit our challenges. We challenge our limits. Always. We’re ambitious. We’re game changers. And we play to win. We set the highest standards and execute beyond them. And if you’re like us, we can offer you the ultimate career opportunity that will light a fire within you.

So, what's the role all about?

The Senior Program Manager, Forward Deployed Engineering, partners with our Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) to turn customer proofs of concept (POCs) into delivered outcomes and clear product requirements. You are customer-facing: you run the engagement plan with the customer, keep scope and timelines honest, and make sure what the FDE learns on site reaches Product and Engineering in a form they can act on.

You will sit in the program function in Business Operations within NiCE's Engagement Orchestration product organization, working alongside the FDE, Customer Success, and account teams. The role is technical and communication-heavy: you will be in the room with customer executives and engineers one day, and with Product Owners and Engineering leads the next.

How will you make an impact?

Run customer POCs and engagements with the FDE: build the plan, scope, and timeline, set success criteria with the customer, and keep milestones, risks, and decisions visible.
Be a trusted, customer-facing point of contact: lead working sessions and status meetings, manage expectations, and communicate clearly with customer executives and technical teams.
Translate POC findings into product requirements: write problem statements, user stories, acceptance criteria, and success metrics that Product and Engineering can prioritize and build against.
Separate one-off from repeatable: identify patterns across customers and bring evidence to Product so productize, standardize, or stop decisions are made deliberately.
Partner with Product Owners and Engineering leads: take requirements through intake, track them in Jira, and report back to the customer and FDE on status.
Manage dependencies, risks, and escalations across the customer, FDE, Product, Engineering, Customer Success, and Support, and raise blockers early with the tradeoff stated.
Plan the hand-off: make sure each engagement ends with documentation, enablement, and a named owner on the customer side and on the product team.
Keep Jira, Salesforce, and Confluence current so customer commitments, requirements, and engagement status reconcile.
Coordinate with the cross-functional program team where a customer's issues also need a broader program, so customers see one coordinated response.
Improve the FDE operating model: build intake, scoping, and reporting templates, and track how many POCs convert to product decisions and roadmap items.

Have you got what it takes?

5-7+ years of program, project, or product management in a software or SaaS environment, with at least 3 years in customer-facing delivery, solutions, or professional services.
Comfort in technical environments: you can follow integrations, APIs, architecture, and defect discussions, ask good questions, and explain them to executives and non-technical stakeholders.
Exceptional written and verbal communication, including running customer meetings and writing requirements that engineers can build from.
Experience turning ambiguous customer needs into clear requirements, user stories, and acceptance criteria.
Proven ability to influence without direct authority across customers, engineering, and product teams.
Strong scoping, risk, and dependency management in time-boxed engagements, including the judgment to say no or to escalate early.
Hands-on experience with Jira, Confluence, and Salesforce for tracking, reporting, and documentation.
Working knowledge of Agile and Scrum and the software delivery lifecycle.
Commercial awareness and sound stakeholder management with customers, sales, and Customer Success.
Bachelor's degree in Business, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

You will have an advantage if:

Experience in CCaaS, CX, conversational AI, or agentic workflow products.
Background in forward deployed engineering, solutions engineering, sales engineering, or technical product management.
Experience converting bespoke customer work into scalable product capabilities.
Experience running POCs, pilots, or design partnerships with enterprise customers.
Comfort with data and analytics tools such as Power BI, SQL, or Tableau.
PMP, Agile, or similar certification.

What’s in it for you?

Join an ever-growing, market disrupting, global company where the teams – comprised of the best of the best – work in a fast-paced, collaborative, and creative environment! As the market leader, every day at NICE is a chance to learn and grow, and there are endless internal career opportunities across multiple roles, disciplines, domains, and locations. If you are passionate, innovative, and excited to constantly raise the bar, you may just be our next NICEr!

Enjoy NICE-FLEX!

At NICE, we work according to the NICE-FLEX hybrid model, which enables maximum flexibility: 2 days working from the office and 3 days of remote work, each week. Naturally, office days focus on face-to-face meetings, where teamwork and collaborative thinking generate innovation, new ideas, and a vibrant, interactive atmosphere.

jobs.title: Senior Program Manager
jobs.description:
As our Sr. Program Manager at Macmillan Learning, you'll drive the commercial success and educational impact of our Earth Systems portfolio—spanning earth science, environmental science, ecology, and botany—while leading our STEM-wide growth strategy for labs and authentic scientific practice. You'll own business strategy and P&L performance across your portfolio and partner with Go-to-Market, Product, Sales, Marketing, Implementation, and fellow STEM portfolio leads to build distinctive, scalable learning experiences across physical materials, digital simulations, inquiry, and experimentation. Reporting to the Executive Program Director, STEM, you'll strengthen our market position and help shape the future of undergraduate STEM education.

This role is built for someone who enjoys turning market intelligence, educator insights, and evolving scientific practices into actionable product and investment strategies. You'll bring strong commercial and analytical instincts alongside the relationship-building skills needed to engage authors, disciplinary leaders, and cross-functional partners across established and emerging STEM markets.

What You'll Do

Earth Systems Portfolio Strategy & P&L Ownership: You'll define and execute business strategy for earth science, environmental science, ecology, and botany in partnership with Go-to-Market teams, owning portfolio P&L performance and using financial, competitive, and TAM/SAM/SOM market intelligence to achieve commercial goals.
STEM-Wide Labs & Authentic Scientific Practice Strategy: You'll own the cross-STEM growth strategy for labs and authentic scientific practice across all disciplines and delivery models—spanning physical materials, digital simulation, inquiry, experimentation, and emerging approaches—in coordination with other STEM portfolio leads.
Growth Development & Investment Prioritization: You'll evaluate opportunities across disciplines and institutional segments, assess right to play and right to win, and build data-informed business cases to secure investment for new initiatives, products, and learning experiences.
Market & Disciplinary Intelligence: You'll track academic disciplines, instructional innovations, laboratory and field teaching practices, and emerging competitors, combining external signals with internal insights to identify market gaps and guide product direction.
External Engagement & STEM Leadership: You'll cultivate a diverse network of thought leaders, innovators, and change agents, convening conversations and positioning Macmillan Learning as a destination of choice for influential partners and promising proposals.
Author & Collaborator Partnerships: You'll engage current authors in evolving digital and portfolio strategies—aligning textbook updates and revisions with broader product directions—while building relationships with collaborators and content creators.
Cross-Functional Execution: You'll align Product, Sales, Marketing, Implementation, and senior leadership around cohesive strategies, translating prioritized opportunities into actionable roadmaps with clear accountability for commercial and educational outcomes.

What You Bring To The Team

Experience commensurate with a senior-level position in educational publishing, learning product or program management, curriculum strategy, or a related commercial and content leadership role.
A conferred bachelor's degree in a STEM discipline.
Strong knowledge of undergraduate laboratory and field instruction, including how students develop and apply authentic scientific skills.
Proven financial and commercial acumen, including experience owning portfolio P&L performance, conducting market opportunity assessments (TAM/SAM/SOM), and building data-informed business cases for investment.
Strategic thinking and sound judgment in ambiguous environments, with the ability to weigh incomplete market evidence, evaluate right to play/right to win, and prioritize which opportunities to pursue, test, defer, or stop.
Demonstrated ability to build strategic external networks with educators, authors, and disciplinary leaders, translating varied institutional and instructor perspectives into inclusive, customer-centered solutions.
Exceptional communication and coalition-building skills, with experience aligning cross-functional partners and presenting complex market evidence and business recommendations to senior stakeholders.

SALARY RANGE

The base salary range for this full-time position is $95,000 to $115,000/year.
Final salary will be determined once interviews and assessments are complete. This role is also eligible for participation in the company bonus plan.

JOB LOCATION

This is a hybrid role based in Austin, TX, working between our office at Braker & 183 and your home office.

TRAVEL

Up to 10% travel for conferences and work related events.

Benefits

Health coverage from day one. Time to step away. Support for what comes next.

Your health: Medical, dental, and vision insurance, including HSA-qualified, EPO, and PPO medical plan options; an HSA with employer contributions for eligible participants; and mental health support through Headspace.
Your financial future: Participation in the company bonus plan, company retirement contributions through Fidelity's 401(k) plan in the U.S. or a Registered Retirement Savings Plan in Canada, and 100% employer-paid life and AD&D insurance.
Your time: Paid time off, sick time, floating holidays, and paid company holidays.
Your everyday support: Employee Assistance and Education Assistance programs, plus commuter assistance for eligible employees.
Your next read: Access to Macmillan Publishing's library, with free ebook and audio book downloads and discounts on physical books.

Benefits begin on the employee's date of hire for regular full-time and qualifying part-time employees and their eligible dependents. Health coverage is also available to qualifying domestic partners; additional documentation may be required.

The Roseburg VA Medical Center Green Environmental Management Systems (GEMS) program manager is the key member of the VAMC GEMS Committee responsible for responsible for implementing - developing and maintaining - and ensuring the GEMS Program remains compliant with ISO 14001 Environmental Management System across RVAMC organizational elements.

Qualifications

To qualify for this position - applicants must meet all requirements by the closing date of this announcement - 11/27/2026. Time-In-Grade Requirement: Applicants who are current Federal employees and have held a GS grade any time in the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements by the closing date of this announcement. For a GS-11 position you must have served 52 weeks at the GS-9. The grade may have been in any occupation - but must have been held in the Federal service. An SF-50 that shows your time-in-grade eligibility must be submitted with your application materials. If the most recent SF-50 has an effective date within the past year - it may not clearly demonstrate you possess one-year time-in-grade - as required by the announcement. In this instance - you must provide an additional SF-50 that clearly demonstrates one-year time-in-grade. Note: Time-In-Grade requirements also apply to former Federal employees applying for reinstatement as well as current employees applying for Veterans Employment Opportunities Act of 1998 (VEOA) appointment. You may qualify based on your experience and/or education as described below: Specialized Experience: You must have one year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the next lower grade (GS-9) in the normal line of progression for the occupation in the organization. Examples of specialized experience would typically include - but are not limited to: planning - implementing - and evaluating environmental protection programs; administering a green environmental management program; leading environmental facility inspections to ensure compliance with applicable laws and regulations; advising management on environmental program status; preparing reports; and training others on specific environmental topics. OR - Education: Applicants may substitute education for the required experience. To qualify based on education for this grade level you must have a Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree. This education must demonstrate the knowledge - skills - and abilities necessary to do the work of this position. The Platform Services and Emerging Technologies (PSET) team is seeking a Technical Program Manager (TPM) to drive successful delivery of Autodesk's Generative AI Accelerator (GAIA) outcomes.

In this role, you will drive complex, cross-functional programs that move emerging AI capabilities from research into production. This role requires strong technical depth including AI fluency, excellent execution discipline, and the ability to operate effectively across organizations to align priorities, manage risk, and drive outcomes in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.

Aperçu du Poste

L'équipe « Platform Services and Emerging Technologies » (PSET) recherche un responsable de programme technique (TPM) chargé de piloter la mise en œuvre réussie des résultats du programme « Generative AI Accelerator » (GAIA) d'Autodesk.

À ce poste, vous piloterez des programmes complexes et transversaux visant à faire passer les capacités émergentes en IA de la recherche à la production. Vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec les responsables de la recherche, de l’ingénierie, de l’architecture, des données, de la sécurité, des affaires juridiques et des produits afin de garantir que les nouvelles capacités d’IA soient mises en œuvre de manière responsable, prévisible et à grande échelle.

Ce poste exige de solides connaissances techniques, notamment une maîtrise approfondie de l’IA, une excellente discipline d’exécution et la capacité à intervenir efficacement au sein de différentes structures organisationnelles pour aligner les priorités, gérer les risques et obtenir des résultats dans des environnements ambigus et en constante évolution.

Piloter la mise en œuvre de bout en bout des résultats du programme GAIA, de l’expérimentation à la mise en production et à l’adoption
Piloter les résultats commerciaux obtenus grâce à la mise en œuvre des capacités d’IA/ML, en partenariat avec les équipes d’ingénierie et les responsables dans les domaines de l’intégration des produits, de l’adoption de la plateforme et de l’évolutivité opérationnelle
Élaborer et maintenir des plans de mise en œuvre intégrés entre les équipes de recherche et d’ingénierie, en garantissant la clarté des jalons, des dépendances et de la gestion des risques
Piloter les prévisions de mise en œuvre, le suivi de l’exécution et le reporting transparent tout au long du cycle de vie des programmes
Orchestrer la mise en œuvre entre les équipes de recherche, d’ingénierie, de sécurité, juridiques, produit et de plateforme, en suivant les répercussions en aval sur tout ce qu’elles touchent
Collaborer avec les parties prenantes de la direction, les architectes et les responsables produit pour définir la stratégie, l’enchaînement des étapes et les plans d’exécution
Fournir des rapports d’état clairs et exploitables tant au niveau de la direction qu’au niveau des équipes, incluant les risques, les compromis et les stratégies d’atténuation
Anticiper les dépendances et les risques plutôt que de les découvrir a posteriori, qu’il s’agisse des données, de l’état de préparation des modèles ou des délais de mise en œuvre
Soutenir les équipes en éliminant les obstacles, en gérant les exceptions et en résolvant les dépendances
Utiliser de manière responsable les outils d’IA et d’automatisation approuvés pour garantir la visibilité, la reproductibilité et une source unique de vérité tout au long de la livraison, tout en validant les résultats et en préservant le jugement humain
Promouvoir les pratiques de livraison Agile et Lean, en soutenant les équipes auto-organisées évoluant dans des environnements complexes
S’appuyer sur des données factuelles et des enseignements validés pour adapter les plans, améliorant ainsi l’efficacité de la livraison, la collaboration et les résultats du programme
Agir en tant qu’agent du changement, en aidant les équipes à s’adapter à l’évolution des exigences, aux incertitudes liées à la recherche et aux priorités de la plateforme

Excellentes compétences en communication et en gestion des parties prenantes, avec la capacité d’influencer des publics tant techniques que non techniques
