jobs.title: Senior Program Manager, Cross-Functional Programs
jobs.description:
At NiCE, we don’t limit our challenges. We challenge our limits. Always. We’re ambitious. We’re game changers. And we play to win. We set the highest standards and execute beyond them. And if you’re like us, we can offer you the ultimate career opportunity that will light a fire within you.

So, what's the role all about?

The Senior Program Manager, within NiCE's Engagement Orchestration product organization, runs cross-functional programs that resolve critical customer and product issues spanning multiple engineering teams, and keeps leadership, Product, Engineering, Customer Success, and Support working from one accurate status. The role coordinates; product and engineering teams deliver and own the outcome.

You will sit in the program function in Business Operations, outside Product and R&D. You will lead one to three programs at a time, each a short, sprint-style effort with a named sponsor, a defined outcome, and a clear exit. You will also help run the program system itself: intake, triage, charter, cadence, and reporting.

This is a technical, high-visibility role. You will be in the room with Product Owners, Engineering leads, and executives, and you need to make complex cross-team problems simple to act on.

How will you make an impact?

Lead assigned customer escalation and cross-customer issue programs end to end: draft the charter with the sponsor and engineering leaders, run the three-week cycles, and drive each program to validated close or an agreed disposition.
Run weekly planning for each program, naming next week's work and the specific people needed, and sizing requests in hours of named people against each team's committed capacity.
Keep status accurate and visible: maintain one shared view of progress, risks, blockers, and decisions, and publish a weekly report for leadership, Product, and Customer Success.
Escalate early and cleanly. Raise blockers over 48 hours, bring declined requests to leadership with the tradeoff stated, and record the decision.
Work with engineering and product leaders and their team representatives to turn program requests into team commitments, and check delivery areas (documentation, UX, launch readiness, enablement) at exit.
Support intake and triage: assess nominations from escalation reports, the unified issue view, commitments reviews, and demand themes against entry criteria (red account, revenue at risk, aged P1/P2 defects, customer commitment at risk, or shared root cause).
Keep Jira, Salesforce, and Confluence clean and connected so commitments, defects, and customer cases reconcile at exit.
Coordinate with other lines of business where an issue spans them, running our workstream under one shared status.
Improve the program model: gather lessons from each cycle, tune thresholds and templates, and help evaluate the one-quarter pilot against its goals.

Have you got what it takes?

5-7+ years of program or project management in a software or SaaS environment, including cross-functional programs with Product and Engineering.
Comfort in technical environments: you can follow architecture, defect, and release discussions, ask good questions, and translate them for non-technical leaders.
Excellent written and verbal communication, with the ability to tailor the same update for engineers, Customer Success, and executives.
Proven ability to influence without direct authority and to lead through ambiguity across teams and organizations.
Strong risk, dependency, and escalation management, including the judgment to know when to escalate and the discipline to do it early.
Hands-on experience with Jira, Confluence, and Salesforce for tracking, reporting, and documentation.
Working knowledge of Agile and Scrum, and of the software delivery lifecycle: planning, defect triage, release readiness, and customer commitments.
Strong organization, attention to detail, and the ability to manage several time-boxed efforts at once under pressure.
Bachelor's degree in Business, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

You will have an advantage if:

Experience in CCaaS, CX, or AI product environments, or with enterprise customers on escalated accounts.
Background in Scrum Master, QA, release management, or engineering roles.
Experience building program frameworks such as intake, charters, status reporting, and governance.
Comfort with data and reporting tools such as Power BI, SQL, or Tableau.
PMP, Agile, or similar certification.
Experience using AI tools to speed up reporting, analysis, and documentation.

What’s in it for you?

Join an ever-growing, market disrupting, global company where the teams – comprised of the best of the best – work in a fast-paced, collaborative, and creative environment! As the market leader, every day at NICE is a chance to learn and grow, and there are endless internal career opportunities across multiple roles, disciplines, domains, and locations. If you are passionate, innovative, and excited to constantly raise the bar, you may just be our next NICEr!

Enjoy NICE-FLEX!

At NICE, we work according to the NICE-FLEX hybrid model, which enables maximum flexibility: 2 days working from the office and 3 days of remote work, each week. Naturally, office days focus on face-to-face meetings, where teamwork and collaborative thinking generate innovation, new ideas, and a vibrant, interactive atmosphere.

Senior Director, Product Operations

NICE Ltd. About Bridge

We're creating an entirely new payments platform, built with stablecoins, to simplify global money movement. Bridge enables faster, cheaper payments and borderless access to dollars via stablecoins. Through our APIs, businesses can send and receive funds across borders faster and cheaper vs. SWIFT and other fiat-only rails. Our virtual accounts enable international consumers and businesses to easily access, store, and spend US dollars. Our payouts infrastructure enables platforms to disburse USD to anyone globally. We have a small team of people who have previously built financial infrastructure at some of the world's leading companies (Coinbase, Stripe, Square, Brex, Upstart, DoorDash, Airbnb), and each and every one of them chose Bridge because they fundamentally believe that stablecoins will be a critical piece of financial infrastructure that allows for the improvement of global money movement.

Company Description

Job Description

Remote Approved - Must be in USA.

We are seeking an experienced Security Manager to lead the governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) pillar of our Enterprise Cybersecurity program. This people-leadership role owns the cybersecurity governance operating rhythm, executive and board-level reporting, third-party security risk management, data security program management, security awareness, and cybersecurity policy and compliance activities. The Security Manager is accountable for the cadence, quality, and continuity of these programs — turning security metrics, risk data, and regulatory requirements into clear, actionable insight for leadership and the Board.

The ideal candidate combines strong program and people management with a solid understanding of security frameworks (such as NIST CSF and CMMC), risk management, and stakeholder engagement across IT, Legal, business units, and external partners. This role reports to the Sr. Dir, Enterprise Cyber Security and directly manages analysts supporting governance, risk, and awareness functions.

Responsibilities

Cybersecurity Governance & Reporting

Own the cybersecurity governance program, including the Monthly Cybersecurity Metrics Report and Quarterly Board Dashboard measures.
Define and maintain cybersecurity metrics, KPIs, and KRIs; track program maturity against the NIST CSF; and drive strategic initiatives, risks, and governance commitments to closure.
Coordinate identity governance activities, including monthly AD account reviews, access certifications, and IAM metrics reporting.
Coordinate cybersecurity inputs for the annual cyber insurance renewal and annual Incident Response Plan update and Management tabletop exercise.

Data Security Program Management

Lead data discovery and classification governance across IT, Legal, and business stakeholders, tracking data risk reduction and reporting progress through program metrics.

Third-Party & Supplier Cyber Risk Management

Manage the third-party cyber risk assessment program, including new third-party service reviews, periodic reassessments, critical-supplier (direct and indirect) assessments, and FBIN questionnaires.
Track and drive remediation of third-party and supplier risks and integrate cyber-risk data into governance reporting.

Security Vendor Administration & Operational Oversight

Provide governance administration for cybersecurity vendors (PO creation, invoice processing, DocuSign workflows, renewal tracking) and support legal/contract activities such as NDA/MNDA reviews and security questionnaire responses.

Cybersecurity Policies, Standards & Compliance

Maintain cybersecurity governance documentation, coordinating annual policy and standard updates, approvals, publication and archive.
Support compliance initiatives including SOX controls, CMMC readiness, NIST CSF maturity reporting, SOC 2 assurance, and audit evidence collection and manage governance repositories and control attestations.

Security Awareness Program

Administer the enterprise security awareness program, including annual training, new hire training, National Cybersecurity Awareness Month, quarterly phishing simulations and ad hoc awareness articles on the FBIN intranet.

Leadership & Continuous Improvement

Manage, mentor, and develop analysts supporting governance, risk, and awareness functions.
Partner with cross-functional teams: IT, Legal, connected product, and business units to embed security best practices and continuously improve the maturity, efficiency, and clarity of processes and reporting.

KEY COMPETENCIES

Collaborate: Build partnerships and work collaboratively with others to meet shared objectives.
Communicate Effectively: Develop and deliver multi-mode communications that convey a clear understanding of the unique needs of different audiences.
Instill Trust: Gain the confidence and trust of others through honesty, integrity, and authenticity.
Builds Effective Teams: Attract, develop, and retain talent to meet current and future organizational needs.
Drives Results: Consistently achieve results, even under challenging circumstances.
Decision Quality: Make sound and timely decisions that keep the organization moving forward.
Plans and Aligns: Plan and prioritize work to meet commitments aligned with organizational goals.
Ensures Accountability: Hold self and others accountable to meet commitments.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Information Security, Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
Minimum of 7+ years of overall technology experience, with at least 5+ years in an information security, cybersecurity, or GRC role.
Demonstrated experience owning cybersecurity governance, risk, or compliance programs and producing executive- or board-level reporting.
Working knowledge of security frameworks such as NIST CSF and CMMC, and of enterprise risk and third-party risk management practices.
Experience coordinating security awareness, data security, or identity governance programs across cross-functional stakeholders.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex security topics for technical and non-technical audiences, including leadership.
Strong analytical, organizational, and program-management skills.

Preferred

Prior people-leadership or team-management experience.
Relevant certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CRISC, CISA, or CompTIA Security+.
Experience with GRC and risk platforms and data security tooling.
Familiarity with SOC 2, cyber insurance renewal processes, and audit/assurance coordination.
Experience supporting incident response governance and tabletop exercises.

jobs.description:
JOB SUMMARY:
The Security Manager is responsible for the leadership, administration, and oversight of the company's security programs supporting defense, aerospace, unmanned systems, and government contracting operations. This position manages personnel security, facility security, physical security, classified contract compliance, COMSEC accountability, Technology Control Plan (TCP) administration, and security awareness initiatives while ensuring compliance with applicable government, customer, and contractual security requirements.
The Security Manager serves as the principal security advisor to management, supporting the protection of classified information, controlled technical information, company assets, personnel, and facilities. This role works closely with Operations, Engineering, Information Technology, Human Resources, and Program Management to maintain a strong security posture and ensure operational readiness.

DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES:
• Serve as the company's designated Facility Security Officer and administer the industrial security program in accordance with NISPOM, DCSA, and contractual security requirements.
• Develop, implement, and continuously improve security policies, procedures, and programs to ensure compliance with NISPOM, contractual requirements, customer directives, and company standards.
• Serve as the primary liaison with DCSA representatives, including ISRs and Industrial Security Integration (ISI) personnel, as well as government security officials, customers, auditors, and inspectors.
• Manage personnel security programs, including clearance processing, access authorizations, visit requests, security briefings, debriefings, training, recordkeeping, and related investigations.
• Administer facility security programs, including Facility Clearance (FCL) requirements, access control, visitor management, badging, physical security measures, and security inspections.
• Lead responses to security incidents, violations, emergencies, and corrective action initiatives.
• Oversee COMSEC accountability and ensure the proper handling, storage, transfer, inventory, destruction, and safeguarding of classified communications assets and materials.
• Develop, implement, and maintain Technology Control Plans (TCPs), including monitoring access to controlled information, systems, facilities, technical data, and restricted programs.
• Assist with the planning, design, construction, accreditation, and ongoing compliance of Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities (SCIFs).
• Conduct audits, inspections, and compliance reviews to assess adherence to security requirements and identify areas for improvement.
• Maintain security documentation and records required by government regulations, customer requirements, and company policies.
• Monitor regulatory, contractual, and security program changes and implement necessary updates to maintain compliance.
• Develop and deliver security awareness and compliance training programs and promote a culture of security throughout the organization.
• Advise leadership on security risks, regulatory requirements, mitigation strategies, and operational impacts.
• Perform other duties as assigned.

BASIC REQUIREMENTS:
• Bachelor's degree in Security Management, Criminal Justice, Homeland Security, Business Administration, Intelligence Studies, or a related field; or an equivalent combination of education, training, military service, and relevant experience.
• Minimum seven (7) years of progressively responsible experience administering industrial security programs within a defense, aerospace, intelligence, or government contracting environment.
• Demonstrated experience serving as a Facility Security Officer (FSO), Assistant Facility Security Officer (AFSO), Contractor Program Security Officer (CPSO), COMSEC Custodian, or in a comparable security leadership role with responsibility for NISP compliance.
• Thorough knowledge of the National Industrial Security Program Operating Manual (NISPOM), DCSA regulations, classified contract administration, and facility clearance requirements.
• Experience working directly with DCSA representatives, including Industrial Security Representatives (ISRs), during inspections, self-assessments, corrective actions, and ongoing compliance activities.
• Working knowledge of government security systems, including DISS, NISS, NBIS, and related personnel security and industrial security applications.
• Experience administering COMSEC accountability programs, including inventory management, safeguarding, destruction procedures, audits, and recordkeeping requirements.
• Experience developing, implementing, and maintaining Technology Control Plans (TCPs) and controlling access to sensitive, proprietary, or classified information and systems.
• Experience supporting the planning, construction, accreditation, or operation of secure facilities, including SCIFs, closed areas, and other classified workspaces.
• Knowledge of classified information handling requirements, document accountability, physical security controls, visitor control procedures, security incident reporting, and safeguarding requirements.
• Ability to interpret government regulations, contract security requirements, ICDs, and customer directives and translate them into practical business processes and security procedures.
• Strong organizational, analytical, and investigative skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining accurate and compliant security records.
• Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to brief executive leadership, employees, auditors, government officials, and customer representatives.
• Demonstrated ability to exercise sound judgment, discretion, and professionalism when handling classified, controlled, proprietary, and sensitive information.
• Must be a U.S. Citizen.
• Must possess and maintain an active Secret or Top Secret security clearance; Top Secret clearance with SCI eligibility is strongly preferred.
• Must be capable of obtaining and maintaining all required government accesses and customer-specific security authorizations.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:
• Active Top Secret clearance with SCI eligibility or current TS/SCI.
• Experience as the primary FSO for a cleared facility.
• Experience supporting SAP, SCI, SCIF, or Special Access environments.
• Certified Industrial Security Professional (ISP), Security Fundamentals Professional Certification (SFPC), Industrial Security Oversight Certification (ISOC), or comparable security credential.
• NSA COMSEC training and certification.
• Experience supporting aerospace, UAV/UAS, defense manufacturing, research and development, or engineering operations.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Must be able to lift up to 15 pounds at times.
• Ability to traverse the manufacturing facility.

The role is critical in safeguarding the organisation’s people, information, assets, and operations while supporting business resilience and crisis management efforts. The successful candidate will also work collaboratively as part of a global security function, providing regional leadership and expertise in a dynamic, fast-paced environment.

The successful post holder will also hold Group Security Controller responsibilities for Collins Aerospace locations in the United Kingdom.

This is a UK based remote position.

What You Will Do:

Strategic Leadership and Compliance:

Develop and implement security strategies and initiatives that align with organisational goals and comply with UK Government Security requirements, including the HMG Security Policy Framework, ISO 17799 & 27001 Security Frameworks, Information Assurance Standards, HMG International Visits Control Office (IVCO) notifications, and Cabinet Office STAMP requirements.
Act as the Group Security Controller, ensuring compliance with all relevant regulations, including the management of Security Aspects Letters (SALs) and the flow-down of security requirements to third parties and subcontractors.
Support Security Controllers and Site Security Control Officials at UK locations to ensure compliance to both legal and company requirements.
Maintain a strong understanding of the UK Defence Sector’s security needs and vetting processes, ensuring full compliance with local laws, regulations, and customer expectations.
Conduct and oversee internal and external audits to ensure adherence to security policies and frameworks.

Facility and Physical Security Management:

Oversee security operations across multiple UK sites, including site access, access control, visitor management, and maintenance of accreditations.
Conduct regular physical security assessments to identify potential vulnerabilities and implement risk mitigation measures.
Support the management of technical and physical security systems, including access control, CCTV, alarm response procedures, and visitor management systems, in collaboration with the Global Security team and relevant Centres of Excellence (COEs).
Liaise with all relevant stakeholders in respect of on-site and off-site events, including overseas travel as required.

Security Awareness and Training:

Deliver security awareness training programs for both security and non-security practitioners on both HMG Security Frameworks and Physical Security requirements.
Conduct regular security briefings to senior leadership, site-based Security Control Officials, and employees.
Coordinate and support emergency response drills, ensuring all sites maintain updated security and evacuation plans.

Incident Response and Risk Management:

Lead incident response efforts, including investigations, reporting, root-cause analysis, and post-incident reviews.
Monitor emerging threats (e.g., geopolitical, terrorism, natural disasters) and conduct threat assessments and risk analyses to develop mitigation strategies.
Provide guidance and support to project/program teams on meeting customer security requirements, highlighting and escalating risks where necessary.

Vendor and Stakeholder Management:

Support locations with the management of third-party security vendors, contracts, and on-site personnel, ensuring quality, compliance, and performance.
Collaborate with HR, IT Security, Legal, Facilities, and other regional and global stakeholders to foster an integrated security culture.
Establish and maintain strong relationships with emergency services, law enforcement agencies, and ISAC/Contracting Authorities.

Skills, Experience and Qualifications You Must Have:

Extensive experience in UK Government Security practices, including HMG Security Framework, Information Assurance Standards, and Good Practice Guides.
In-depth knowledge of the UK Defence Sector, including Cabinet Office STAMP requirements and UK Security Vetting processes.
Familiarity with cryptographic material management and the role of a Crypto Custodian.
Proven regional or multi-site leadership experience in security, with the ability to manage diverse teams and stakeholders.
Strong understanding of physical and technical security systems, crisis management, risk mitigation practices, and information assurance.
Experience writing, maintaining, and ensuring compliance with security policies and procedures.
Exceptional interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to deliver briefings and build relationships at all levels, including senior leadership and board-level executives.
Ability to work independently and proactively, with strong problem-solving and decision-making skills.
Bachelor’s degree in security management, Criminal Justice, Risk Management, or a related field (Master’s preferred).
Prior relevant experience in protective security roles, including positions in corporate, regional, or government security.
Excellent verbal/written communication skills in English.
Strong understanding of physical security systems, crisis management, and risk mitigation practices.
Prior experience managing a budget and supervising both direct and indirect employees and contractors.
UK SC-level security clearance (existing clearance is highly desirable).

Skills, Qualifications and Experience We Prefer:

Membership of professional security and information assurance bodies (e.g., DISA, ASIS).
Relevant certifications such as Certified Protection Professional (CPP) or Physical Security Professional (PSP).
Detailed understanding of ISO 17799 & 27001 Security Frameworks.
Familiarity with cryptographic material management and the role of a Crypto Custodian.
Experience supporting travel security and executive protection initiatives.

Additional Requirements:

Willingness to travel across the UK, sometimes at short notice.
Occasional travel to the wider EMEA region.
High level of integrity and discretion, with the ability to handle sensitive information.
Demonstrated ability to work in a global security function, collaborating across different regions and cultures.

Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Team

The Risk Operations Enablement team sits within the Risk Operations org and is responsible for building and operating the core business and strategic programs that are critical to Risk Operations. These programs range from operational excellence initiatives to high-priority, cross-functional initiatives that typically require partnering across broader Risk (e.g., Risk Product) and risk-adjacent (e.g., Policy) teams. More specifically, we both lead initiatives to make step changes in the Risk User Experience and devise and execute strategies to ensure that a wide range of missing-critical business processes are effective at achieving our dual goals of preventing bad actors from exploiting our systems and delivering an exceptional user experience for legitimate users.

What you'll do

You'll partner cross-functionally across Risk (e.g., Risk Product) and Risk-adjacent (e.g., Policy) teams to lead ambiguous, high-priority problem spaces that change the trajectory of Risk Operations. You'll also partner across Risk Operations to deliver and measure processes that enable operational excellence at scale within the Risk Operations org.

Responsibilities

Lead complex global programs, from initial scoping to design and execution and work on high-impact strategic initiatives
Collaborate with multiple stakeholders across Risk Operations, Risk Product, Risk Eng, and other stakeholder teams (e.g., Policy, Data Science) to prioritize and maximize the impact of your projects
Design and launch programs that lead to step-change improvements in our operational processes and business outcomes
Serve as the Risk Operations expert and partner closely with our cross-functional stakeholders to scope and execute large projects to create operational efficiencies and ensure operational readiness
Embody our Operating Principles and foster our values and culture

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum Requirements

6+ years of experience in risk program management, strategy, management consulting, business operations, or operations program management
The ability to dig deep into the data and think from first principles while delivering the best results
Ability to manage multiple stakeholders with varying priorities and drive creative solutions and commitment to a shared goal
Strong program management skills with experience managing end-to-end execution of projects and programs that have transformed your company's operations
Enjoys solving complex and hard problems and can turn incomplete, conflicting, or ambiguous inputs into solid action plans and deliver quantifiable business impact
Ability to identify repeated user and specialist-facing issues and build scalable solutions and processes to address them

Preferred Qualifications

2+ years in consulting
Experience with SQL or willingness to learn
MBA or other graduate degree
Prior experience partnering with Product, Eng, and Operations teams preferred

Hybrid work at Stripe

This role is available either in an office or a remote location (35+ miles or 56+ km from a Stripe office).

In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This hits a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility about how to do this in a way that makes sense for individuals and their teams.

Working remotely at Stripe

A remote location is defined as being 35 miles (56 kilometers) or more from one of our offices. While you would be welcome to come into the office for team/business meetings, on-sites, meet-ups, and events, our expectation is you would regularly work from home rather than a Stripe office. Stripe does not cover the cost of relocating to a remote location. We encourage you to apply for roles that match the location where you currently live or plan to live.

Pay and benefits

The annual US base salary range for this role is $127,600 - $191,400. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.

We look forward to hearing from you.

At Stripe, we're looking for people with passion, grit, and integrity. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. Your skills and passion will stand out—and set you apart—especially if your career has taken some extraordinary twists and turns. At Stripe, we welcome diverse perspectives and people who think rigorously and aren't afraid to challenge assumptions. Join us.

Description & Requirements

Electronic Arts creates next-level entertainment experiences that inspire players and fans around the world. Here, everyone is part of the story. Part of a community that connects across the globe. A place where creativity thrives, new perspectives are invited, and ideas matter. A team where everyone makes play happen.

Founded in 2010 by the original creators of the Call of Duty Franchise, Respawn was created with the philosophy that when talented people have creative freedom, they'll make extraordinary games that achieve the unexpected. From our roots as an indie studio to joining the expansive roster of studios at Electronic Arts, this remains our guiding principle. We truly love what we do and want to share our passion with players worldwide. Our shipped titles include critically acclaimed multi-platform games Apex Legends, Titanfall, Titanfall 2, Star Wars™ Jedi: Fallen Order, Star Wars™ Jedi: Survivor and Medal of Honor: Above and Beyond. Join us for the opportunity to create groundbreaking games with some of the best developer talent in the industry.

You can learn more about our studio and values at respawn.com/studio.

About The Role

Apex Legends is a live-service game shipping on a seasonal cadence across many pods, regions and partners. As Program Manager, you own the studio-wide programs that no single pod can run alone. You design the systems, rhythms and handoffs that let Delivery Leads and their teams move faster.

This is a systems role, not a feature-delivery role. You won't own pod sprints or feature velocity. You'll own the operational connective tissue between Apex Production, QV, Finance, Talent Acquisition, Studio Ops and EA Shanghai.

What You'll Do

Level up Playtesting. Run a discovery tour with Design, Engineering and QV to find why playtests underperform: attendance, build readiness, feedback capture. Then stand up a predictable cadence, build gates and a standard debrief for creative leadership.
Run budget governance rituals. Partner with FP&A and Delivery Leads on regular check-ins that keep teams within their team and location envelopes. Roll out and support a standard spend template (spreadsheet or Airtable) that teams maintain, and flag overrun risk early.
Lead the China SKU partnership. Be the Apex point of contact for EA Shanghai on localizing and culturalizing the Rest of World SKU for mainland China. Track requirements, route asks to the right pods and keep both sides aligned on schedule.
Run headcount and hiring operations. Move requisition tracking from spreadsheets into Airtable, run the biweekly TA sync and improve studio onboarding with Studio Ops and People Experiences.
Drive other cross-initiative programs. Take on the next problem that spans pods, starting with a Confluence overhaul that makes it the trusted source of truth.

What You Bring

5+ years of program, production or operations management in games or another live-service product.
A track record of building systems teams actually adopt: cadences, trackers, templates and governance.
Comfort with budgets: reading allocations, tracking variance and working with Finance partners.
Experience coordinating across time zones and with international or partner studios. Mandarin is a plus, not a requirement.
Strong written communication; you can turn ambiguity into a one-page plan.
Fluency with Confluence, Jira and Airtable (or similar), and curiosity about using AI tools in your workflow.
A player's understanding of Apex Legends or competitive shooters.

Provides field service technical support to all field service locations and staff as requested

Overview

safely and thoughtfully. With deep expertise and innovative waste management technology across a growing nationwide footprint, Arcwood protects people, communities, and the environment through work that often happens behind the scenes.

Our Values

We Move Forward Together, One Team With a Shared Purpose, Counting On Each Other Every Day. Our Core Values Demonstrate How We Work Together To Deliver Value For Our Customers, Putting Them At The Center Of All We Do

Lead with Safety: We uphold the highest safety and compliance standards to protect our teams, our customers and the communities that count on us.
Solve Problems Creatively: We push for better – advancing technologies, processes, and ideas that protect human health and the environment.

jobs.description:
About Northern Trust

As a global leader in innovative wealth management, asset servicing, asset management and banking services, Northern Trust (Nasdaq: NTRS) is proud to guide the world’s most successful individuals, families, corporations and institutions.

Since 1889, we have aligned our efforts with our three guiding Principles That Endure: Service, Expertise, and Integrity. Together, they reflect the three cornerstones of business conduct which we strive to instill in our employees, whom we call partners, and to provide to our clients and the communities we serve worldwide.

With more than 135 years of financial experience and over 24,000 partners, we serve the world’s most sophisticated clients using leading technology and exceptional service.

About The Role

The Regulatory Program Manager role will lead enterprise deliveries encompassing financial and non-financial risk regulations, and provide continuity across various programs and projects necessary to manage effective regulatory change across a global organization and ensure that it is operationally embedded for continued compliance.

The ideal candidate will have a track record of supporting complex change programs, particularly in the compliance space and have a well-practiced understanding of regulatory frameworks, working with diverse, cross-functional teams and facilitating reporting needs from stakeholders across the organization.

The Key Responsibilities Of The Role Include

Leading the execution of identified regulatory change deliveries
Collaborating with stakeholders across all lines of defense, multiple business units and operational leaders to quickly identify and create effective and sustainable solutions for managing regulatory risk
Leading Working Group meetings to support transformation and maintaining efficient and appropriate governance to enable successful outcomes
Maintaining program data and business intelligence solutions to support successful execution of complex, cross-enterprise change projects.
Maintaining business intelligence solutions to communicate program objectives; risks; issues and overall status to multiple levels of the organization.
Managing deliverables with a forward-looking mindset, i.e., proactively anticipating any potential issues, prevent them and/or define pragmatic contingency plans, with timely escalations as needed
Proactively managing dependencies, ‘reusable assets’ (components of a solution that have been built elsewhere already), roadblocks and learning points (i.e., milestones defined to provide clarity and direction)
Developing and controlling deadlines, budgets and activities pertaining to the supported projects
Leveraging and contributing to best practice in change management and execution of complex cross-enterprise deliveries
Translating and operationalizing project/program requirements and source system data into appropriate solutions
Effectively communicate with developers, data architects and infrastructure resources to ensure there is a clear and concise understanding of requirements and acceptance criteria

Skills / Experience Required

Deep understanding of project management and portfolio management tools, techniques and methods (i.e., what good looks like), change management principles and how to build and deliver high-performing teams
Experience in the financial services industry with an understanding of regulatory obligations, compliance and risk management within asset servicing, wealth management and banking, and the regulatory environment in which they operate
Knowledge of and experience in agile ways of working is an asset
Great skills across communication, facilitation, interpersonal, conflict resolution, team building, coaching members on practices, framework, ability to teach/train etc.
Ability to establish trust-based relationships with stakeholders across enterprise, lead them towards common objectives and managing upwards and downwards (e.g., experience acting as a constructive conduit between business and non-business teams)
Flexibility and adaptability to change
Strong problem-solving skills, organizational skills and time management skills
Openness to self-learning, improvement and innovation
Several years serving as a program manager or other relevant role

Applicants must have the right to work in Ireland at the time of application and for the duration of employment.

Please note that Northern Trust is unable to provide employment permit sponsorship for this role. This includes Critical Skills Employment Permits, General Employment Permits, Intra-Company Transfer Employment Permits, Stamp 1G permissions, and other employment permits under Irish immigration frameworks.

As a Northern Trust partner, you will be part of a flexible and collaborative work culture, which has a strong history of financial strength and stability. Philanthropy is deeply rooted in Northern Trust’s history and is an essential element of our culture. Employees around the world give their time and talent to work for the greater good of their communities.

About the Role:

The Business Intelligence manager leads workforce management, capacity planning, operational analytics, and business intelligence for Customer Service Operations. Owns the integrated demand, capacity, and staffing-planning process; translates forecasts and operating performance into actionable workforce, budget, and service-level recommendations. Leads the reporting and analytics roadmap, establishes trusted metrics and data governance, and partners across Operations, Finance, Technology, Product, and Data & Analytics to improve customer experience, efficiency, and business outcomes.

Responsibilities:

Lead, coach, and develop a team of workforce management and reporting analysts; set priorities, build capabilities, and ensure reliable delivery of workforce insights and enterprise reporting.
Own the end-to-end capacity-planning process for multi-channel service operations, including volume and workload forecasting, staffing and scheduling models, shrinkage and occupancy assumptions, hiring and attrition plans, budget scenarios, and short- and long-range capacity plans.
Establish forecast-accuracy and capacity-plan performance measures; identify demand, staffing, service-level, and cost risks; and present tradeoffs and recommendations to Operations and Finance leaders.
Develop and execute the workforce management roadmap, aligning investments, processes, and technology enhancements to customer experience, service-level, efficiency, and ROI targets.
Oversee contact center analytics, service-level management, productivity reporting, and operating-performance reviews, translating findings into prioritized improvement actions.
Establish and govern operational metrics, KPI definitions, report standards, and data-quality controls across workforce, customer experience, and revenue-supporting analytics.
Own the analytics and reporting roadmap; prioritize the backlog across stakeholders and development teams, balance strategic initiatives with recurring reporting, and communicate delivery commitments.
Develop executive dashboards, scorecards, and performance narratives that clearly communicate outcomes, risks, trends, and recommended actions.
Lead data-governance practices for reporting, including business definitions, reporting logic, documentation, validation, and appropriate data access.
Partner with Operations, Technology, Data & Analytics, Product, and Finance to integrate data sources, improve processes, and enable data-informed decisions.
Provide functional oversight for Genesys Cloud, Salesforce routing, and workforce-management capabilities; define requirements, govern changes, and coordinate administration, testing, upgrades, and releases with technology partners.
Assess AI, automation, and digital experience use cases; establish measures for adoption and realized value; and ensure initiatives address operational needs and appropriate controls.

Key Outcomes:

Operational Planning - accurate, timely capacity plans that surface staffing, budget, and service tradeoffs; improved forecast accuracy, schedule efficiency, and service-level attainment.
Analytics and Governance - trusted metrics, usable dashboards, documented reporting logic, and prioritized insights that improve operating decisions and demonstrate value realization.

Core Competencies:

Capacity and worforce strategy
Operational analytics and BI
Data governance and quality
Executive storytelling
Cross-functional influence
People leadership

Skills
Required:

Analytics and Governance - trusted metrics, usable dashboards, documented reporting logic, and prioritized insights that improve operating decisions and demonstrate value realization.
Bachelor’s degree in business, analytics, information systems, finance, statistics, mathematics, operations management, or a related field; equivalent relevant experience considered.
Seven or more years of progressive experience in high-volume, multi-channel contact-center operations and workforce management, including forecasting, capacity planning, scheduling, shrinkage, adherence, and service-level management.
Three or more years leading workforce management, analytics, operational reporting, or business intelligence teams.
Demonstrated experience using forecasts and capacity models to make staffing, budget, hiring, and service-level recommendations.
Strong executive communication, stakeholder-management, analytical problem-solving, and data-visualization skills.
Advanced SQL, dashboard development, data analysis, and data-governance skills.

Preferred

Experience with Genesys Cloud and its workforce-management, routing, reporting, and IVR capabilities, or comparable tools such as NICE, Verint, IEX, or Five9.
Experience with Power BI, Tableau, Salesforce case management and routing workflows, AI/automation measurement, and digital-experience analytics.
Advanced degree or relevant certification in workforce management, COPC, CCXP, Lean/Six Sigma, PMP, or a related discipline.

jobs.title: Cyber Threat Intelligence Analyst, Senior
jobs.description:
Job Number: R0253565

Cyber Threat Intelligence Analyst, Senior

The Opportunity:

We are seeking an experienced Cyber Threat Intelligence Analyst to join our Security Operations Center (SOC) team. This role supports analysis and research on latest advanced cyber threats to provide actionable threat intelligence, including adversary indicators of compromise (IOCs), tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs), behaviors, and trends to help defend the client agency. The analyst will conduct analysis to profile threat actor TTPs used to infiltrate networks, systems, and assets to produce threat actor cards, profiles, or threat briefs. You’ll report on current and emerging threats that will exploit vulnerabilities and details of the vulnerabilities to stakeholders.

Cyber threats are evolving. Booz Allen is committed to creating an environment where you not only keep pace with the industry, but propel it forward. With access to academic programs, certifications, and opportunities to use expert tradecraft, we’ll continuously invest in you so you can create the career you want as you grow.

What You’ll Work On:

Collect, analyze, and correlate cyber threat intelligence from open-source, commercial, and government sources.
Monitor open-source intelligence, industry reports, and internal security logs to gather threat information, then synthesize and disseminate critical insights to relevant stakeholders.
Conduct tactical, operational, and strategic threat analysis in support of ongoing monitoring and investigations, identify patterns, and attribute attacks to specific actors.
Track threat actors, phishing campaigns, malware, and TTPs relevant to the agency’s mission and technology footprint.
Produce actionable reports, briefings, and IOCs for internal stakeholders.
Support the development of new detection rules and analytics based on evolving threats.

Join us. The world can’t wait.

You Have: 

10+ years of experience in cybersecurity threat intelligence, intelligence analysis, or threat analysis
Experience as a cyber threat analyst, collaborating with multiple internal and external stakeholders to gather data and intelligence, analyze, vet, and enrich the intelligence, create joint reports, and share with entities
Experience using intelligence platforms such as the MISP Threat Intelligence Platform
Experience with Confluence and Jira
Experience with ticketing systems such as ServiceNow
Experience with CNE and CNA tools and tradecraft along with signatures and TTPs associated with the preparation for, and execution or implementation of, such attacks
Knowledge of cyber threats, open-source research, nation state actors, and vulnerabilities and cyber attacks
Ability to prioritize and juggle multiple events or initiatives simultaneously
Top Secret clearance
Bachelor’s degree

Nice If You Have: 

Experience working in a SOC or cyber operations environment
Experience working with Splunk, including writing or comprehending queries and evaluating telemetry logs
Knowledge of current and emerging cyber adversaries and their TTPs
Knowledge of threat modeling and adversary tactics and techniques frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK matrices, Cyber Kill Chain, STRIDE, and PASTA
Ability to write or deliver succinct briefings, presentations, and reports to convey analysis, threat trends, threat actor profiles, indicator bulletins, vulnerability details, and defensive strategies to varied audiences
CISSP, GCTI, GCIA, GCIH, CEH, CTIA, or similar Certification

Clearance:

Applicants selected will be subject to a security investigation and may need to meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information; Top Secret clearance is required.

Compensation

At Booz Allen, we celebrate your contributions, provide you with opportunities and choices, and support your total well-being. Our offerings include health, life, disability, financial, and retirement benefits, as well as paid leave, professional development, tuition assistance, work-life programs, and dependent care. Our recognition awards program acknowledges employees for exceptional performance and superior demonstration of our values. Full-time and part-time employees working at least 20 hours a week on a regular basis are eligible to participate in Booz Allen’s benefit programs. Individuals that do not meet the threshold are only eligible for select offerings, not inclusive of health benefits. We encourage you to learn more about our total benefits by visiting the Resource page on our Careers site and reviewing Our Employee Benefits page.

Salary at Booz Allen is determined by various factors, including but not limited to location, the individual’s particular combination of education, knowledge, skills, competencies, and experience, as well as contract-specific affordability and organizational requirements. The projected compensation range for this position is $86,800.00 to $198,000.00 (annualized USD). The estimate displayed represents the typical salary range for this position and is just one component of Booz Allen’s total compensation package for employees. This posting will close within 90 days from the Posting Date.

Identity Statement

As part of the hiring process, we will ask you to complete an identity verification process that leverages advanced biometrics and artificial intelligence to ensure authenticity and protect against identity fraud. You are expected to be on camera during interviews and assessments. We reserve the right to take your picture to verify your identity and prevent fraud.

Candidate AI Usage Policy

AI is a part of our daily work at Booz Allen, and we are committed to the responsible and ethical use of AI tools. However, we want to ensure a fair candidate process based on your
own skills and knowledge. As part of this commitment, the use of artificial intelligence (AI) or other tools to assist with responses during interviews (whether in-person or virtual) is prohibited unless permission is explicitly provided
.

Work Model

Our people-first culture prioritizes the benefits of collaboration. To support engagement and effective communication, employees working virtually are generally expected to have their cameras on during meetings.

Remote: If this position is listed as remote, there may still be occasions when you are required to work in person at a Booz Allen or customer facility.
Hybrid: If this position is listed as hybrid, you will be expected to work from a Booz Allen or customer facility, in alignment with your leadership's expectations and the needs of the role.
Onsite: If this position is listed as onsite, work will primarily be performed full-time at a customer facility, where employees will collaborate directly with colleagues and customers as required by the role.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to disability, status as a protected veteran or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, local, or international law.

jobs.description:
At Moody's, we unite the brightest minds to turn today’s risks into tomorrow’s opportunities. We do this by striving to create an inclusive environment where everyone feels welcome to be who they are—with the freedom to exchange ideas, think innovatively, and listen to each other and customers in meaningful ways. Moody’s is transforming how the world sees risk. As a global leader in ratings and integrated risk assessment, we’re advancing AI to move from insight to action—enabling intelligence that not only understands complexity but responds to it. We decode risk to unlock opportunity, helping our clients navigate uncertainty with clarity, speed, and confidence.

If you are excited about this opportunity but do not meet every single requirement, please apply! You still may be a great fit for this role or other open roles. We are seeking candidates who model our values: invest in every relationship, lead with curiosity, champion diverse perspectives, turn inputs into actions, and uphold trust through integrity.

Skills And Competencies

1–2 years of experience in communications, market or media intelligence, research and analysis, or a related analytical discipline; internships count
Strong attention to detail and comfort with repetitive data-quality work; solid understanding of data quality principles, documentation standards, validation procedures, and control-minded analysis to deliver reliable dashboards, reports, and analytical outputs
Proficient in structured data analysis using SQL and/or Python. Hands-on experience with BI and reporting tools such as Tableau or Power BI, combined with advanced Microsoft Excel skills; familiarity with media monitoring platforms such as Meltwater is a plus
Experience supporting data extraction, preparation, transformation, validation, and analysis across multiple data sources; exposure to data pipelines, ETL processes, or workflow automation is preferred
Effective written and verbal communication skills with the ability to present findings, explain data issues, provide actionable recommendations, synthesize information for senior audiences, and translate technical concepts into clear business language
Ability to independently execute assigned work, apply established standards, and deliver accurate, high-quality, and timely results while exercising sound judgment and escalating issues as appropriate
Calm under pressure with strong time-management skills; comfortable managing multiple priorities and deadlines and collaborating with global stakeholders across time zones
Basic understanding of artificial intelligence concepts, with curiosity and enthusiasm for learning how AI tools can be used to improve processes and drive efficiency. Interest in exploring AI systems and a willingness to develop awareness of responsible AI practices, including risk management and ethical use

Education

Undergraduate degree in communications, journalism, business, data and analytics, or a related discipline

Responsibilities

Support data collection, accuracy, and quality validation across Meltwater, NewsEdge, and other monitoring sources
Provide hands-on data collection, cleaning, and validation capacity that underpins the Communications Intelligence function, sustaining the team's recurring intelligence deliverables while building toward a broader communications-intelligence and AI-enabled skillset over time
Support daily production of Moody's news briefs across Global, Private Credit, Corporates and Government, and Artificial Intelligence streams, including distribution management
Assist with the production of initial reports and dashboard inputs ahead of senior review; contribute data and formatting inputs to monthly leadership reporting
Monitor for reputational-risk and high-impact developments against thresholds set by the Communications Intelligence team, escalating promptly per team protocol.Provide cross-time-zone coverage for time-sensitive deliverables, including occasional out-of-hours coverage
Assist in the technical development and maintenance of upcoming and existing projects within Corporate Affairs; contribute to Power BI dashboard build and maintenance including regional and thematic realignment
Gain hands-on exposure to the team's GEO and AEO tools, supporting prompt curation, output analysis, and content-optimization recommendations under the Manager's direction
With demonstrated capability, take on a defined slice of independent reporting or tool ownership, to be scoped jointly with the Manager. Experiment with AI tools and lightweight automations to improve team workflows, bringing practical ideas forward for review rather than independently deploying new tools

About The Team

The Communications and Data Intelligence Analyst sits within the Content Strategy and Communications Intelligence team, part of Corporate Affairs and Moody's Shared Services — the branch of Moody's responsible for providing professional services that support the success of our global Moody's Ratings and Moody's Analytics businesses. The team serves as the audience-and-signal engine for Corporate Affairs, translating media coverage, audience behavior, and content performance data into insight that shapes editorial, messaging, and distribution strategy — and is increasingly a builder of its own AI-enabled tools. By joining the team, you will contribute to work that directly informs how Moody's communicates its voice, manages its reputation, and leads with intelligence across global markets.

jobs.description:
Job Title: Data and Business Intelligence Analyst

Who We Are

Cahill Contractors is a majority family- and woman-owned general contractor that specializes in the construction of multi-family residential, education, hospitality, and other commercial projects. With offices in San Francisco, Oakland, and San Jose, Cahill works throughout the San Francisco Bay Area. Now in its fourth generation of family leadership, Cahill has been building lasting relationships and quality structures with integrity since 1911. Cahill serves as a trusted partner to our clients, committed to their success from early in preconstruction through construction and beyond. Our employees take tremendous pride in their work and are consistently guided by Cahill’s five core values: Safety, Integrity, Commitment, Collaboration, and Continuous Improvement. Cahill is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

Position Summary

The Data & BI Analyst is responsible for keeping Cahill’s data accurate, organized, and usable, and for building the queries, reports, and Power BI dashboards that sit on top of it. This individual maintains the tables, pipelines, and integrations that feed our data warehouse, checks that the numbers match the systems they came from, and turns that data into reporting our project, preconstruction, and accounting teams can trust.

This is an early-career role with room to grow. It works alongside our Operations Team and uses AI tools every day to work faster and smarter. The ideal candidate is detail-oriented, curious about how our systems store information, and comfortable explaining technical work to non-technical teammates.

Responsibilities Include

Data Warehouse & Infrastructure

Maintain Cahill’s data warehouse utilizing the Kroo (or similar) connectors, ensuring data integrity, security, and accessibility.
Establish and enforce data governance standards, including naming conventions, documentation, and access controls.
Monitor data warehouse performance and optimize queries, storage, and infrastructure for reliability and speed.
Aggregate additional data sources into a data lake through Fabric (or similar).

Process Improvement & Innovation

Work cross-departmentally with Operations, Preconstruction, Field, Safety, Quality Control, and Accounting teams to identify process bottlenecks and opportunities where AI and automation could streamline workflows.
Document and share lessons learned, success stories, and measurable impact of implemented solutions.

Dashboards & Reporting

Design and build interactive dashboards using Power BI (or similar tools) to provide real-time insights into project performance, financial metrics, scheduling, safety, and other key business indicators.
Partner with stakeholders to define KPIs and reporting requirements that drive informed decision-making.
Maintain and enhance existing reports and dashboards as business needs evolve.

AI Agents & Automation

Design and deploy internal AI agents and automation tools to streamline repetitive tasks and improve operational efficiency across departments.
Develop custom AI solutions (e.g., document analysis, predictive analytics, natural language interfaces) tailored to Cahill’s construction workflows.
Integrate AI tools with existing platforms such as project management software, scheduling tools, and communication systems.
Continuously iterate on deployed solutions based on user feedback and evolving business needs.

AI Software Evaluation & Strategy

Research, evaluate, and recommend third-party AI software and platforms for potential adoption across the organization.
Stay current with emerging AI technologies, industry trends, and best practices relevant to the construction sector.
Assist with the development and maintenance of an AI roadmap aligned with Cahill’s strategic goals and Continuous Improvement initiatives.

Training & Support

Provide hands-on training and ongoing support to all departments and employees on the effective use of AI tools and data resources.
Develop training materials, guides, and best-practice documentation tailored to varying levels of technical proficiency.
Serve as one of the go-to resource for AI-related questions, troubleshooting, and adoption support across the company.
Champion a data-literate culture by promoting awareness of how data and AI can enhance day-to-day work.

Desired Skills And Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Data Analytics, Information Systems, Computer Science, Business, Mathematics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
1–3 years of relevant experience, including internships, coursework, or comparable hands-on work.
Working knowledge of SQL and relational databases (joins, filtering, aggregation, basic data validation).
Experience building reports or dashboards in Power BI, Tableau, or a comparable tool, including data modeling, DAX, publishing, and refresh management. Crystal Reports a plus.
Familiarity with Microsoft data tools (Fabric, Azure) preferred.
Experience with construction, accounting, ERP, scheduling, or field operations data (e.g., Viewpoint Vista, Procore, Primavera) helpful.
Quick learner and adaptable problem-solver with strong interpersonal skills, able to work cross-functionally, juggle multiple priorities, and handle confidential information with discretion.

Physical Requirements

The physical requirements described herein are representative of those that must be met by the employee, with or without reasonable accommodation, to perform the essential functions of this job successfully. While performing the duties of this job, the employee occasionally works in an office or hybrid setting. The employee is required to work in compliance with company safety policies, procedures, and applicable laws. This position will be regularly required to:

Repetitively use hand motions for keyboard use and physical use of vision to read computer monitors and paper documents.
Regularly use hands to operate standard office equipment (personal computer, phone, printer, etc.)
See with close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and have the ability to adjust focus.
Sit at a desk for prolonged periods of time working on a computer.
Talk and hear at normal levels. The noise level in the office work environment is usually low to moderate.
Must be able to lift up to 15 pounds at times, and up to 30 pounds occasionally.

What Can Cahill Offer You?

Employment - This is a full-time position located in downtown San Francisco. This role is hybrid, with a minimum of 3 days in the office. In addition to a competitive salary, we offer an annual discretionary performance-based bonus.
Healthcare Benefits - We provide coverage options with a PPO plan, an HMO plan, including Kaiser. Cahill covers 100% of monthly premiums for employee medical/dental/vision coverage for HMO and PPO plans. Multiple options are available for spouse/partner and family coverage. Additionally, we offer a Medical FSA option.
Retirement - Our 401(k) plan includes significant employer matching and an annual discretionary contribution. We also offer financial advisors to help you plan for your future.
Time Off - We understand the importance of balancing work and personal life. Our flexible PTO package allows you to recharge and take care of life's demands. The position starts with 5 days of PTO already earned and will accrue 3 additional weeks of PTO in the first year.
Volunteer Time Off - We provide paid time-off for volunteering, so our team members can make a meaningful impact to the communities we serve.
Wellness Program Cahill's Wellness Program supports physical, mental, financial, and community well-being with an annual wellness stipend, plus free resources and training.

The base annual salary for this exempt role is targeted between $100,000 - $120,000.

Job Description

About Aberdeen

Aberdeen Group plc is one of Europe’s largest investment companies, and we are built on a long-standing culture of caring about the future and making a positive impact. Together we invest for a better future. We do it to make a difference to the lives of our clients and customers, our employees, society, and our shareholders. Our business is structured around three distinct areas focused on our clients' changing needs: Aberdeen Investments, Aberdeen Adviser, and interactive investor.

As a Data Analyst within Aberdeen Adviser, you will help turn data into meaningful insight and support our ambition to invest in our clients’ futures while investing in your tomorrow.

About The Department

The Data & Analytics team supports Aberdeen Adviser by delivering insight that improves decision-making, operational performance and customer outcomes. Working closely with business stakeholders, the team combines data, analytics, reporting and emerging technologies to help colleagues make informed decisions and enable our clients to be better investors. The culture is collaborative, curious and focused on continuous improvement.

About The Role

As a Data Analyst reporting to the Lead Analyst, you will support the delivery of analytics, reporting and data models that inform strategic and operational decisions. You will work across analytical projects, develop actionable insight and build trusted relationships with stakeholders across the organisation. This is an excellent opportunity to grow your technical capability in Power BI, SQL, Python, Microsoft Fabric and AI-enabled analytics while contributing to a data-driven culture. Based in Edinburgh on a permanent basis, the role offers the chance to make a visible impact while investing in your tomorrow.

Key Responsibilities

Support the design and delivery of analytical projects, ensuring outputs are robust, scalable and aligned to business priorities.
Develop and maintain Power BI reporting, data models and insight solutions that drive business action.
Use DAX, SQL, Python and AI-enabled approaches to analyse data and generate meaningful insight.
Translate analytical findings into clear narratives and visualisations for technical and non-technical audiences.
Contribute to data governance, documentation, reusable data assets and CI/CD ways of working.
Build strong stakeholder relationships and collaborate across the team to share knowledge and best practice.

About The Candidate - Essential Skills

Experience developing reports and data models using Power BI.
Proficiency in at least one of DAX, M Code, SQL or Python to solve business problems.
Familiarity with Microsoft Fabric, cloud-based data platforms and source control concepts.
Experience using AI to support analytics or technology deliverables.
Understanding of data architecture, data modelling and governance principles.

Desirable skills

Strong communication skills, stakeholder engagement capability and a desire to learn and improve continuously.
Previous experience with user experience/user journey design
Exposure to CI/CD - Redeployment pipelines

We are proud to be a Disability Confident Committed employer. If you have a disability and would like to apply to one of our UK roles under the Disability Confident Scheme, please notify us by completing the relevant section in our candidate questionnaire. One of our team will reach out to support you through your application process.

We want you to be the real you throughout our recruitment process. Sharing your diversity information helps us understand the reach and impact of our hiring practices, and build a workplace where all people can thrive and belong.

This information is kept separate from your application and is not visible to recruiters, hiring managers, or assessors at any stage.

Our Benefits

There's more to working life than coming home with a good salary. We have an environment where you can learn, get involved and be supported.

When you join us, your reward will be one of the best around. This includes 40 days’ annual leave, a 16% employer pension contribution, a discretionary performance-based bonus (where applicable), private healthcare and a range of flexible benefits – including gym discounts, season ticket loans and access to an employee discount portal. You can read more about our benefits here.

Our business

Enabling our clients to be better investors drives everything we do. Our business is structured around three distinct areas – our vectors of growth – focused on our clients’ changing needs. You can find out more about what we do here.

An inclusive way of working

jobs.title: PRINCIPAL CYBER SECURITY ANALYST
jobs.description:
Position Summary Description

The Principal Cyber Analyst will be a key leader in our cybersecurity team, responsible for enhancing the organization’s security posture and providing expert guidance on complex cyber threats and vulnerabilities. This role requires a deep understanding of cybersecurity principles, advanced analytics, and incident response methodologies. The Principal Cyber Analyst will spearhead initiatives to proactively identify risks, develop mitigation strategies, and ensuring compliance with North American Electric Reliability Corporation Critical Infrastructure Protection (NERC CIP) standards as well as adherence to National Institute of Standards and Technology Cybersecurity Framework (NIST CSF).

Qualifications and Education Requirements

Bachelor of Science degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Cybersecurity, or a related field is required, with a master's degree preferred. Candidate must have a minimum of fifteen (15) years of experience in cybersecurity, focusing on threat analysis and incident response. Relevant cybersecurity certifications (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CEH, GCIH) are highly desirable. Extensive knowledge of cybersecurity frameworks, best practices, and regulatory requirements is essential. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills are necessary, along with the ability to work under pressure and manage multiple priorities. Excellent communication and presentation skills are required, with the capability to conveying technical information to non-technical stakeholders. Experience with security tools and technologies, such as SIEM, IDS/IPS, firewalls, endpoint protection, and vulnerability management, is also required.

Core Competencies:  
Adaptable, Collaborative, Communicator, Critical-Thinking, Detail-Oriented, and Outcome-Driven

Technical Competencies/Skills:

Cybersecurity Frameworks (NIST CSF, ISO 27001, and NERC CIP)

Threat Intelligence and Analysis

Intrusion Detection

Incident Response Methodologies

Security Information and Event Management (SIEM)

Security Technologies

Ethical Hacking

Vulnerability Management

Network Security

Cloud Security

Regulatory Compliance

Risk Management

Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications

Soft Competencies/Skills:

Effective verbal/nonverbal, listening and written communications

Collaboration

Critical Thinking

Customer Service Oriented

Leadership and Mentorship

Managing Change

Essential Functions

Develop and implement comprehensive cybersecurity strategies and policies to protect organizational assets.

Assess and enhance the organization's security posture against emerging threats and vulnerabilities.

Conduct in-depth analysis of cyber threats, vulnerabilities, and exploits relevant to the organization.

Monitor and evaluate industry trends, attack vectors, and the tactics of cyber adversaries.

Lead incident response efforts, including the identification, containment, eradication, and recovery from cybersecurity incidents.

Conduct forensic analysis on compromised systems and provide actionable recommendations for remediation.

Perform risk assessments and security audits to identify gaps in security practices.

Work with business units to prioritize risks and develop mitigation strategies.

Collaborate with IT, compliance, and business units to ensure alignment of security programs with business objectives.

Train and mentor junior analysts and staff on cybersecurity best practices and tools.

Ensure compliance with relevant laws, regulations, and industry standards (e.g., NIST, ISO 27001, GDPR, NERC CIP).

Prepare and present reports to senior management and stakeholders on the effectiveness of security measures and risk levels.

Stay current on the latest cybersecurity technologies, trends, and methodologies to continuously improve the organization's security capabilities.

Participate in the development of security products and solutions to enhance security monitoring and detection capabilities.

Perform other duties as applicable to the position or as assigned.

NERC Compliance: 
Performs NERC Compliance Program roles if/as designated in Seminole's Standard Ownership Matrix (SOM) including ongoing evidence retention in "audit-ready" form. You should also be familiar with Seminole's Enterprise Internal Compliance Program (ENT-GCD-RGC-EP-054) to further your understanding of Seminole's compliance program and your duties and responsibilities in the SOM. 

Physical Requirements

Must be able to follow established protective measures including wearing required personal protective equipment (PPE). Must possess a valid driver’s license and acceptable Motor Vehicle Report.  

Working Conditions

Some travel and work outside of normal business hours. While working in certain areas of the plant there is the potential for exposure to hazards typical of an industrial working environment. Must be capable of working extra hours and/or weekends when necessary to complete a project on time. Must be available on a 24-hour basis in the event of a system malfunction that requires assistance.
