new_jobs.title: Principal Technical Program Manager, GTM Integration & Launch
new_jobs.description:
ClickHouse is powering the next generation of real-time analytics and AI infrastructure. We recently raised a $400M Series D at a $15B valuation, and we're growing fast: expanding our customer base, scaling our cloud business, and widening our product line through acquisitions and net-new Tier-1 launches into new product categories.

We're looking for a Principal Technical Program Manager, GTM Integration & Launch to own how those products get to market. An acquired product isn't sellable on day one, and neither is a Tier-1 launch: the pricing, packaging, quoting logic, approval rules, and controls have to be built and tested end-to-end, the acquired base has to be migrated onto ClickHouse paper, and the field has to know who to sell it to and how they get paid for it. This role owns getting there.

Reporting to the Sr. Director of Global Revenue Operations, you'll own the path to market across Product, Finance, Legal, Operations, Engineering, Enablement, and the acquired team: the commercial diligence, the requirements, the design decisions, the build, the testing, and go-live readiness. You'll also shape the GTM plan itself – who we sell to first, how reps are compensated, how the field is trained – and report monthly to leadership on how our emerging products are actually selling. Beyond any single launch, you'll turn integration into a repeatable playbook and build the tooling that makes the commercial system faster and more reliable. This is a senior individual contributor role on the critical path for every acquisition and every Tier-1 launch.

What You'll Be Doing

Own the integration path for acquired products. Bring an acquired offering onto the commercial system, reconcile its pricing and contract mechanics with how ClickHouse sells, and get it sellable through the same standard as an organic launch.
Shape GTM strategy for the products you're integrating. Help define the motion for newly acquired products (e.g., Langfuse) and net-new Tier-1 launches (e.g., Postgres): who we sell to first and why, how reps get paid for it, and how the field gets trained – partnering with Sales Leadership, Comp/Planning, and Enablement, and building the target account lists from usage signals and account intelligence.
Run commercial diligence and pre-close planning. Assess the target's pricing model, contract paper, billing stack, metering, and revenue recognition, and land at close with a sequenced integration plan rather than a blank page.
Own the commercial and operational design. Define the requirements and make the calls on pricing setup, quoting logic, discount and approval rules, and the controls that govern how the product gets sold, in partnership with Commercial leadership.
Own contract and customer migration. Map the acquired base's entitlements to ClickHouse SKUs, move customers onto ClickHouse paper at renewal, and protect revenue through the transition.
Own the program end-to-end. Hold the timeline, drive deliverables across Product, Finance, Legal, Operations, Engineering, and the acquired team, and synthesize the cross-functional work into a single readiness plan.
Test the end-to-end flow before launch. Run UAT on the quote-to-cash path, catch what breaks, and confirm the full flow works before go-live.
Own go-live readiness. Set the launch criteria with product marketing, run the go/no-go, and make the call on whether the flow is ready. Coordinate field activation with Enablement so the product lands when it ships.
Own monthly GTM reporting. Report wins, gaps, and what broke to leadership, and feed it back into the process so the next integration goes faster.
Build the playbook and the tooling. Turn each integration into a repeatable path, and find and fix what's manual, slow, or error-prone in the commercial system along the way.

What You Bring

10+ years in technical program management, revenue operations, product operations, or commercial systems, with a track record of owning launches end-to-end and building the systems behind them.
Direct experience building GTM strategy for a new or unproven product.
Experience with usage-based or consumption-based business models. You understand how metering, commits, and overages create dependencies across billing, contracts, revenue recognition, and the commercial system – and that a launch has to get all of them right together.
Strong working knowledge of the systems an integration depends on: Salesforce and CPQ, financial and billing systems, product rating, and telemetry. You can design quoting rules, approval logic, and automated controls across them.
Depth to own the design, not just the plan. You write the requirements, facilitate the design calls on quoting, approval, and control logic, and build parts of the solution yourself.
Sales compensation design experience, or direct partnership with Sales/Comp teams on incentive structures.
M&A or technology integration experience. Bringing an acquired product onto the commercial system runs the same path as an organic launch, and this role owns that work.
Cross-functional program management at the core. You hold a timeline, drive deliverables across teams, and synthesize across stakeholders. You measure readiness by whether the full flow works end-to-end.
Partnership with enablement teams to build training programs and measure them against outcome metrics.
Strong analytical skills, including SQL, to build target lists, measure pilot results, and report on launch effectiveness.
Strong written and verbal communication. Comfortable driving a cross-functional forum and presenting readiness status to senior stakeholders.
Bachelor's degree; quantitative or technical field preferred. MBA or equivalent experience a plus.

Perks

Flexible work environment - ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and remote-friendly. We currently operate in over 25 countries.
Healthcare - Employer contributions towards your healthcare.
Equity in the company - Every new eligible team member who joins our company receives equity.
Time off - Flexible time off in the US, generous entitlement in other countries.
A USD$500 Home office setup if you’re a remote employee.
Global Gatherings – We believe in the power of in-person connection and offer opportunities to engage with colleagues at company-wide offsites.

Culture - We All Shape It

As part of a rapidly scaling start-up, you will be instrumental in shaping our culture.

new_jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Extensibility Platform
new_jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About Our Organization

The Developer Experience & Product Platform (DEeP) organization empowers all of Stripe's products with a shared product platform that delivers high-quality, consistent, cross-product experiences across our UI and API surfaces. DEeP focuses on providing a scalable developer experience that any developer can leverage to accelerate a customer's ability to create value from Stripe.

Within DEeP, the Extensibility program is how Stripe expands its total addressable market, and increases customer retention. With extensibility, Stripe becomes programmable — customers and product teams can adapt Stripe to their needs on a common platform.

Stripe Has Three Interconnected Extensibility Primitives

Scripts — Secure, isolated TypeScript runtime allowing merchants and developers to customize Stripe product behavior (e.g., discount calculations, invoice logic, proration).

Custom Objects — User-defined data models (e.g., Shipments, Locations, Warranties, Entitlements) with first-class APIs, SDKs, and Dashboard experiences.

Workflows — A programmable orchestration layer (graduating to GA at Sessions) enabling no-code and pro-code business logic across Stripe, including custom actions, delays, smart retries, and 3P integrations.

These primitives are deeply interdependent, involve 10+ cross-functional teams and culminate in a flagship product launch.

What you’ll do

We are seeking a product-focused Technical Program Manager to drive the Extensibility program across the Workflows, Custom Objects, and Scripts workstreams. This is a newly created, high-impact role at the intersection of platform engineering, product management, and cross-organizational program ownership.

In this role, you will own one of the most strategically consequential programs in DEeP — driving the direction, health, and outcomes of Stripe's Extensibility platform across Scripts, Custom Objects, and Workflows. You will set the program strategy in partnership with DEeP leadership, holding organizations accountable to the success of the program.

Drive cross-org decisions across DRIs in Script Platform, Custom Objects, Apps, SDK, Observability, DevEx, and Versioning — actively resolving the hard, ambiguous integration and ownership questions that fall between team boundaries.
Own the critical path to major launches — proactively shaping scope, driving descope decisions, and negotiating trade-offs across teams so that launches reflect deliberate strategic choices.
Influence and shape product and engineering roadmaps — bringing a program-level perspective to team planning cycles, pushing back where individual team roadmaps are misaligned with broader extensibility strategy, and advocating for cross-cutting investments that no single team will prioritize on their own.
Support ProServ and Partnerships — Ensure ProServ and Partnerships requirements are surfaced into the roadmap with the same rigor as product requirements, and hold the bridge between what the platform delivers and what those teams need to close and serve complex customers.

Qualifications

Minimum requirements

5+ years of technical program management experience with demonstrated success in driving complex cross organizational programs.
Strong product sense and ability to understand enterprise customer needs
Demonstrated ability to communicate with precision and credibility across engineering, product, and executive audiences, translating complex technical trade-offs into strategic decisions, and driving alignment.
Demonstrated ability to lead and align cross-functional teams — driving decisions, resolving conflict, and building consensus across organizations with competing priorities
Proven track record of successful program delivery in complex technical environments
Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience

Preferred Qualifications

Background in product management or product operations
Experience with developer platforms, API products, or payment systems

Hybrid work at Stripe

This role is available either in an office or a remote location (35+ miles or 56+ km from a Stripe office).

In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This hits a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility about how to do this in a way that makes sense for individuals and their teams.

Working remotely at Stripe

A remote location is defined as being 35 miles (56 kilometers) or more from one of our offices. While you would be welcome to come into the office for team/business meetings, on-sites, meet-ups, and events, our expectation is you would regularly work from home rather than a Stripe office. Stripe does not cover the cost of relocating to a remote location. We encourage you to apply for roles that match the location where you currently live or plan to live.

Pay and benefits

The annual US base salary range for this role is $157,700 - $236,500. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.

We look forward to hearing from you.

At Stripe, we're looking for people with passion, grit, and integrity. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. Your skills and passion will stand out—and set you apart—especially if your career has taken some extraordinary twists and turns. At Stripe, we welcome diverse perspectives and people who think rigorously and aren't afraid to challenge assumptions. Join us.

Apply now

new_jobs.description:
University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus

Department: OBGYN

Job Title: GynOnc Research Program Manager

Position #: 00854512 – Requisition #:
41733

Job Summary:

The Gynecologic Oncology Division Research Program Manager is a full-time position within the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology at the University of Colorado School of Medicine. This role will be responsible for providing management and oversight for clinical trials in close partnership with the Division Chief, Division Administrator Director, and Division Faculty members. This position will be team lead and have direct oversight of the GynOnc Division’s Research Services Professional positions. In order to succeed in this position, this detail-oriented individual must be able to demonstrate superior organizational skills to successfully track multiple tasks occurring in parallel. This incumbent must be self-motivated to complete tasks quickly and within set deadlines. This position is the ‘hub’ of communication between external (review committee coordinators, review committee members, study monitors) and internal (clinical study staff, investigators, clinical managers) contacts, thus superior communication skills (oral and written) are required. The position may be utilized to support research at the main Anschutz Medical Campus as well as in Northern Colorado. The professional in this position will not be called on to make independent medical decisions at any time, but a solid fundamental knowledge of biological and medical sciences is necessary for this position. Additionally, appreciation of accepted methods of clinical research is highly desirable.

In addition to their team lead role, this position will be responsible for cross-training and providing coverage to clinical coordination duties including active patient recruiting and consenting, visit coordination, and study team compliance with regulatory documents (Delegation of Authority Log, Form 1572, Financial Disclosure forms, Site Qualification Documents). This position will be responsible for human subjects research regulatory compliance of study teams in the GynOnc Division and will interface with regulatory and financial bodies in conjunction with the contacts within the OBGYN Administrative Research Core (ARC) Team.

Key Responsibilities:

Personnel Management: 25%

Provide direct supervision to GynOnc research staff personnel in their day-to-day work and with matters including recruitment, hiring, onboarding, training and retention strategies.

Financial Management: 10%

Works with finance team members to review invoices for accuracy in work performed, resolve discrepancies, and to review outgoing invoices and account balances on a regular basis.
Manage expenses and allocate resources from all research funding sources including gifts, grants and contracts funds.

Team Lead Operational Duties & Responsibilities: 40%

Assists with identifying issues related to operational efficiency and shares results with leadership.
Assists clinical research staff with technical issues, problem solving and intervention when appropriate; delegates responsibility for elements of the conduct of selected clinical trials.
Serves as study team contact for ongoing and potential clinical research studies including multi-center studies and meets with representatives from sponsoring pharmaceutical firms or in-house staff for initial orientation to studies and for review of regulatory records.
Provides service coverage for RSP/CRC to complete day-to-day patient focused research activities when necessary.
Oversees the operational execution of clinical trials by ensuring protocol compliance, participant eligibility and enrollment, informed consent processes, study visit coordination, specimen management, safety reporting, and regulatory documentation.

Quality Assurance: 25%

Oversees data review, collection, and documentation of all research subject data pertaining to the research protocol onto protocol-specific Case Report Forms (CRFs) and into the Cancer Center clinical trials database in an accurate and timely fashion.
Obtains oncology grading levels for study product toxicities, including assessment of clinical significance of all lab and test results and relatedness of adverse reactions to study product according to protocol guidelines.
Meets with Monitors to respond to any question of data validity and corrects/revises data as appropriate; responds to queries from Sponsor.
Participates in external audits and internal process improvement strategies to promote consistent best practices.

Work Location:

Hybrid – this role is eligible for a hybrid schedule of 4 days per week on campus and as needed for in-person meetings.

Why Join Us:

The University of Colorado, Department of Obstetrics & Gynecology’s, Division of Gynecologic Oncology is a women's health oncology practice dedicated to treating, curing and providing support for reproductive cancers. As the only National Comprehensive Cancer Network in the rocky mountain region, CU's Gynecologic Oncology group provides patients with the highest level of expertise available delivered in compassionate and individualized care.

Why work for the University?

We have AMAZING benefits and offer exceptional amounts of holiday, vacation, and sick leave! The University of Colorado offers an excellent benefits package including:

Medical: Multiple plan options
Dental: Multiple plan options
Additional Insurance: Disability, Life, Vision
Retirement 401(a) Plan: Employer contributes 10% of your gross pay
Paid Time Off: Accruals over the year
Vacation Days: 22/year (maximum accrual 352 hours)
Sick Days: 15/year (unlimited maximum accrual)
Holiday Days: 15/year
Tuition Benefit: Employees have access to this benefit on all CU campuses
ECO Pass: Reduced rate RTD Bus and light rail service

There are many additional perks & programs with the CU Advantage.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in any field. Substitution: A combination of education and related technical/military/paraprofessional experience may be substituted for a bachelor’s degree on a year for year basis.
Four (4) years clinical research or related experience.

Applicants must meet minimum qualifications at the time of hire.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in science or health related field.
Master’s degree in public health, public administration, social/behavioral sciences, physical sciences, nursing, healthcare, finance, accounting, business administration, business, or a directly related field from an accredited institution.
Five (5) years clinical research or related experience.
Prior experience providing program and/or project management duties in a clinical research setting.
Experience with electronic data capture systems (e.g. EMR or EHR and data management systems).
One of the below certifications:
CCRC – Certified Clinical Research Coordinator
CCRP – Certified Clinical Research Professional
CCRA – Certified Clinical Research Associate

Bilingual, Spanish Fluency.
Prior training and/or experience in Cancer Research, specific to OBGYN.
Experience working at a large health care related organization, University or state agency.
Experience working in the local (Denver or Colorado) health care environment.
Experience with Phase I clinical research trials.
Experience serving as a primary coordinator for clinical trials.
Previous personnel management, supervisory experience, or successful completion of the CU SOM Management Certification Program.

Conditions of Employment:

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States without requiring sponsorship. We are unable to provide work visa sponsorship or employment authorization for this position now or in the future.

Competencies: Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities (KSAs)

Strong project management skills and experience within a complex and diverse environment.
Advanced knowledge and understanding of federal regulations and Good Clinical Practice (GCP).
Demonstration of strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Ability to communicate effectively, both in writing and orally.
Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with employees at all levels throughout the institution.
Outstanding customer service skills.
Knowledge of basic human anatomy, physiology, and medical terminology.
Ability to interpret and master complex research protocol information.
Organization, time management, and prioritization skills.
Outstanding leadership skills.
Advanced knowledge of GCP, FDA Rules and Regulations in relation to clinical trials, NIH guidelines, ICH guidelines and HIPAA regulations in relation to clinical trials, and NCI common toxicity definitions.
Understanding of the phases and concepts of clinical trials and the overall philosophies of conducting cooperative group research as they differ with National Cancer Institute (NCI) sponsored, private industry and investigator initiated clinical trials.

At AMD, we believe technology has the power to solve the world’s most important challenges. From advancing healthcare and scientific discovery to powering AI and the technologies people rely on every day, innovation at AMD is shaping the future.

The Role

AMD's Global Sales Strategy & Planning organization is seeking a highly motivated and execution-focused Senior Manager, Cloud Partner Program Manager
to lead the implementation and operational readiness of the AMD Partner Network (APN) Cloud Program.

This highly visible role will serve as the operational leader and program management lead, translating the approved program strategy into a scalable, governed, and partner-ready operating model. The opportunity combines enterprise program leadership, cloud and channel operations, financial governance, and cross-functional execution to support the continued growth of AMD's cloud partner ecosystem. Beyond the initial implementation, this position is expected to evolve into end-to-end operational leadership of AMD's Cloud Partner Program, providing continuity, governance, and accountability as the program scales throughout 2027 and beyond.

Working closely with Cloud Sales, the Cloud Business Unit, Finance, Legal, IT, Sales Operations, regional channel teams, and external platform providers, you will drive critical decisions, establish clear accountability, and coordinate implementation across the full partner lifecycle, from onboarding and certification through usage reporting, incentives, claims, and payments.

AECOM is seeking a senior remediation leader to oversee one of our largest environmental remediation portfolios supporting Oil & Gas clients across the western United States.

As the Remediation Program Manager,
you will serve as the senior delivery leader for a major Oil & Gas remediation program. You will be accountable for portfolio performance, resource planning, risk management, client satisfaction, and financial success, while coaching and developing the next generation of Program Managers.

new_jobs.description:
At NiCE, we don’t limit our challenges. We challenge our limits. Always. We’re ambitious. We’re game changers. And we play to win. We set the highest standards and execute beyond them. And if you’re like us, we can offer you the ultimate career opportunity that will light a fire within you.

So, what's the role all about?

The Senior Program Manager, Forward Deployed Engineering, partners with our Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) to turn customer proofs of concept (POCs) into delivered outcomes and clear product requirements. You are customer-facing: you run the engagement plan with the customer, keep scope and timelines honest, and make sure what the FDE learns on site reaches Product and Engineering in a form they can act on.

You will sit in the program function in Business Operations within NiCE's Engagement Orchestration product organization, working alongside the FDE, Customer Success, and account teams. The role is technical and communication-heavy: you will be in the room with customer executives and engineers one day, and with Product Owners and Engineering leads the next.

How will you make an impact?

Run customer POCs and engagements with the FDE: build the plan, scope, and timeline, set success criteria with the customer, and keep milestones, risks, and decisions visible.
Be a trusted, customer-facing point of contact: lead working sessions and status meetings, manage expectations, and communicate clearly with customer executives and technical teams.
Translate POC findings into product requirements: write problem statements, user stories, acceptance criteria, and success metrics that Product and Engineering can prioritize and build against.
Separate one-off from repeatable: identify patterns across customers and bring evidence to Product so productize, standardize, or stop decisions are made deliberately.
Partner with Product Owners and Engineering leads: take requirements through intake, track them in Jira, and report back to the customer and FDE on status.
Manage dependencies, risks, and escalations across the customer, FDE, Product, Engineering, Customer Success, and Support, and raise blockers early with the tradeoff stated.
Plan the hand-off: make sure each engagement ends with documentation, enablement, and a named owner on the customer side and on the product team.
Keep Jira, Salesforce, and Confluence current so customer commitments, requirements, and engagement status reconcile.
Coordinate with the cross-functional program team where a customer's issues also need a broader program, so customers see one coordinated response.
Improve the FDE operating model: build intake, scoping, and reporting templates, and track how many POCs convert to product decisions and roadmap items.

Have you got what it takes?

5-7+ years of program, project, or product management in a software or SaaS environment, with at least 3 years in customer-facing delivery, solutions, or professional services.
Comfort in technical environments: you can follow integrations, APIs, architecture, and defect discussions, ask good questions, and explain them to executives and non-technical stakeholders.
Exceptional written and verbal communication, including running customer meetings and writing requirements that engineers can build from.
Experience turning ambiguous customer needs into clear requirements, user stories, and acceptance criteria.
Proven ability to influence without direct authority across customers, engineering, and product teams.
Strong scoping, risk, and dependency management in time-boxed engagements, including the judgment to say no or to escalate early.
Hands-on experience with Jira, Confluence, and Salesforce for tracking, reporting, and documentation.
Working knowledge of Agile and Scrum and the software delivery lifecycle.
Commercial awareness and sound stakeholder management with customers, sales, and Customer Success.
Bachelor's degree in Business, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

Experience in CCaaS, CX, conversational AI, or agentic workflow products.
Background in forward deployed engineering, solutions engineering, sales engineering, or technical product management.
Experience converting bespoke customer work into scalable product capabilities.
Experience running POCs, pilots, or design partnerships with enterprise customers.
Comfort with data and analytics tools such as Power BI, SQL, or Tableau.
PMP, Agile, or similar certification.

Join an ever-growing, market disrupting, global company where the teams – comprised of the best of the best – work in a fast-paced, collaborative, and creative environment! As the market leader, every day at NICE is a chance to learn and grow, and there are endless internal career opportunities across multiple roles, disciplines, domains, and locations. As our Sr. Program Manager at Macmillan Learning, you'll drive the commercial success and educational impact of our Earth Systems portfolio—spanning earth science, environmental science, ecology, and botany—while leading our STEM-wide growth strategy for labs and authentic scientific practice. You'll own business strategy and P&L performance across your portfolio and partner with Go-to-Market, Product, Sales, Marketing, Implementation, and fellow STEM portfolio leads to build distinctive, scalable learning experiences across physical materials, digital simulations, inquiry, and experimentation. Reporting to the Executive Program Director, STEM, you'll strengthen our market position and help shape the future of undergraduate STEM education.

This role is built for someone who enjoys turning market intelligence, educator insights, and evolving scientific practices into actionable product and investment strategies. You'll bring strong commercial and analytical instincts alongside the relationship-building skills needed to engage authors, disciplinary leaders, and cross-functional partners across established and emerging STEM markets.

What You'll Do

Earth Systems Portfolio Strategy & P&L Ownership: You'll define and execute business strategy for earth science, environmental science, ecology, and botany in partnership with Go-to-Market teams, owning portfolio P&L performance and using financial, competitive, and TAM/SAM/SOM market intelligence to achieve commercial goals.
STEM-Wide Labs & Authentic Scientific Practice Strategy: You'll own the cross-STEM growth strategy for labs and authentic scientific practice across all disciplines and delivery models—spanning physical materials, digital simulation, inquiry, experimentation, and emerging approaches—in coordination with other STEM portfolio leads.
Growth Development & Investment Prioritization: You'll evaluate opportunities across disciplines and institutional segments, assess right to play and right to win, and build data-informed business cases to secure investment for new initiatives, products, and learning experiences.
Market & Disciplinary Intelligence: You'll track academic disciplines, instructional innovations, laboratory and field teaching practices, and emerging competitors, combining external signals with internal insights to identify market gaps and guide product direction.
External Engagement & STEM Leadership: You'll cultivate a diverse network of thought leaders, innovators, and change agents, convening conversations and positioning Macmillan Learning as a destination of choice for influential partners and promising proposals.
Author & Collaborator Partnerships: You'll engage current authors in evolving digital and portfolio strategies—aligning textbook updates and revisions with broader product directions—while building relationships with collaborators and content creators.
Cross-Functional Execution: You'll align Product, Sales, Marketing, Implementation, and senior leadership around cohesive strategies, translating prioritized opportunities into actionable roadmaps with clear accountability for commercial and educational outcomes.

What You Bring To The Team

Experience commensurate with a senior-level position in educational publishing, learning product or program management, curriculum strategy, or a related commercial and content leadership role.
A conferred bachelor's degree in a STEM discipline.
Strong knowledge of undergraduate laboratory and field instruction, including how students develop and apply authentic scientific skills.
Proven financial and commercial acumen, including experience owning portfolio P&L performance, conducting market opportunity assessments (TAM/SAM/SOM), and building data-informed business cases for investment.
Strategic thinking and sound judgment in ambiguous environments, with the ability to weigh incomplete market evidence, evaluate right to play/right to win, and prioritize which opportunities to pursue, test, defer, or stop.
Demonstrated ability to build strategic external networks with educators, authors, and disciplinary leaders, translating varied institutional and instructor perspectives into inclusive, customer-centered solutions.
Exceptional communication and coalition-building skills, with experience aligning cross-functional partners and presenting complex market evidence and business recommendations to senior stakeholders.

new_jobs.title: Senior Program Manager, Cross-Functional Programs
new_jobs.description:
At NiCE, we don’t limit our challenges. We challenge our limits. Always. We’re ambitious. We’re game changers. And we play to win. We set the highest standards and execute beyond them. And if you’re like us, we can offer you the ultimate career opportunity that will light a fire within you.

So, what's the role all about?

The Senior Program Manager, within NiCE's Engagement Orchestration product organization, runs cross-functional programs that resolve critical customer and product issues spanning multiple engineering teams, and keeps leadership, Product, Engineering, Customer Success, and Support working from one accurate status. The role coordinates; product and engineering teams deliver and own the outcome.

You will sit in the program function in Business Operations, outside Product and R&D. You will lead one to three programs at a time, each a short, sprint-style effort with a named sponsor, a defined outcome, and a clear exit. You will also help run the program system itself: intake, triage, charter, cadence, and reporting.

This is a technical, high-visibility role. You will be in the room with Product Owners, Engineering leads, and executives, and you need to make complex cross-team problems simple to act on.

How will you make an impact?

Lead assigned customer escalation and cross-customer issue programs end to end: draft the charter with the sponsor and engineering leaders, run the three-week cycles, and drive each program to validated close or an agreed disposition.
Run weekly planning for each program, naming next week's work and the specific people needed, and sizing requests in hours of named people against each team's committed capacity.
Keep status accurate and visible: maintain one shared view of progress, risks, blockers, and decisions, and publish a weekly report for leadership, Product, and Customer Success.
Escalate early and cleanly. Raise blockers over 48 hours, bring declined requests to leadership with the tradeoff stated, and record the decision.
Work with engineering and product leaders and their team representatives to turn program requests into team commitments, and check delivery areas (documentation, UX, launch readiness, enablement) at exit.
Support intake and triage: assess nominations from escalation reports, the unified issue view, commitments reviews, and demand themes against entry criteria (red account, revenue at risk, aged P1/P2 defects, customer commitment at risk, or shared root cause).
Keep Jira, Salesforce, and Confluence clean and connected so commitments, defects, and customer cases reconcile at exit.
Coordinate with other lines of business where an issue spans them, running our workstream under one shared status.
Improve the program model: gather lessons from each cycle, tune thresholds and templates, and help evaluate the one-quarter pilot against its goals.

Have you got what it takes?

5-7+ years of program or project management in a software or SaaS environment, including cross-functional programs with Product and Engineering.
Comfort in technical environments: you can follow architecture, defect, and release discussions, ask good questions, and translate them for non-technical leaders.
Excellent written and verbal communication, with the ability to tailor the same update for engineers, Customer Success, and executives.
Proven ability to influence without direct authority and to lead through ambiguity across teams and organizations.
Strong risk, dependency, and escalation management, including the judgment to know when to escalate and the discipline to do it early.
Hands-on experience with Jira, Confluence, and Salesforce for tracking, reporting, and documentation.
Working knowledge of Agile and Scrum, and of the software delivery lifecycle: planning, defect triage, release readiness, and customer commitments.
Strong organization, attention to detail, and the ability to manage several time-boxed efforts at once under pressure.
Bachelor's degree in Business, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

You will have an advantage if:

Experience in CCaaS, CX, or AI product environments, or with enterprise customers on escalated accounts.
Background in Scrum Master, QA, release management, or engineering roles.
Experience building program frameworks such as intake, charters, status reporting, and governance.
Comfort with data and reporting tools such as Power BI, SQL, or Tableau.
PMP, Agile, or similar certification.
Experience using AI tools to speed up reporting, analysis, and documentation.

What’s in it for you?

Join an ever-growing, market disrupting, global company where the teams – comprised of the best of the best – work in a fast-paced, collaborative, and creative environment! As the market leader, every day at NICE is a chance to learn and grow, and there are endless internal career opportunities across multiple roles, disciplines, domains, and locations. If you are passionate, innovative, and excited to constantly raise the bar, you may just be our next NICEr!

Enjoy NICE-FLEX!

At NICE, we work according to the NICE-FLEX hybrid model, which enables maximum flexibility: 2 days working from the office and 3 days of remote work, each week. Naturally, office days focus on face-to-face meetings, where teamwork and collaborative thinking generate innovation, new ideas, and a vibrant, interactive atmosphere.

Requisition ID: 12004

Reporting into:
Senior Director, Product Operations

Role Type:
Individual Contributor

NICE Ltd. (NASDAQ: NICE) software products are used by 25,000+ global businesses, including 85 of the Fortune 100 corporations, to deliver extraordinary customer experiences, fight financial crime and ensure public safety. Every day, NiCE software manages more than 120 million customer interactions and monitors 3+ billion financial transactions.

Known as an innovation powerhouse that excels in AI, cloud and digital, NiCE is consistently recognized as the market leader in its domains, with over 8,500 employees across 30+ countries.

Drive team meetings and deliver timely and accurate meeting recaps and status.
Create a positive environment by working collaboratively, energizing others, and encouraging continuous improvement from project teams.

Change control
Cross-team leadership

Who we are

About Bridge

We're creating an entirely new payments platform, built with stablecoins, to simplify global money movement. Bridge enables faster, cheaper payments and borderless access to dollars via stablecoins. Through our APIs, businesses can send and receive funds across borders faster and cheaper vs. SWIFT and other fiat-only rails. Our virtual accounts enable international consumers and businesses to easily access, store, and spend US dollars. Our payouts infrastructure enables platforms to disburse USD to anyone globally. We believe many trillions of dollars will move and settle through stablecoin payment rails. Bridge is pulling this future forward.

We have a small team of people who have previously built financial infrastructure at some of the world's leading companies (Coinbase, Stripe, Square, Brex, Upstart, DoorDash, Airbnb), and each and every one of them chose Bridge because they fundamentally believe that stablecoins will be a critical piece of financial infrastructure that allows for the improvement of global money movement.

Collaborate cross-functionally with engineering, product, and Stripe’s security org to move fast without compromising safety.

We are seeking an experienced Security Manager to lead the governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) pillar of our Enterprise Cybersecurity program. This people-leadership role owns the cybersecurity governance operating rhythm, executive and board-level reporting, third-party security risk management, data security program management, security awareness, and cybersecurity policy and compliance activities. The Security Manager is accountable for the cadence, quality, and continuity of these programs — turning security metrics, risk data, and regulatory requirements into clear, actionable insight for leadership and the Board.

The ideal candidate combines strong program and people management with a solid understanding of security frameworks (such as NIST CSF and CMMC), risk management, and stakeholder engagement across IT, Legal, business units, and external partners. Responsibilities

Cybersecurity Governance & Reporting

Own the cybersecurity governance program, including the Monthly Cybersecurity Metrics Report and Quarterly Board Dashboard measures.
Define and maintain cybersecurity metrics, KPIs, and KRIs; track program maturity against the NIST CSF; and drive strategic initiatives, risks, and governance commitments to closure.
Coordinate identity governance activities, including monthly AD account reviews, access certifications, and IAM metrics reporting.
Coordinate cybersecurity inputs for the annual cyber insurance renewal and annual Incident Response Plan update and Management tabletop exercise.

Data Security Program Management

Lead data discovery and classification governance across IT, Legal, and business stakeholders, tracking data risk reduction and reporting progress through program metrics.

Third-Party & Supplier Cyber Risk Management

Manage the third-party cyber risk assessment program, including new third-party service reviews, periodic reassessments, critical-supplier (direct and indirect) assessments, and FBIN questionnaires.
Track and drive remediation of third-party and supplier risks and integrate cyber-risk data into governance reporting.

Cybersecurity Policies, Standards & Compliance

Maintain cybersecurity governance documentation, coordinating annual policy and standard updates, approvals, publication and archive.
Support compliance initiatives including SOX controls, CMMC readiness, NIST CSF maturity reporting, SOC 2 assurance, and audit evidence collection and manage governance repositories and control attestations.

Security Awareness Program

Administer the enterprise security awareness program, including annual training, new hire training, National Cybersecurity Awareness Month, quarterly phishing simulations and ad hoc awareness articles on the FBIN intranet.

Leadership & Continuous Improvement

Manage, mentor, and develop analysts supporting governance, risk, and awareness functions.
Partner with cross-functional teams: IT, Legal, connected product, and business units to embed security best practices and continuously improve the maturity, efficiency, and clarity of processes and reporting.

KEY COMPETENCIES

Collaborate: Build partnerships and work collaboratively with others to meet shared objectives.
Communicate Effectively: Develop and deliver multi-mode communications that convey a clear understanding of the unique needs of different audiences.
Instill Trust: Gain the confidence and trust of others through honesty, integrity, and authenticity.
Builds Effective Teams: Attract, develop, and retain talent to meet current and future organizational needs.
Drives Results: Consistently achieve results, even under challenging circumstances.
Decision Quality: Make sound and timely decisions that keep the organization moving forward.
Plans and Aligns: Plan and prioritize work to meet commitments aligned with organizational goals.
Ensures Accountability: Hold self and others accountable to meet commitments.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Information Security, Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
Minimum of 7+ years of overall technology experience, with at least 5+ years in an information security, cybersecurity, or GRC role.
Demonstrated experience owning cybersecurity governance, risk, or compliance programs and producing executive- or board-level reporting.
Working knowledge of security frameworks such as NIST CSF and CMMC, and of enterprise risk and third-party risk management practices.
Experience coordinating security awareness, data security, or identity governance programs across cross-functional stakeholders.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex security topics for technical and non-technical audiences, including leadership.
Strong analytical, organizational, and program-management skills.

Preferred

Relevant certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CRISC, CISA, or CompTIA Security+.
Experience with GRC and risk platforms and data security tooling.
Familiarity with SOC 2, cyber insurance renewal processes, and audit/assurance coordination.
Experience supporting incident response governance and tabletop exercises.

This position manages personnel security, facility security, physical security, classified contract compliance, COMSEC accountability, Technology Control Plan (TCP) administration, and security awareness initiatives while ensuring compliance with applicable government, customer, and contractual security requirements.
The Security Manager serves as the principal security advisor to management, supporting the protection of classified information, controlled technical information, company assets, personnel, and facilities. This role works closely with Operations, Engineering, Information Technology, Human Resources, and Program Management to maintain a strong security posture and ensure operational readiness.

DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES:
• Serve as the company's designated Facility Security Officer and administer the industrial security program in accordance with NISPOM, DCSA, and contractual security requirements.
• Develop, implement, and continuously improve security policies, procedures, and programs to ensure compliance with NISPOM, contractual requirements, customer directives, and company standards.
• Serve as the primary liaison with DCSA representatives, including ISRs and Industrial Security Integration (ISI) personnel, as well as government security officials, customers, auditors, and inspectors.
• Manage personnel security programs, including clearance processing, access authorizations, visit requests, security briefings, debriefings, training, recordkeeping, and related investigations.
• Administer facility security programs, including Facility Clearance (FCL) requirements, access control, visitor management, badging, physical security measures, and security inspections.
• Lead responses to security incidents, violations, emergencies, and corrective action initiatives.
• Oversee COMSEC accountability and ensure the proper handling, storage, transfer, inventory, destruction, and safeguarding of classified communications assets and materials.
• Develop, implement, and maintain Technology Control Plans (TCPs), including monitoring access to controlled information, systems, facilities, technical data, and restricted programs.
• Assist with the planning, design, construction, accreditation, and ongoing compliance of Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities (SCIFs).
• Conduct audits, inspections, and compliance reviews to assess adherence to security requirements and identify areas for improvement.
• Maintain security documentation and records required by government regulations, customer requirements, and company policies.
• Monitor regulatory, contractual, and security program changes and implement necessary updates to maintain compliance.
• Develop and deliver security awareness and compliance training programs and promote a culture of security throughout the organization.
• Advise leadership on security risks, regulatory requirements, mitigation strategies, and operational impacts.
• Perform other duties as assigned.

BASIC REQUIREMENTS:
• Bachelor's degree in Security Management, Criminal Justice, Homeland Security, Business Administration, Intelligence Studies, or a related field; or an equivalent combination of education, training, military service, and relevant experience.
• Minimum seven (7) years of progressively responsible experience administering industrial security programs within a defense, aerospace, intelligence, or government contracting environment.
• Demonstrated experience serving as a Facility Security Officer (FSO), Assistant Facility Security Officer (AFSO), Contractor Program Security Officer (CPSO), COMSEC Custodian, or in a comparable security leadership role with responsibility for NISP compliance.
• Thorough knowledge of the National Industrial Security Program Operating Manual (NISPOM), DCSA regulations, classified contract administration, and facility clearance requirements.
• Experience working directly with DCSA representatives, including Industrial Security Representatives (ISRs), during inspections, self-assessments, corrective actions, and ongoing compliance activities.
• Working knowledge of government security systems, including DISS, NISS, NBIS, and related personnel security and industrial security applications.
• Experience administering COMSEC accountability programs, including inventory management, safeguarding, destruction procedures, audits, and recordkeeping requirements.
• Experience developing, implementing, and maintaining Technology Control Plans (TCPs) and controlling access to sensitive, proprietary, or classified information and systems.
• Experience supporting the planning, construction, accreditation, or operation of secure facilities, including SCIFs, closed areas, and other classified workspaces.
• Knowledge of classified information handling requirements, document accountability, physical security controls, visitor control procedures, security incident reporting, and safeguarding requirements.
• Ability to interpret government regulations, contract security requirements, ICDs, and customer directives and translate them into practical business processes and security procedures.
• Strong organizational, analytical, and investigative skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining accurate and compliant security records.
• Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to brief executive leadership, employees, auditors, government officials, and customer representatives.
• Demonstrated ability to exercise sound judgment, discretion, and professionalism when handling classified, controlled, proprietary, and sensitive information.
• Must be a U.S. Citizen.
• Must possess and maintain an active Secret or Top Secret security clearance; Top Secret clearance with SCI eligibility is strongly preferred.
• Must be capable of obtaining and maintaining all required government accesses and customer-specific security authorizations.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:
• Active Top Secret clearance with SCI eligibility or current TS/SCI.
• Experience as the primary FSO for a cleared facility.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

Strategic Leadership and Compliance:

Develop and implement security strategies and initiatives that align with organisational goals and comply with UK Government Security requirements, including the HMG Security Policy Framework, ISO 17799 & 27001 Security Frameworks, Information Assurance Standards, HMG International Visits Control Office (IVCO) notifications, and Cabinet Office STAMP requirements.
Act as the Group Security Controller, ensuring compliance with all relevant regulations, including the management of Security Aspects Letters (SALs) and the flow-down of security requirements to third parties and subcontractors.

What You Bring

5+ years of program, production or operations management in games or another live-service product.

new_jobs.description:
Job Number: R0253565

Cyber Threat Intelligence Analyst, Senior

The Opportunity:

We are seeking an experienced Cyber Threat Intelligence Analyst to join our Security Operations Center (SOC) team. This role supports analysis and research on latest advanced cyber threats to provide actionable threat intelligence, including adversary indicators of compromise (IOCs), tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs), behaviors, and trends to help defend the client agency. The analyst will conduct analysis to profile threat actor TTPs used to infiltrate networks, systems, and assets to produce threat actor cards, profiles, or threat briefs. You’ll report on current and emerging threats that will exploit vulnerabilities and details of the vulnerabilities to stakeholders.

Cyber threats are evolving. Booz Allen is committed to creating an environment where you not only keep pace with the industry, but propel it forward. With access to academic programs, certifications, and opportunities to use expert tradecraft, we’ll continuously invest in you so you can create the career you want as you grow.

What You’ll Work On:

Collect, analyze, and correlate cyber threat intelligence from open-source, commercial, and government sources.
Monitor open-source intelligence, industry reports, and internal security logs to gather threat information, then synthesize and disseminate critical insights to relevant stakeholders.
Conduct tactical, operational, and strategic threat analysis in support of ongoing monitoring and investigations, identify patterns, and attribute attacks to specific actors.
Track threat actors, phishing campaigns, malware, and TTPs relevant to the agency’s mission and technology footprint.
Produce actionable reports, briefings, and IOCs for internal stakeholders.
Support the development of new detection rules and analytics based on evolving threats.

Join us. The world can’t wait.

You Have: 

10+ years of experience in cybersecurity threat intelligence, intelligence analysis, or threat analysis
Experience as a cyber threat analyst, collaborating with multiple internal and external stakeholders to gather data and intelligence, analyze, vet, and enrich the intelligence, create joint reports, and share with entities
Experience using intelligence platforms such as the MISP Threat Intelligence Platform
Experience with Confluence and Jira
Experience with ticketing systems such as ServiceNow
Experience with CNE and CNA tools and tradecraft along with signatures and TTPs associated with the preparation for, and execution or implementation of, such attacks
Knowledge of cyber threats, open-source research, nation state actors, and vulnerabilities and cyber attacks
Ability to prioritize and juggle multiple events or initiatives simultaneously
Top Secret clearance
Bachelor’s degree

Nice If You Have: 

Experience working in a SOC or cyber operations environment
Experience working with Splunk, including writing or comprehending queries and evaluating telemetry logs
Knowledge of current and emerging cyber adversaries and their TTPs
Knowledge of threat modeling and adversary tactics and techniques frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK matrices, Cyber Kill Chain, STRIDE, and PASTA
Ability to write or deliver succinct briefings, presentations, and reports to convey analysis, threat trends, threat actor profiles, indicator bulletins, vulnerability details, and defensive strategies to varied audiences
CISSP, GCTI, GCIA, GCIH, CEH, CTIA, or similar Certification

Clearance:

Applicants selected will be subject to a security investigation and may need to meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information; Top Secret clearance is required.

Position Summary

The Data & BI Analyst is responsible for keeping Cahill’s data accurate, organized, and usable, and for building the queries, reports, and Power BI dashboards that sit on top of it. This individual maintains the tables, pipelines, and integrations that feed our data warehouse, checks that the numbers match the systems they came from, and turns that data into reporting our project, preconstruction, and accounting teams can trust.

This is an early-career role with room to grow. It works alongside our Operations Team and uses AI tools every day to work faster and smarter. The ideal candidate is detail-oriented, curious about how our systems store information, and comfortable explaining technical work to non-technical teammates.

Responsibilities Include

Data Warehouse & Infrastructure

Maintain Cahill’s data warehouse utilizing the Kroo (or similar) connectors, ensuring data integrity, security, and accessibility.
Establish and enforce data governance standards, including naming conventions, documentation, and access controls.
Monitor data warehouse performance and optimize queries, storage, and infrastructure for reliability and speed.
Aggregate additional data sources into a data lake through Fabric (or similar).

Process Improvement & Innovation

Work cross-departmentally with Operations, Preconstruction, Field, Safety, Quality Control, and Accounting teams to identify process bottlenecks and opportunities where AI and automation could streamline workflows.
Document and share lessons learned, success stories, and measurable impact of implemented solutions.

Dashboards & Reporting

Design and build interactive dashboards using Power BI (or similar tools) to provide real-time insights into project performance, financial metrics, scheduling, safety, and other key business indicators.
Partner with stakeholders to define KPIs and reporting requirements that drive informed decision-making.
Maintain and enhance existing reports and dashboards as business needs evolve.

AI Agents & Automation

Design and deploy internal AI agents and automation tools to streamline repetitive tasks and improve operational efficiency across departments.
Develop custom AI solutions (e.g., document analysis, predictive analytics, natural language interfaces) tailored to Cahill’s construction workflows.
Integrate AI tools with existing platforms such as project management software, scheduling tools, and communication systems.
Continuously iterate on deployed solutions based on user feedback and evolving business needs.

AI Software Evaluation & Strategy

Research, evaluate, and recommend third-party AI software and platforms for potential adoption across the organization.
Stay current with emerging AI technologies, industry trends, and best practices relevant to the construction sector.
Assist with the development and maintenance of an AI roadmap aligned with Cahill’s strategic goals and Continuous Improvement initiatives.

Training & Support

Provide hands-on training and ongoing support to all departments and employees on the effective use of AI tools and data resources.
Develop training materials, guides, and best-practice documentation tailored to varying levels of technical proficiency.
Serve as one of the go-to resource for AI-related questions, troubleshooting, and adoption support across the company.
Champion a data-literate culture by promoting awareness of how data and AI can enhance day-to-day work.

Desired Skills And Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Data Analytics, Information Systems, Computer Science, Business, Mathematics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
1–3 years of relevant experience, including internships, coursework, or comparable hands-on work.
Working knowledge of SQL and relational databases (joins, filtering, aggregation, basic data validation).
Experience building reports or dashboards in Power BI, Tableau, or a comparable tool, including data modeling, DAX, publishing, and refresh management. Crystal Reports a plus.
Familiarity with Microsoft data tools (Fabric, Azure) preferred.
Experience with construction, accounting, ERP, scheduling, or field operations data (e.g., Viewpoint Vista, Procore, Primavera) helpful.
Quick learner and adaptable problem-solver with strong interpersonal skills, able to work cross-functionally, juggle multiple priorities, and handle confidential information with discretion.

Physical Requirements

The physical requirements described herein are representative of those that must be met by the employee, with or without reasonable accommodation, to perform the essential functions of this job successfully. While performing the duties of this job, the employee occasionally works in an office or hybrid setting. The employee is required to work in compliance with company safety policies, procedures, and applicable laws. This position will be regularly required to:

Repetitively use hand motions for keyboard use and physical use of vision to read computer monitors and paper documents.
Regularly use hands to operate standard office equipment (personal computer, phone, printer, etc.)
See with close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and have the ability to adjust focus.
Sit at a desk for prolonged periods of time working on a computer.
Talk and hear at normal levels. The noise level in the office work environment is usually low to moderate.
Must be able to lift up to 15 pounds at times, and up to 30 pounds occasionally.

What Can Cahill Offer You?

Employment - This is a full-time position located in downtown San Francisco. This role is hybrid, with a minimum of 3 days in the office. In addition to a competitive salary, we offer an annual discretionary performance-based bonus.
Healthcare Benefits - We provide coverage options with a PPO plan, an HMO plan, including Kaiser. Cahill covers 100% of monthly premiums for employee medical/dental/vision coverage for HMO and PPO plans. Multiple options are available for spouse/partner and family coverage. Additionally, we offer a Medical FSA option.
Retirement - Our 401(k) plan includes significant employer matching and an annual discretionary contribution. We also offer financial advisors to help you plan for your future.
Time Off - We understand the importance of balancing work and personal life. Our flexible PTO package allows you to recharge and take care of life's demands. The position starts with 5 days of PTO already earned and will accrue 3 additional weeks of PTO in the first year.
Volunteer Time Off - We provide paid time-off for volunteering, so our team members can make a meaningful impact to the communities we serve.
Wellness Program Cahill's Wellness Program supports physical, mental, financial, and community well-being with an annual wellness stipend, plus free resources and training.

The base annual salary for this exempt role is targeted between $100,000 - $120,000.

Please view our Privacy Notice (https://cahill-sf.com/privacy-statement/).

Cahill is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

Job Description

About Aberdeen

Aberdeen Group plc is one of Europe’s largest investment companies, and we are built on a long-standing culture of caring about the future and making a positive impact. Together we invest for a better future. We do it to make a difference to the lives of our clients and customers, our employees, society, and our shareholders. Our business is structured around three distinct areas focused on our clients' changing needs: Aberdeen Investments, Aberdeen Adviser, and interactive investor.

As a Data Analyst within Aberdeen Adviser, you will help turn data into meaningful insight and support our ambition to invest in our clients’ futures while investing in your tomorrow.

About The Department

The Data & Analytics team supports Aberdeen Adviser by delivering insight that improves decision-making, operational performance and customer outcomes. Working closely with business stakeholders, the team combines data, analytics, reporting and emerging technologies to help colleagues make informed decisions and enable our clients to be better investors. The culture is collaborative, curious and focused on continuous improvement.

About The Role

As a Data Analyst reporting to the Lead Analyst, you will support the delivery of analytics, reporting and data models that inform strategic and operational decisions. You will work across analytical projects, develop actionable insight and build trusted relationships with stakeholders across the organisation. This is an excellent opportunity to grow your technical capability in Power BI, SQL, Python, Microsoft Fabric and AI-enabled analytics while contributing to a data-driven culture. Based in Edinburgh on a permanent basis, the role offers the chance to make a visible impact while investing in your tomorrow.

Key Responsibilities

Support the design and delivery of analytical projects, ensuring outputs are robust, scalable and aligned to business priorities.
Develop and maintain Power BI reporting, data models and insight solutions that drive business action.
Use DAX, SQL, Python and AI-enabled approaches to analyse data and generate meaningful insight.
Translate analytical findings into clear narratives and visualisations for technical and non-technical audiences.
Contribute to data governance, documentation, reusable data assets and CI/CD ways of working.
Build strong stakeholder relationships and collaborate across the team to share knowledge and best practice.

About The Candidate - Essential Skills

Experience developing reports and data models using Power BI.
Proficiency in at least one of DAX, M Code, SQL or Python to solve business problems.
Familiarity with Microsoft Fabric, cloud-based data platforms and source control concepts.
Experience using AI to support analytics or technology deliverables.
Understanding of data architecture, data modelling and governance principles.

Desirable skills

Strong communication skills, stakeholder engagement capability and a desire to learn and improve continuously.
Previous experience with user experience/user journey design
Exposure to CI/CD - Redeployment pipelines

We are proud to be a Disability Confident Committed employer. If you have a disability and would like to apply to one of our UK roles under the Disability Confident Scheme, please notify us by completing the relevant section in our candidate questionnaire. We want you to be the real you throughout our recruitment process. Sharing your diversity information helps us understand the reach and impact of our hiring practices, and build a workplace where all people can thrive and belong.

This information is kept separate from your application and is not visible to recruiters, hiring managers, or assessors at any stage.

Our Benefits

There's more to working life than coming home with a good salary. We have an environment where you can learn, get involved and be supported.

When you join us, your reward will be one of the best around. This includes 40 days’ annual leave, a 16% employer pension contribution, a discretionary performance-based bonus (where applicable), private healthcare and a range of flexible benefits – including gym discounts, season ticket loans and access to an employee discount portal. You can read more about our benefits here.

Our business

Enabling our clients to be better investors drives everything we do. Our business is structured around three distinct areas – our vectors of growth – focused on our clients’ changing needs. You can find out more about what we do here.

An inclusive way of working

Whatever way you like to work, if you have the talent and commitment to join our team, we’d like to hear from you.

At Aberdeen we’ve adopted a ‘blended working’ approach. This approach combines the benefits of face-to-face collaboration, coaching and connecting in our offices with the flexibility of working from home. It enables colleagues to find a balance that works for their roles, their teams, our clients and our business.

An inclusive culture, where diverse perspectives drive our actions, is at the core of who we are and what we do. new_jobs.description:
Position Summary Description

The Principal Cyber Analyst will be a key leader in our cybersecurity team, responsible for enhancing the organization’s security posture and providing expert guidance on complex cyber threats and vulnerabilities. This role requires a deep understanding of cybersecurity principles, advanced analytics, and incident response methodologies. The Principal Cyber Analyst will spearhead initiatives to proactively identify risks, develop mitigation strategies, and ensuring compliance with North American Electric Reliability Corporation Critical Infrastructure Protection (NERC CIP) standards as well as adherence to National Institute of Standards and Technology Cybersecurity Framework (NIST CSF).

Qualifications and Education Requirements

Bachelor of Science degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Cybersecurity, or a related field is required, with a master's degree preferred. Candidate must have a minimum of fifteen (15) years of experience in cybersecurity, focusing on threat analysis and incident response. Relevant cybersecurity certifications (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CEH, GCIH) are highly desirable. Extensive knowledge of cybersecurity frameworks, best practices, and regulatory requirements is essential. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills are necessary, along with the ability to work under pressure and manage multiple priorities. Excellent communication and presentation skills are required, with the capability to conveying technical information to non-technical stakeholders. Experience with security tools and technologies, such as SIEM, IDS/IPS, firewalls, endpoint protection, and vulnerability management, is also required.

Core Competencies:  
Adaptable, Collaborative, Communicator, Critical-Thinking, Detail-Oriented, and Outcome-Driven

Technical Competencies/Skills:

Cybersecurity Frameworks (NIST CSF, ISO 27001, and NERC CIP)

Threat Intelligence and Analysis

Intrusion Detection

Incident Response Methodologies

Security Information and Event Management (SIEM)

Security Technologies

Ethical Hacking

Vulnerability Management

Network Security

Cloud Security

Regulatory Compliance

Risk Management

Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications

Soft Competencies/Skills:

Effective verbal/nonverbal, listening and written communications

Collaboration

Critical Thinking

Customer Service Oriented

Leadership and Mentorship

Managing Change

Essential Functions

Develop and implement comprehensive cybersecurity strategies and policies to protect organizational assets.

Assess and enhance the organization's security posture against emerging threats and vulnerabilities.

Conduct in-depth analysis of cyber threats, vulnerabilities, and exploits relevant to the organization.

Monitor and evaluate industry trends, attack vectors, and the tactics of cyber adversaries.

Lead incident response efforts, including the identification, containment, eradication, and recovery from cybersecurity incidents.

Conduct forensic analysis on compromised systems and provide actionable recommendations for remediation.

Perform risk assessments and security audits to identify gaps in security practices.

Work with business units to prioritize risks and develop mitigation strategies.

Collaborate with IT, compliance, and business units to ensure alignment of security programs with business objectives.

Train and mentor junior analysts and staff on cybersecurity best practices and tools.

Ensure compliance with relevant laws, regulations, and industry standards (e.g., NIST, ISO 27001, GDPR, NERC CIP).

Prepare and present reports to senior management and stakeholders on the effectiveness of security measures and risk levels.

Stay current on the latest cybersecurity technologies, trends, and methodologies to continuously improve the organization's security capabilities.

Participate in the development of security products and solutions to enhance security monitoring and detection capabilities.

Perform other duties as applicable to the position or as assigned.

NERC Compliance: 
Performs NERC Compliance Program roles if/as designated in Seminole's Standard Ownership Matrix (SOM) including ongoing evidence retention in "audit-ready" form. You should also be familiar with Seminole's Enterprise Internal Compliance Program (ENT-GCD-RGC-EP-054) to further your understanding of Seminole's compliance program and your duties and responsibilities in the SOM. 

Physical Requirements

Must be able to follow established protective measures including wearing required personal protective equipment (PPE). Must possess a valid driver’s license and acceptable Motor Vehicle Report.  

Working Conditions

Some travel and work outside of normal business hours. While working in certain areas of the plant there is the potential for exposure to hazards typical of an industrial working environment. Must be capable of working extra hours and/or weekends when necessary to complete a project on time. Must be available on a 24-hour basis in the event of a system malfunction that requires assistance.
